subtitle.en: Designing, building and running backend systems
subtitle.zh: 设计、构建与运行后端系统

description.en: One long street that follows the life of a backend system: requirements and design, code and collaboration, data, service architecture, testing, security, and finally delivery and operations.
description.zh: 一条沿后端系统生命周期展开的长街：需求与设计、代码与协作、数据、服务架构、测试、安全，最后是交付与运维。

metaphor.en: One long street that follows a system from its first requirement to its thousandth deploy.
metaphor.zh: 一条长街，跟着一个系统从第一条需求走到第一千次部署。

summary.en: Deciding what to build, stating it so it can be tested, and shaping interfaces and modules so the system stays easy to change.
summary.zh: 决定做什么、把需求写成可验证的形式，并设计好接口和模块，让系统易于修改。

summary.en: Turning vague wishes into small, testable stories, measurable quality targets and a shared model of the domain.
summary.zh: 把模糊的愿望变成小而可测的故事、可度量的质量目标和共享的领域模型。

summary.en: A user story says who wants what and why; acceptance criteria turn it into something you can test.
summary.zh: 用户故事说明谁想要什么、为什么；验收标准让它变得可以测试。

explain.en: A user story is a short requirement told from the user's side: 'As a <role>, I want <capability>, so that <benefit>.' It is a placeholder for a conversation, not a full specification. Acceptance criteria state when the story is done, often as Given/When/Then scenarios, so developers, testers and the product owner agree on 'done' and can automate the checks. Good stories are small and sliced vertically: each one cuts through UI, API and database to deliver a thin piece of working value, rather than a horizontal layer such as 'build all the tables first'. INVEST (independent, negotiable, valuable, estimable, small, testable) is a common checklist.
explain.zh: 用户故事从用户的角度描述需求：“作为<角色>，我想要<功能>，以便<收益>”。它是一次对话的占位符，而不是完整的规格说明。验收标准（acceptance criteria）写明故事何时算完成，常用 Given/When/Then 场景表达，让开发、测试和产品对“完成”达成一致，并能写成自动化检查。好的故事要小，并且纵向切分：每个故事贯穿界面、API 和数据库，交付一小块能用的价值，而不是“先把所有表建好”这样的横向分层。INVEST（独立、可协商、有价值、可估算、小、可测试）是常用的检查清单。

example.en: Story: As a shopper, I want my cart saved, so that I can finish buying on another device. Criteria: Given a signed-in shopper with 3 items in the cart, when she signs in on her phone, then the same 3 items appear. Given a guest, when the browser closes, then the cart is kept for 7 days. First vertical slice: save and restore the cart for signed-in shoppers only.
example.zh: 故事：作为购物者，我想保存购物车，以便在另一台设备上继续购买。验收标准：假设已登录用户的购物车里有 3 件商品，当她在手机上登录时，那么看到同样的 3 件商品；假设是游客，当浏览器关闭时，那么购物车保留 7 天。第一个纵向切片：只为已登录用户保存并恢复购物车。

image.en: A giant pink cake fills the classroom, already cut into wedges that each run from the icing down to the base. A child holds up a scroll with her wish. The teacher, in a chef's hat, points at the blackboard, where Given, When and Then are chalked one under another, and a big green stamp waits beside the cake to mark a slice as done.
image.zh: 一个巨大的粉色蛋糕占满了教室，已经切成一块块从奶油顶一直切到底的楔形。一个孩子举着写有心愿的卷轴。戴厨师帽的老师指着黑板，上面一行行写着 Given、When、Then；蛋糕旁一枚绿色大印章，等着给做好的那块盖“完成”。

means.en: As a … I want … so that …: the story
means.zh: “作为…我想要…以便…”：故事本身

thing.en: Given / When / Then on the board

means.en: acceptance criteria that make the story testable
means.zh: 让故事可测试的验收标准

means.en: vertical slices: each one goes through UI, API and data
means.zh: 纵向切片：每块都贯穿界面、API 和数据

means.en: done only when every criterion passes
means.zh: 所有标准都通过才算完成

summary.en: Quality targets such as latency, availability, scalability, security and cost, stated as numbers you can measure.
summary.zh: 延迟、可用性、可扩展性、安全和成本等质量目标，要写成可度量的数字。

explain.en: Functional requirements say what the system does; non-functional requirements (quality attributes) say how well it must do it: latency, throughput, availability, scalability, durability, security, cost and maintainability. They shape the architecture more than most features do, and they are useless when vague. 'Fast' and 'highly available' cannot be tested; 'p99 latency under 200 ms at 1,000 requests per second' and '99.9% monthly availability' can. Use percentiles rather than averages, because a few slow requests hide inside a mean. Quality attributes pull against each other (stronger consistency or encryption can cost latency and money), so rank them with the stakeholders.
explain.zh: 功能需求说明系统做什么；非功能需求（质量属性）说明要做到多好：延迟、吞吐量、可用性、可扩展性、持久性、安全、成本和可维护性。它们对架构的影响往往大于具体功能，而且一旦含糊就毫无用处。“要快”“高可用”无法测试；“每秒 1000 个请求时 p99 延迟低于 200 毫秒”“月可用性 99.9%”才能测试。要用百分位数而不是平均值，因为少数慢请求会被均值掩盖。各项质量属性相互牵制（更强的一致性或加密可能增加延迟和成本），需要与干系人一起排出优先级。

example.en: 99.9% availability allows 0.001 × 30 days × 24 h × 60 min ≈ 43 minutes of downtime a month; 99.99% allows about 4.3 minutes. If 98 of 100 requests take 50 ms and 2 take 2 s, the mean is 89 ms and looks fine, but the p99 is 2 s.
example.zh: 99.9% 可用性允许每月停机 0.001 × 30 天 × 24 小时 × 60 分钟 ≈ 43 分钟；99.99% 只允许约 4.3 分钟。100 个请求中 98 个各耗时 50 毫秒、2 个耗时 2 秒，平均值是 89 毫秒，看起来不错，但 p99 是 2 秒。

image.en: A giant ruler on a stand runs from 0 to 300 ms across the classroom. Four white rabbits sit near its start, but one huge turtle plods along far past the 200 mark. The teacher clicks her stopwatch and points at the turtle, while a small sign beside the rabbits demands 99.9%.
image.zh: 一把立着的巨大标尺横跨教室，从 0 标到 300 毫秒。四只白兔蹲在起点附近，一只巨龟却慢吞吞地爬过了 200 的刻度。老师按下秒表，指着那只乌龟；兔子旁边的小牌子写着 99.9%。

means.en: most requests are fast, so the mean looks fine
means.zh: 大多数请求很快，均值看着不错

means.en: the slow tail that p99 exposes and a mean hides
means.zh: p99 暴露、均值掩盖的慢尾

means.en: measure: a requirement must be a testable number
means.zh: 去测量：需求必须是可测的数字

means.en: an availability target: about 43 minutes down a month
means.zh: 可用性目标：每月约 43 分钟停机

summary.en: Model the business in its own words: entities, value objects and aggregates inside bounded contexts that share one ubiquitous language.
summary.zh: 用业务自己的语言建模：在限界上下文中划分实体、值对象和聚合，并使用统一语言。

explain.en: Domain-driven design (DDD) shapes code around the business domain. An entity has an identity that lasts while its attributes change (customer 42). A value object is defined only by its values and is usually immutable (Money(10, 'EUR'), an address). An aggregate is a cluster of objects changed together through one root that enforces their invariants; outside code holds references only to the root, and one transaction usually changes one aggregate. A bounded context is the boundary inside which a model and its words have a single meaning: 'account' in billing need not match 'account' in login. Within it, developers and domain experts share a ubiquitous language, used both in conversation and in code.
explain.zh: 领域驱动设计（DDD）让代码围绕业务领域来组织。实体（entity）有贯穿始终的身份，属性可以变化（42 号客户）。值对象（value object）只由取值决定，通常不可变（Money(10, 'EUR')、地址）。聚合（aggregate）是一组必须一起修改的对象，由聚合根统一维护不变量；外部只引用聚合根，一个事务通常只改一个聚合。限界上下文（bounded context）是模型及其术语保持单一含义的边界：计费里的“账户”不必等同于登录里的“账户”。在边界内，开发者和领域专家使用同一套统一语言（ubiquitous language），对话和代码都用它。

example.en: An Order aggregate has the root Order (an entity, id 1001) and its OrderLines. Rule: the total may not exceed the customer's credit limit, so lines are added only through order.add_line(sku, qty), never by editing a line directly. Price is a value object: two Money(9.99, 'USD') values are interchangeable. In the Shipping context the same order is just a Parcel with a weight and an address.
example.zh: 订单聚合以 Order（实体，id 1001）为根，内含若干 OrderLine。规则：总额不得超过客户的信用额度，因此只能通过 order.add_line(sku, qty) 添加明细，不能直接改某一行。价格是值对象：两个 Money(9.99, 'USD') 可以互换。在物流上下文里，同一个订单只是一个带重量和地址的包裹（Parcel）。

image.en: Inside a curved wooden fence, a stern owl broods on a big nest, with three eggs peeking out in front of it: anyone who wants an egg has to deal with the owl. A green parrot perched on the fence squawks 'Order!', and the farmer and the programmer standing in front both point at it and repeat the very same word.
image.zh: 一圈弧形木栅栏里，一只神情严肃的猫头鹰趴在大鸟巢上，三枚蛋从它身前露出来：谁想拿蛋，都得先过猫头鹰这一关。栅栏上的绿鹦鹉大叫“订单！”，站在前面的农夫和程序员都指着它，重复着同一个词。

means.en: a bounded context: one model, one meaning per word
means.zh: 限界上下文：一个模型，词义唯一

means.en: the aggregate root: every change goes through it and it guards the rules
means.zh: 聚合根：一切修改都经过它，由它守护规则

means.en: objects inside the aggregate, changed together in one transaction
means.zh: 聚合内的对象，在一个事务里一起修改

means.en: the ubiquitous language shared by experts and code
means.zh: 专家和代码共用的统一语言

summary.en: Designing HTTP APIs other teams can rely on: clear resources, honest status codes, safe paging and careful evolution.
summary.zh: 设计别的团队能放心依赖的 HTTP API：清晰的资源、准确的状态码、稳妥的分页和谨慎的演进。

summary.en: Name things with noun URLs, act on them with HTTP methods, exchange representations, and keep every request self-contained.
summary.zh: 用名词 URL 命名资源，用 HTTP 方法操作，交换资源的表述，并让每个请求自带全部信息。

explain.en: REST (Representational State Transfer, Roy Fielding, 2000) is an architectural style. In everyday HTTP APIs it means: each thing of interest is a resource named by a URL built from nouns (/orders/42/items), and the standard methods act on it: GET reads, POST creates or triggers processing, PUT replaces, PATCH partly updates, DELETE removes. Clients exchange representations of a resource (usually JSON), not the resource itself. Requests are stateless: each carries everything the server needs, such as an auth token, so any instance can serve it and the service scales out. GET, PUT and DELETE are idempotent; POST in general is not. Many 'REST' APIs omit the hypermedia links Fielding's definition requires.
explain.zh: REST（表述性状态转移，Roy Fielding 于 2000 年提出）是一种架构风格。在日常的 HTTP API 里，它的意思是：每个被关注的对象都是资源，用名词构成的 URL 命名（/orders/42/items），再用标准方法操作：GET 读取，POST 创建或触发处理，PUT 整体替换，PATCH 部分更新，DELETE 删除。客户端交换的是资源的表述（通常是 JSON），而不是资源本身。请求无状态：每个请求自带服务器所需的一切（例如认证令牌），任何实例都能处理，服务便于水平扩展。GET、PUT、DELETE 是幂等的，POST 一般不是。很多所谓的 REST API 省略了 Fielding 定义中必需的超媒体链接。

example.en: GET /orders/42 returns {"id": 42, "status": "paid"}. PATCH /orders/42 with {"status": "cancelled"} changes one field. POST /orders/42/refunds creates a refund and returns 201 with Location: /orders/42/refunds/7. Avoid verbs in paths, such as POST /cancelOrder?id=42.
example.zh: GET /orders/42 返回 {"id": 42, "status": "paid"}。PATCH /orders/42 携带 {"status": "cancelled"}，只改一个字段。POST /orders/42/refunds 创建一笔退款，返回 201 和 Location: /orders/42/refunds/7。避免把动词写进路径，比如 POST /cancelOrder?id=42。

image.en: A giant envelope addressed '/orders/42' stands at the post-office counter, and a big rubber stamp beside it decides what will happen to it: read, replace or delete. Above the counter floats a goldfish clerk who forgets every customer the moment they turn away, so the next customer arrives holding an envelope that carries everything needed, token included.
image.zh: 邮局柜台前立着一个巨大的信封，地址写着“/orders/42”，旁边一枚大橡皮图章决定怎么处理它：读取、替换还是删除。柜台上方漂着一条金鱼职员，客人一转身它就忘得一干二净，所以下一位客人递来的信封里自带一切所需，连令牌也在里面。

means.en: a resource named by a noun URL
means.zh: 用名词 URL 命名的资源

means.en: the HTTP method says the action: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE
means.zh: HTTP 方法表示动作：GET、POST、PUT、PATCH、DELETE

means.en: a stateless server keeps no session between requests
means.zh: 无状态服务器不在请求之间保存会话

means.en: each request carries its own token and context
means.zh: 每个请求自带令牌和上下文

summary.en: The status code tells the client what happened and whether retrying can help; a consistent error body says why.
summary.zh: 状态码告诉客户端发生了什么、重试是否有用；统一的错误体说明原因。

explain.en: 2xx means success (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content). 4xx means the client must change something: 400 malformed, 401 not authenticated, 403 authenticated but not allowed, 404 not found, 409 conflicts with the current state (a duplicate, a stale version), 422 well-formed but invalid (many APIs use 400 for both), 429 too many requests. 5xx means the server failed: 500 a bug, 502 or 504 a failing or slow upstream, 503 temporarily unavailable. Resending an unchanged 4xx request usually fails again; 429 is retried after waiting. 5xx errors and timeouts may be retried with backoff, but only for idempotent operations. Return one error shape everywhere, such as {code, message, details}.
explain.zh: 2xx 表示成功（200 OK、201 Created、204 No Content）。4xx 表示客户端得改点什么：400 格式错误，401 未认证，403 已认证但无权限，404 不存在，409 与当前状态冲突（重复创建、版本过期），422 格式正确但校验失败（不少 API 都用 400），429 请求过多。5xx 表示服务器出错：500 程序缺陷，502/504 上游故障或超时，503 暂时不可用。原样重发 4xx 请求通常还会失败，429 等一等再试除外；5xx 和超时可以带退避重试，但仅限幂等操作。所有接口返回同一种错误结构，例如 {code, message, details}。

example.en: POST /users with broken JSON: 400. Valid JSON but a bad email: 422 {"code": "invalid_email", "message": "email must contain @"}. Email already registered: 409. User database down: 503 with Retry-After: 30. The client may retry that 503 safely only if the POST carries an idempotency key; retrying the 422 unchanged is pointless.
example.zh: POST /users 的 JSON 写坏了：400。JSON 合法但邮箱非法：422 {"code": "invalid_email", "message": "email must contain @"}。邮箱已注册：409。用户数据库宕机：503，并带 Retry-After: 30。只有 POST 带了幂等键，客户端才能放心重试这个 503；原样重试 422 毫无意义。

image.en: In the sorting room a robot arm drops every reply into one of three baskets: green for delivered, orange for 'return to sender', red for 'our fault'. The red basket is on fire. A customer shrugs at the orange letter handed back to her, while a clerk holding a stopwatch tells the next one to wait a while before trying again.
image.zh: 分拣室里，机械臂把每封回信丢进三个篮子之一：绿色是“已送达”，橙色是“退回寄件人”，红色是“我们的错”。红篮子正在着火。一位顾客拿着被退回的橙色信件耸耸肩；拿秒表的职员则让下一位先等一会儿再来。

means.en: 2xx: success
means.zh: 2xx：成功

means.en: 4xx: the client must change the request; resending fails again
means.zh: 4xx：客户端得改请求，原样重发还会失败

means.en: 5xx: the server failed
means.zh: 5xx：服务器出错

means.en: retry 5xx or 429 later, with backoff, only if idempotent
means.zh: 5xx 或 429 稍后带退避重试，前提是幂等

summary.en: Return long lists in pages; cursor pagination over a stable, unique order with an opaque token stays correct and fast while data changes.
summary.zh: 长列表要分页返回；按稳定唯一的顺序、用不透明令牌做游标分页，数据变化时仍然正确又快。

explain.en: Offset pagination (LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40) is simple and can jump to page 3, but the database still walks past every skipped row, so deep pages get slow, and rows inserted or deleted between requests shift the window, causing repeats or gaps. Cursor (keyset) pagination remembers where the last page ended and asks for rows after it: WHERE (created_at, id) < (:t, :id) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 20. With an index on the sort key each page costs about the same, and new rows do not shift it. The order must be stable and unique, so add a tie-breaker such as the id. Return the cursor as an opaque token (for example base64) so clients cannot depend on its format.
explain.zh: 偏移分页（LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40）简单，还能直接跳到第 3 页，但数据库仍要逐行走过被跳过的记录，页越深越慢；两次请求之间有插入或删除时，窗口会错位，造成重复或遗漏。游标分页（keyset）记住上一页结束的位置，只取它之后的行：WHERE (created_at, id) < (:t, :id) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 20。排序键有索引时每页代价基本相同，新插入的行也不会让结果错位。顺序必须稳定且唯一，所以要加 id 这类决胜键。游标以不透明令牌（例如 base64）返回，客户端就无法依赖它的内部格式。

example.en: A feed shows 20 posts per page, newest first. A user reads page 1 (posts 100 to 81); meanwhile 5 new posts arrive. With OFFSET 20, page 2 now returns posts 85 to 66, repeating 85 to 81. With a cursor, page 2 asks for posts older than 81 and gets 80 to 61, no repeats. The response looks like {"items": [...], "next": "eyJpZCI6ODF9"}.
example.zh: 信息流每页 20 条，最新在前。用户看完第 1 页（第 100 到 81 条），这时来了 5 条新帖。用 OFFSET 20，第 2 页返回第 85 到 66 条，85 到 81 重复出现。用游标，第 2 页请求“比 81 更早”的帖子，得到第 80 到 61 条，没有重复。响应形如 {"items": [...], "next": "eyJpZCI6ODF9"}。

image.en: A conveyor belt carries parcels from left to right while a robot keeps shoving new ones on at the start. On the left, a clerk with a magnifying glass counts parcels from the beginning to find 'number 21' and keeps getting it wrong. On the right, a second clerk left a red flag where she stopped last time; now she simply takes the parcels after the flag.
image.zh: 传送带载着包裹从左往右走，一个机器人不停地往起点塞新包裹。左边的职员拿着放大镜从头数，想找到“第 21 个”，却总数错。右边的第二位职员上次在停下的地方插了一面红旗，现在只管拿红旗后面的包裹。

means.en: OFFSET: walks past skipped rows; inserts shift the window
means.zh: OFFSET：逐行跳过；插入会让窗口错位

thing.zh: 往起点塞包裹的机器人

means.en: concurrent inserts that cause repeats or gaps
means.zh: 并发插入造成重复或遗漏

means.en: the cursor: continue after the last key seen
means.zh: 游标：从见到的最后一个键之后继续

thing.en: a plain flag with no writing

means.en: an opaque token clients hand back unread
means.zh: 客户端原样交回的不透明令牌

summary.en: Evolve an API with additive, backward-compatible changes; keep new versions for breaking ones and give clients time to move.
summary.zh: 用增量、向后兼容的改动演进 API；只有破坏性改动才开新版本，并给客户端留出迁移时间。

explain.en: Once other teams depend on an API, its contract can only grow. Backward-compatible changes are additive: a new optional field, endpoint or parameter. Breaking changes remove or rename a field, change a type or meaning, make an optional input required, or tighten validation. Clients should ignore unknown fields (the tolerant reader) and servers should keep accepting old requests. When a break is unavoidable, publish a new version, run both side by side, announce a deprecation period (for example with Deprecation and Sunset headers) and watch traffic until the old version is idle. The version can live in the path (/v2/orders), a header or a media type: the path is most visible, a header keeps URLs stable.
explain.zh: 一旦别的团队依赖了某个 API，它的契约就只能扩展。向后兼容的改动是增量式的：新增可选字段、接口或参数。破坏性改动包括删除或重命名字段、改变类型或含义、把可选输入改为必填、收紧校验。客户端应忽略不认识的字段（容错读者），服务器应继续接受旧请求。实在要破坏兼容时，发布新版本并与旧版并行运行，公布弃用期（例如用 Deprecation 和 Sunset 响应头），持续观察流量直到旧版无人调用。版本号可以放在路径（/v2/orders）、请求头或媒体类型里：路径最直观，请求头让 URL 保持不变。

example.en: v1 returns {"name": "Ada Lovelace"}. Adding "email" next to it is safe. Splitting name into first_name and last_name breaks every client that reads name, so ship it as /v2/users, keep v1 running with a Sunset date six months out, and email the teams whose traffic still reaches v1.
example.zh: v1 返回 {"name": "Ada Lovelace"}。在旁边加一个 "email" 字段是安全的。把 name 拆成 first_name 和 last_name 会让所有读取 name 的客户端出错，所以应作为 /v2/users 发布，v1 继续运行并定下六个月后的 Sunset 日期，再给仍在调用 v1 的团队发邮件。

image.en: Two post boxes stand side by side: a faded blue one with an hourglass running out on its roof, and a shiny red new one. A signpost between them points to v1 and v2. An elderly customer still posts his letters into the old box, a newcomer uses the new one, and a clerk with a megaphone announces the day the old box will close.
image.zh: 两个邮筒并排而立：一个是褪色的蓝邮筒，顶上的沙漏快漏完了；另一个是崭新的红邮筒。两者之间的路牌分别指向 v1 和 v2。一位老顾客仍把信投进旧邮筒，新来的顾客用新邮筒，拿扩音器的职员正在宣布旧邮筒关闭的日子。

means.zh: 新旧版本并行运行

means.en: a deprecation period with a sunset date
means.zh: 带停用日期的弃用期

thing.zh: 仍用 v1 的老顾客

means.en: existing clients keep working; nothing breaks overnight
means.zh: 现有客户端照常工作，不会一夜崩溃

means.en: announce deprecation and contact the remaining callers
means.zh: 公告弃用，联系剩下的调用方

means.en: the version lives in the path, header or media type
means.zh: 版本放在路径、请求头或媒体类型里

summary.en: Keeping code easy to change: cohesive modules, loose coupling, SOLID, injected dependencies and a few classic patterns.
summary.zh: 让代码易于修改：高内聚、低耦合、SOLID、依赖注入和几个经典模式。

summary.en: Aim for high cohesion inside each module and low coupling between modules, which meet only through small, clear interfaces.
summary.zh: 模块内部高内聚，模块之间低耦合，彼此只通过小而清晰的接口连接。

explain.en: Cohesion measures how closely the parts of one module belong together; coupling measures how much modules depend on each other. High cohesion means a module does one job and the code for that job lives in one place. Low coupling means a change inside one module rarely forces changes in others. The tool is information hiding (Parnas, 1972): put each design decision that is likely to change behind a narrow interface, and let other modules use only that interface, never the internals or shared mutable data. Coupling cannot be zero, since modules must cooperate, but depending on a stable interface is far cheaper than depending on details. SOLID, layering and service boundaries all build on these two ideas.
explain.zh: 内聚衡量一个模块内部各部分关联得有多紧密；耦合衡量模块之间相互依赖的程度。高内聚指一个模块只做一件事，相关代码集中在一处；低耦合指改动一个模块的内部，很少迫使其他模块跟着改。手段是信息隐藏（Parnas，1972）：把每个可能变化的设计决策藏在窄接口后面，其他模块只使用接口，不碰内部实现或共享的可变数据。耦合不可能为零，模块总要协作，但依赖稳定的接口比依赖细节便宜得多。SOLID、分层和服务边界都建立在这两条原则之上。

example.en: A checkout module that reads the payments table directly is tightly coupled: renaming a column breaks checkout. If checkout calls payments.charge(order_id, amount) instead, the payments team can change tables, providers or retries without touching checkout. A utils.py that parses dates, sends email and renders PDFs has low cohesion; split it by job.
example.zh: 结账模块直接读支付表就是紧耦合：支付表改个列名，结账就坏了。改为调用 payments.charge(order_id, amount)，支付团队就能随意更换表结构、支付渠道或重试策略，而不必动结账代码。一个同时负责解析日期、发邮件和生成 PDF 的 utils.py 内聚很低，应按职责拆开。

image.en: On the left of the workshop a mechanic strains against a big gear train: turn one gear and the other two must turn with it. On the right stands a neat tower of blue, yellow and green toy bricks, each brick a single solid colour. A giant hand holds up a red brick beside the tower, ready to snap it on, because every brick has the same studs.
image.zh: 工坊左边，一位机械师使劲推着一组大齿轮：转动一个，另外两个也得跟着转。右边立着一座整齐的积木塔，蓝、黄、绿三块积木各是一种纯色。一只巨手在塔旁举起一块红积木，随时可以扣上去，因为每块积木的凸点都一模一样。

means.zh: 紧耦合：一处改动牵连邻居

means.en: a small, stable interface
means.zh: 小而稳定的接口

thing.en: the red brick ready to snap on

means.zh: 低耦合：换掉一个模块不碰其余部分

means.en: high cohesion: one module, one job
means.zh: 高内聚：一个模块只做一件事

summary.en: Five object-oriented design principles that keep classes focused, extensible, substitutable, lean and decoupled.
summary.zh: 五条面向对象设计原则，让类职责单一、易于扩展、可以替换、接口精简、依赖解耦。

explain.en: S, single responsibility: a class should have one reason to change, that is, serve one actor. O, open/closed: open for extension, closed for modification; add a new class instead of editing a growing switch. L, Liskov substitution: a subtype must work wherever its base type is expected, keeping its contract (no stronger preconditions, no weaker postconditions). I, interface segregation: several small, client-specific interfaces beat one fat one. D, dependency inversion: high-level policy and low-level details both depend on abstractions, so business logic owns the interface and the database adapter implements it. They are heuristics, not laws; applied blindly they add needless indirection.
explain.zh: S，单一职责：一个类只应有一个变化的理由，即只服务于一类使用者。O，开闭原则：对扩展开放、对修改关闭，用新增类代替不断膨胀的 switch。L，里氏替换：凡是需要基类的地方都能换成子类，且不破坏契约（前置条件不能更强，后置条件不能更弱）。I，接口隔离：多个面向具体调用方的小接口胜过一个臃肿的大接口。D，依赖倒置：高层策略和底层细节都依赖抽象，由业务逻辑定义接口，数据库适配器去实现。它们是经验法则而非定律，机械套用只会添加多余的间接层。

example.en: S: move email sending out of UserService into a Mailer. O: add PayPal as a new PaymentMethod subclass, not another elif. L: a Square whose set_width also changes its height breaks code written for Rectangle. I: a read-only caller depends on Reader, not on a 20-method Repo. D: OrderService takes a Gateway interface that StripeGateway implements.
example.zh: S：发邮件从 UserService 移到 Mailer。O：PayPal 写成新的 PaymentMethod 子类，不再加 elif。L：改宽也改高的 Square 会破坏针对 Rectangle 写的代码。I：只读调用方依赖 Reader，而非 20 个方法的 Repo。D：OrderService 接收 Gateway 接口，由 StripeGateway 实现。

image.en: A yellow robot arm with a small standard socket waits on the workshop floor. Beside it lies a row of single-purpose heads, a hammer, a wrench and a pair of scissors, and each snaps on without opening the arm. But a rubber duck that needs a battery has sneaked in among the tools: it looks as if it belongs, yet it cannot do a tool's job. An engineer in a hard hat shrugs at it.
image.zh: 工坊地上，一台带小型标准接口的黄色机械臂在等待。旁边一排单一用途的工具头：锤子、扳手、剪刀，每个都不用拆开机械臂就能扣上。可是一只要装电池的橡皮鸭混进了工具堆：看起来像是同类，却干不了工具的活。戴安全帽的工程师冲它耸耸肩。

means.en: S: a single reason to change
means.zh: S：只有一个变化的理由

thing.en: heads snap on without opening the arm

means.en: O: extend without modifying
means.zh: O：扩展而不修改

thing.en: the duck that needs a battery

means.en: L: a subtype that breaks the base type's contract
means.zh: L：破坏基类契约的子类

means.en: I: lean interfaces with nothing a client does not use
means.zh: I：精简接口，不含调用方用不到的东西

thing.en: the arm knows only the socket

means.en: D: depend on abstractions, not on concrete tools
means.zh: D：依赖抽象，而非具体工具

summary.en: Hand an object its collaborators from outside instead of letting it build them, so they can be swapped and faked in tests.
summary.zh: 由外部把协作对象交给一个对象，而不是让它自己创建，这样就能替换，测试时也能换成假对象。

explain.en: Without injection a class builds what it needs: self.db = PostgresDB("prod-url"). It is then welded to that database, its configuration and its side effects. With dependency injection the class declares what it needs, usually as constructor parameters typed by an interface, and the code that assembles the application (the composition root) passes in real implementations. Tests pass fakes or stubs instead, with no network and no database. Injection is the usual way to apply the dependency inversion principle. A DI container (Spring, Guice, the one built into .NET) automates the wiring of large object graphs; it is optional, and plain constructor arguments are often enough. Avoid the service locator, which hides dependencies inside the class.
explain.zh: 不用注入时，类自己创建依赖：self.db = PostgresDB("prod-url")，于是它和这个数据库、它的配置及副作用焊死在一起。依赖注入让类声明自己需要什么，通常是以接口为类型的构造函数参数，由组装应用的代码（组合根）传入真实实现；测试时改传假对象或桩，不需要网络和数据库。注入是落实依赖倒置原则的常用方式。DI 容器（Spring、Guice、.NET 自带的容器）可为大型对象图自动装配，但它是可选的，直接传构造参数往往就够了。要避免服务定位器，它把依赖藏进了类的内部。

example.en: class Checkout: def __init__(self, payments: PaymentGateway, clock: Clock). Production: Checkout(StripeGateway(key), SystemClock()). Test: Checkout(FakeGateway(declines=True), FixedClock("2026-01-01")) checks in milliseconds that a declined card creates no order, without calling Stripe.
example.zh: Checkout 的构造函数接收 payments: PaymentGateway 和 clock: Clock。生产：Checkout(StripeGateway(key), SystemClock())。测试：Checkout(FakeGateway(declines=True), FixedClock("2026-01-01"))，几毫秒就能验证拒卡时不生成订单，且不调用 Stripe。

image.en: A big robot stands in the workshop with an empty battery hatch, and it has no way to make its own power. A giant hand reaches in from outside and holds up a gold battery for the production shift. On the test bench beside it lies a painted wooden battery, and an inspector points at it: with that one, the robot can be tried out without any real power.
image.zh: 工坊里站着一个大机器人，电池仓空着，它自己没法产生电力。一只巨手从外面伸进来，为生产班次举起一块金色电池。旁边的测试台上放着一块涂了漆的木头电池，检查员指着它：装上这块，不用真电也能试一试机器人。

means.en: the class declares what it needs instead of building it
means.zh: 类声明自己需要什么，而不自己创建

means.en: the composition root or a DI container passes it in
means.zh: 组合根或 DI 容器把依赖传进去

means.en: the real implementation in production
means.zh: 生产环境的真实实现

thing.en: the wooden battery on the test bench

means.en: a fake injected in tests: no network, no database
means.zh: 测试时注入的假对象：不连网络和数据库

summary.en: Strategy swaps an algorithm at runtime, Observer notifies subscribers of a change, Adapter makes an incompatible interface fit.
summary.zh: 策略模式在运行时替换算法，观察者模式向订阅者通知变化，适配器模式让不兼容的接口对上。

explain.en: Strategy: put a family of interchangeable algorithms behind one interface and choose one at runtime (shipping cost per courier, a sort order); it replaces a long if/else chain. Observer: a subject keeps a list of observers and notifies them when its state changes, so it need not know who reacts (UI listeners, domain events). Watch for leaks from forgotten subscriptions and for cascades that are hard to follow. Adapter: wrap an existing class so it offers the interface a client expects, changing neither side, for example wrapping a legacy XML payment SDK to implement your PaymentGateway. All three come from the 1994 'Gang of Four' book. Reach for them when the problem appears, not in advance.
explain.zh: 策略模式：把一族可互换的算法放在同一接口后面，运行时再选（按快递公司计算运费、选择排序方式），用来替代冗长的 if/else。观察者模式：主题维护一份观察者列表，状态变化时通知它们，主题无需知道谁在响应（界面监听器、领域事件）。要当心忘记退订造成的泄漏，以及难以追踪的连锁反应。适配器模式：包装一个现有类，让它提供调用方期望的接口，两边都不用改，比如把老旧的 XML 支付 SDK 包装成你的 PaymentGateway。三者都出自 1994 年的“四人帮”（GoF）一书。等问题真正出现时再用，不要提前套用。

example.en: Strategy: price = pricing.compute(cart), where pricing is RegularPricing or BlackFridayPricing, chosen from config. Observer: an order.placed event fires and the email, inventory and analytics listeners each react; adding a loyalty listener changes nothing else. Adapter: class LegacyPayAdapter(PaymentGateway) turns charge(amount) into the old SDK's doPayment(xml).
example.zh: 策略：price = pricing.compute(cart)，pricing 按配置取 RegularPricing 或 BlackFridayPricing。观察者：order.placed 触发，邮件、库存、分析监听器各自响应，加积分监听器无需改别处。适配器：LegacyPayAdapter(PaymentGateway) 把 charge(amount) 转成旧 SDK 的 doPayment(xml)。

image.en: In the middle of the workshop a big brass bell swings, and a dog and a cat on either side prick up their ears at the same moment. On the left a carpenter in a beret studies a signpost, 'ship' one way and 'fly' the other, choosing the delivery method only now. On the right a funnel sits in the neck of a slim bottle, so the fat barrel next to it can finally pour in.
image.zh: 工坊中央，一口大铜钟摇响，两边的狗和猫同时竖起耳朵。左边，戴贝雷帽的木匠盯着路牌，一边写“海运”，一边写“空运”，到这时才决定怎么发货。右边，一只漏斗插在细瓶口上，旁边的胖木桶终于能往里倒了。

means.zh: 观察者：主题宣布状态变化

thing.en: dog and cat reacting at once

means.en: subscribers are notified; the subject need not know them
means.zh: 订阅者收到通知，主题不必认识它们

means.zh: 策略：运行时选择可互换的算法
