means.zh: 适配器：让不兼容的接口对上

summary.en: Working on one codebase with many people: Git's model and workflows, code review, readable code, refactoring and technical debt.
summary.zh: 多人协作开发同一份代码：Git 的模型与工作流、代码评审、可读性、重构和技术债。

summary.en: Git's data model and the everyday workflows built on it: branches, merges, rebases and undoing mistakes.
summary.zh: Git 的数据模型及其上的日常工作流：分支、合并、变基和撤销错误。

summary.en: A commit is a snapshot of the whole project named by a hash; branches are movable pointers, and HEAD marks where you are.
summary.zh: 提交是整个项目的快照，以哈希命名；分支是可移动的指针，HEAD 标明你所在的位置。

explain.en: Git stores snapshots, not diffs. A commit records a tree (the full project state; unchanged files are shared, not copied), its parent commits, the author and a message. Its id is a hash of that content (SHA-1 by default, SHA-256 optionally), so changing anything in a commit or its ancestry changes the id. Parent links make history a directed acyclic graph; a merge commit has two parents. A branch is just a movable pointer to one commit, stored as a tiny file, and committing moves the current branch forward. HEAD names what is checked out, normally a branch; pointing it straight at a commit gives a 'detached HEAD'. Tags are pointers that do not move. Diffs are computed on demand by comparing snapshots.
explain.zh: Git 存的是快照，不是差异。一个提交记录一棵树（项目的完整状态，未改动的文件共享而非复制）、父提交、作者和说明。提交的 id 是对这些内容取的哈希（默认 SHA-1，可选 SHA-256），所以改动提交本身或它的任何祖先都会改变 id。父链接让历史成为有向无环图，合并提交有两个父提交。分支只是指向某个提交的可移动指针，存成一个小文件，提交时当前分支随之前移。HEAD 表示当前检出的位置，通常指向分支；直接指向某个提交就是“分离 HEAD”。标签是不会移动的指针。差异是比较两个快照时临时算出来的。

example.en: git commit on main creates commit a3f9c2e with parent 71bd04e and moves main to a3f9c2e. git switch -c fix creates the pointer fix at the same commit and points HEAD at it. Two more commits on fix move only fix; main still points to a3f9c2e. git log --graph --oneline --all draws the graph.
example.zh: 在 main 上 git commit：生成提交 a3f9c2e，父提交是 71bd04e，main 移到 a3f9c2e。git switch -c fix 在同一提交上创建指针 fix，并让 HEAD 指向它。在 fix 上再提交两次，只有 fix 前移，main 仍指向 a3f9c2e。git log --graph --oneline --all 可以画出这张图。

image.en: A steam train stands at the platform, its carriage hooked to the engine like a commit to its parent. Before anything new is coupled on, a photographer with a big camera on a crate shoots the whole station, so every carriage carries a complete picture, not a list of changes. A red flag reading 'main' is planted at the newest end of the train, and the conductor, HEAD, points at it, ready to move it forward.
image.zh: 一列蒸汽火车停在站台，车厢挂在机车后面，就像提交连着它的父提交。每挂上新车厢之前，摄影师都会用木箱上的大相机把整个车站拍下来，所以每节车厢装的是一张完整的照片，而不是改动清单。写着“main”的红旗插在列车最新的一端，列车长 HEAD 指着它，随时准备把它往前挪。

means.en: each commit points to its parent: history is a graph
means.zh: 每个提交指向父提交：历史是一张图

means.en: a commit stores a full snapshot, not a diff
means.zh: 提交保存完整快照，而非差异

means.en: a branch: a movable pointer to the newest commit
means.zh: 分支：指向最新提交的可移动指针

means.en: HEAD: what you have checked out
means.zh: HEAD：当前检出的位置

summary.en: Trunk-based development merges small, short-lived branches into main every day; Git Flow keeps long-lived develop and release branches.
summary.zh: 主干开发每天把短命的小分支合入 main；Git Flow 则维护长期存在的 develop 和 release 分支。

explain.en: A branching strategy sets how work flows into the shared code. In trunk-based development everyone integrates into main at least daily, through short-lived branches and small pull requests (or direct commits backed by strong CI); unfinished features hide behind feature flags, and main stays releasable. Merges stay small, which suits continuous delivery. Git Flow (2010) keeps long-lived main and develop branches plus feature, release and hotfix branches; it fits software shipped in numbered versions but tends to produce large, late merges. GitHub flow is a lighter middle path: branch from main, open a pull request, review, merge, deploy. Long-lived branches drift apart and merge painfully, which is why most web teams now prefer trunk-based work.
explain.zh: 分支策略规定工作如何汇入共享代码。主干开发（trunk-based development）要求每个人至少每天向 main 集成一次，通过短命分支和小型拉取请求（或在可靠 CI 保障下直接提交）；未完成的功能藏在特性开关后面，main 始终可发布。每次合并都很小，契合持续交付。Git Flow（2010）维护长期存在的 main 和 develop，外加 feature、release、hotfix 分支，适合按版本号发布的软件，但容易造成又大又晚的合并。GitHub flow 是更轻的折中：从 main 拉分支、提拉取请求、评审、合并、部署。长期分支会越走越远，合并时很痛苦，所以如今多数 Web 团队偏爱主干开发。

example.en: Trunk-based: Mia branches add-coupon-field at 10:00, opens a 60-line pull request at 14:00, and it is reviewed and merged by 16:00; the half-built coupon page stays behind a flag. Git Flow: a team works on feature branches off develop for three weeks, cuts release/2.4, fixes bugs there, then merges it into main and back into develop.
example.zh: 主干开发：Mia 上午 10 点拉出分支 add-coupon-field，下午 2 点提交 60 行的拉取请求，4 点前评审并合并；做了一半的优惠券页面藏在开关后面。Git Flow：团队在从 develop 拉出的 feature 分支上干三周，再拉出 release/2.4，在上面修 bug，最后合入 main 并回合到 develop。

image.en: On platform 1 the main-line train is boarding. Porters hurry up every few minutes, each with a single envelope, and toss it aboard, so nothing waits long; the giant station clock marks the day. Off to the side sits an enormous crate that has waited for weeks, with weeds sprouting on its lid, and it will no longer fit through the carriage door.
image.zh: 一号站台上，干线列车正在上客。搬运工每隔几分钟就跑过来，每人只拿一个信封，往车上一扔，什么都不会久等；巨大的站台钟记着日子。旁边搁着一只等了好几周的大木箱，箱盖上都长出了杂草，已经塞不进车厢门了。

means.en: main, the trunk: always ready to depart
means.zh: main，即主干：随时可以发车

thing.zh: 每人一个信封的搬运工

means.en: short-lived branches and small pull requests
means.zh: 短命分支和小型拉取请求

means.en: integrate into main at least once a day
means.zh: 至少每天向 main 集成一次

means.en: a long-lived branch: it drifts and merges painfully
means.zh: 长期分支：越走越远，合并痛苦

summary.en: Merge joins two histories with a merge commit; rebase replays your commits onto a new base. Never rebase commits others already have.
summary.zh: 合并用合并提交把两段历史连起来；变基把你的提交重放到新的基点上。别人已拿到的提交不要变基。

explain.en: When main and your branch have both moved on, git merge creates a merge commit with two parents: history stays exactly as it happened, at the cost of a branching graph. git rebase main instead replays each of your commits on top of the current main, creating new commits with new hashes and a straight line of history; conflicts are resolved one commit at a time. Because rebase rewrites commits, never rebase commits others have pulled: their copies still hold the old ones, and their next pull tangles old and new together. A common team rule: rebase your private branch to stay current, then merge it, or squash-merge it, through a pull request. git pull --rebase does the same for local work.
explain.zh: 当 main 和你的分支都各自前进后，git merge 生成一个有两个父提交的合并提交：历史按真实发生的样子保留，代价是提交图出现分叉。git rebase main 则把你的每个提交重放到当前 main 之上，生成哈希全新的提交，历史成一条直线；冲突要逐个提交解决。变基会改写提交，所以绝不要对别人已经拉取的提交变基：他们手里仍是旧提交，下次拉取时新旧两份会纠缠在一起。常见的团队约定：私有分支用变基跟上 main，再通过拉取请求合并或压缩合并。git pull --rebase 对本地工作也是这么做的。

example.en: main has commits A–B–C; your branch has A–X–Y. git merge main on your branch adds a merge commit M whose parents are Y and C. git rebase main instead gives A–B–C–X'–Y': X' and Y' carry the same changes as X and Y but have new hashes, so you must force-push the branch with git push --force-with-lease.
example.zh: main 上是 A–B–C，你的分支是 A–X–Y。在分支上 git merge main，会新增合并提交 M，父提交是 Y 和 C。改用 git rebase main，得到 A–B–C–X'–Y'：X' 和 Y' 的改动与 X、Y 相同，但哈希是新的，所以要用 git push --force-with-lease 强推分支。

image.en: A crane on the platform lifts your blue wagon off its old siding and swings it over to the end of the main-line wagons, where it will get a fresh number plate. The operator only ever lifts his own wagon. On the left is the other way to join up: the green wagon stays exactly where it stood, and a heavy chain couples it to the main line.
image.zh: 站台上的吊车把你的蓝色货车厢从旧岔道上吊起，转到干线车厢的末尾，放下后它会换上新的车号牌。操作员只吊自己的车厢。左边是另一种接法：绿色车厢原地不动，一条粗铁链把它和干线连在一起。

means.en: rebase: replay your commits on top of the new tip
means.zh: 变基：把你的提交重放到最新的顶端

means.en: rebased commits are new commits with new hashes
means.zh: 变基后的提交是哈希全新的新提交

means.en: merge: a merge commit joins both histories as they were
means.zh: 合并：合并提交把两段历史原样连起来

thing.en: he lifts only his own wagon

means.en: never rebase commits that others have pulled
means.zh: 别人拉取过的提交绝不变基

summary.en: git revert adds a new commit that cancels an old one; git reset moves a branch pointer; the reflog remembers where HEAD has been.
summary.zh: git revert 新增一个提交来抵消旧提交；git reset 移动分支指针；reflog 记得 HEAD 去过的位置。

explain.en: git revert <commit> creates a new commit whose changes are the inverse of the old one. History only grows, so it safely undoes pushed, shared work. git reset moves the current branch pointer to another commit: --soft keeps the changes staged, --mixed (the default) keeps them in the working tree, --hard throws them away. Reset rewrites the branch, so use it only on commits nobody else has. git restore discards uncommitted edits to files. After a bad reset the commits are not gone at once: the reflog records every position of HEAD and of each branch (by default for 90 days, or 30 for unreachable entries), so git reflog shows the old hash and git reset --hard <hash> brings it back. Uncommitted work wiped by reset --hard is truly lost.
explain.zh: git revert <提交> 生成一个新提交，内容恰好抵消旧提交的改动。历史只增不减，适合撤销已推送的内容。git reset 把当前分支指针移到另一个提交：--soft 把改动留在暂存区，--mixed（默认）留在工作区，--hard 直接丢弃。reset 会改写分支，只能用于没人拿到的提交。git restore 丢弃文件里未提交的修改。reset 错了，提交也不会立刻消失：reflog 记录 HEAD 和各分支去过的每个位置（默认保留 90 天，不可达条目 30 天），用 git reflog 找到旧哈希，再 git reset --hard <哈希> 即可找回。但 reset --hard 抹掉的未提交改动无法找回。

example.en: A pushed commit 9e1d4b2 broke the build: git revert 9e1d4b2 adds commit c07f311 that undoes it, and teammates simply pull. You made two local commits by mistake: git reset --soft HEAD~2 removes them and keeps the edits staged. You ran git reset --hard HEAD~3 by accident: git reflog shows HEAD@{1} at 4a5b6c7, and git reset --hard 4a5b6c7 restores it.
example.zh: 已推送的提交 9e1d4b2 搞坏了构建：git revert 9e1d4b2 新增提交 c07f311 抵消它，队友直接拉取即可。本地误提交了两次：git reset --soft HEAD~2 撤掉这两个提交，改动仍在暂存区。不小心执行了 git reset --hard HEAD~3：git reflog 显示 HEAD@{1} 在 4a5b6c7，git reset --hard 4a5b6c7 即可恢复。

image.en: Three wagons stand on the track, and the last one is painted red: a bad commit. Next to it stands a mirror holding its reversed image, coupled on like one more wagon, so the train only grows. In front, a giant hand plucks up the 'main' flag to plant it further back along the train. The station master reads his logbook, where every spot the flag has ever stood is written down.
image.zh: 轨道上停着三节车厢，最后一节漆成红色：一个坏提交。它旁边立着一面镜子，映出它的反像，像多挂了一节车厢，列车只会变长。前面，一只巨手拔起写着“main”的旗子，要把它插回更靠后的位置。站长在读他的日志本，旗子到过的每个位置都记在上面。

thing.en: the mirror next to the red wagon

means.en: revert: a new commit that inverts the bad one
means.zh: revert：新增一个抵消坏提交的提交

means.en: safe for shared history: nothing is rewritten
means.zh: 对共享历史安全：不改写任何东西

means.en: reset: move the branch pointer (soft, mixed, hard)
means.zh: reset：移动分支指针（soft、mixed、hard）

means.en: the reflog: every past position, for recovery
means.zh: reflog：记下所有旧位置，用于找回

summary.en: Keeping a codebase healthy: reviews, names that explain themselves, refactoring under tests and debt paid down on purpose.
summary.zh: 让代码库保持健康：评审、自解释的命名、有测试保护的重构，以及有计划地偿还技术债。

summary.en: A second pair of eyes on every change catches defects, improves design and spreads knowledge; small pull requests make it work.
summary.zh: 每个改动都让第二双眼睛看过：发现缺陷、改进设计、传播知识；小型拉取请求让评审真正有效。

explain.en: In code review a teammate reads a change before it merges, usually as a pull request. The goals are correctness (bugs, edge cases, security), design (does it fit the architecture, is it simple), readability, and shared knowledge, so that more than one person understands each part. Review works only on small changes: a reviewer can digest a few hundred lines, while a 2,000-line diff gets a skim and a rubber stamp. Authors explain the why in the description and review their own diff first. Reviewers are prompt, specific and kind: comment on the code, not the person, ask questions, mark nits as optional, and approve when the change makes the code better, even if they would have written it differently. Leave style to formatters and linters.
explain.zh: 代码评审是在改动合并前由同事阅读，通常以拉取请求的形式进行。目标包括正确性（缺陷、边界情况、安全）、设计（是否契合架构、是否简单）、可读性，以及知识共享，让每块代码都不止一个人懂。评审只对小改动有效：几百行还能消化，两千行的 diff 只会换来草草一瞥和走过场的批准。作者在描述里写清为什么，并先自审一遍。评审者要及时、具体、友善：对事不对人，多提问，把吹毛求疵的意见标为可选；只要改动让代码变好就批准，哪怕和自己的写法不同。代码风格交给格式化和静态检查工具。

example.en: Instead of 'this is wrong', write: 'If items is empty, line 42 divides by zero. Should we return 0 early? Happy to pair on it.' Label minor points 'nit: could be named total_cents'. Split an 1,800-line pull request into a schema migration, a repository change and an API change, each reviewable in about 20 minutes.
example.zh: 不要写“这里错了”，而是写：“items 为空时第 42 行会除以零，要不要提前返回 0？需要的话可以一起结对看看。”次要意见标上“nit：可以命名为 total_cents”。把 1800 行的拉取请求拆成数据库迁移、仓储层修改和 API 修改三个，每个大约 20 分钟就能评审完。

image.en: In the gallery a small portrait stands on an easel, and a critic in a beret leans in with a magnifying glass, pointing at one brushstroke and asking about line 42. Next to it towers an enormous abstract canvas. Nobody studies it: a bored attendant just stands by a giant green rubber stamp and shrugs.
image.zh: 美术馆里，画架上立着一幅小肖像，戴贝雷帽的评论家拿着放大镜凑近，指着一笔颜料问第 42 行的事。旁边耸立着一幅巨大的抽象画，没人细看：无聊的管理员只是站在一枚绿色大橡皮图章旁边，耸了耸肩。

means.en: a small pull request gets a careful review
means.zh: 小型拉取请求得到仔细评审

means.en: specific, kind comments that ask rather than accuse
means.zh: 具体、友善、多提问的评论

means.en: a huge diff gets skimmed and rubber-stamped
means.zh: 巨大的 diff 只会被草草批准

thing.en: the critic now knows the painting

means.en: review spreads knowledge of the code
means.zh: 评审传播对代码的了解

summary.en: Code is read far more often than it is written: use names that reveal intent, keep functions small, and let comments explain why.
summary.zh: 代码被读的次数远多于被写的次数：用能揭示意图的名字，保持函数短小，让注释解释“为什么”。

explain.en: A good name says what a thing is for, in the problem's vocabulary: elapsed_days instead of d, is_eligible_for_refund() instead of check(). Names should be pronounceable, searchable and consistent (do not mix fetch, get and retrieve for one idea), and carry units where they matter (timeout_ms). Small functions that do one thing at one level of abstraction read like a table of contents, and early returns flatten nested ifs. Comments should explain why: a business rule, a workaround, a non-obvious trade-off. Comments that repeat what the code says go stale and mislead; if code needs a comment to say what it does, rename or extract first. Readability is judged by the next reader, often you in six months.
explain.zh: 好名字用问题领域的词汇说明它的用途：用 elapsed_days 而不是 d，用 is_eligible_for_refund() 而不是 check()。名字要能读出来、能搜索、前后一致（同一概念不要混用 fetch、get、retrieve），需要时带上单位（timeout_ms）。只做一件事、停在同一抽象层次的小函数读起来像目录，提前返回能压平层层嵌套的 if。注释应解释为什么：业务规则、临时绕过、不明显的权衡。复述代码在做什么的注释会过时并误导人；代码要靠注释才看得懂时，先改名或提取函数。可读性由下一个读者评判，而那常常是六个月后的你。

example.en: Before: if (u.t == 2 && d <= 30) ok(); // check user. After: if user.is_premium() and days_since_purchase <= PREMIUM_REFUND_DAYS: approve_refund(), with the comment '# Finance gives premium users a longer refund window (ticket PAY-212).' The names say what; the comment says why.
example.zh: 改写前：if (u.t == 2 && d <= 30) ok(); // check user。改写后：if user.is_premium() and days_since_purchase <= PREMIUM_REFUND_DAYS: approve_refund()，并附注释“# 财务给高级会员更长的退款期（工单 PAY-212）”。名字说明做什么，注释说明为什么。

image.en: Two paintings stand on easels. The label under the left one says only 'd'; a visitor squints at it through a magnifying glass and shrugs. The label under the right one reads 'elapsed_days', and the visitor there throws up her arms in delight: she understood it at a glance.
image.zh: 两幅画立在画架上。左边那幅的标签只写着“d”，一位参观者举着放大镜眯眼看了半天，只能耸耸肩。右边那幅的标签写着“elapsed_days”，那里的参观者高兴地举起双臂：她一眼就看懂了。

thing.zh: 标签 d 和眯眼的参观者

means.en: a cryptic name makes every reader decode it
means.zh: 晦涩的名字让每个读者都得破译

means.en: an intention-revealing name in the domain's words
means.zh: 用领域词汇揭示意图的名字

means.en: code is read far more than written: write for the reader
means.zh: 代码读多于写：为读者而写

thing.zh: 背景上的“注释写为什么”

means.en: comments explain reasons, not mechanics
means.zh: 注释解释原因，不复述做法

summary.en: Refactoring changes code's structure without changing its behaviour, in small steps under tests; code smells show where to start.
summary.zh: 重构在不改变外部行为的前提下调整代码结构，小步进行并有测试保护；代码坏味道指出从哪里下手。

explain.en: Refactoring (Fowler) is a disciplined, behaviour-preserving change to the internal structure of code: rename, extract function, move method, replace conditional with polymorphism. Each step is small and is followed by running the tests, so the system keeps working; without tests it is just risky editing. Code smells are symptoms that suggest a refactoring is due: a long method, a large class, duplicated code, long parameter lists, feature envy (a method more interested in another class's data) and shotgun surgery, where one logical change forces small edits in many classes. Commit refactorings separately from behaviour changes, so reviewers can see nothing else moved, and refactor the code you are about to change rather than everything at once.
explain.zh: 重构（Fowler）是一种有纪律、保持行为不变的代码内部结构调整：改名、提取函数、搬移方法、以多态取代条件表达式。每一步都很小，做完就跑测试，系统始终可用；没有测试的“重构”只是冒险的修改。代码坏味道是提示该重构的征兆：过长函数、过大的类、重复代码、过长参数列表、依恋情结（方法更关心别的类的数据），以及霰弹式修改：一个逻辑改动要在许多类里各改一点。重构与行为改动要分开提交，方便评审确认别的都没动；先重构马上要改的那部分代码，而不是一次全改。

example.en: The same 15 lines that compute shipping cost appear in checkout.py, invoice.py and quote.py, so a new tax rule needs three edits: duplication plus shotgun surgery. With the tests green, extract shipping_cost(order) into one module, replace each copy with a call, and rerun the tests after each replacement. Behaviour is unchanged, and the next tax rule is a one-line change.
example.zh: 计算运费的同样 15 行代码出现在 checkout.py、invoice.py 和 quote.py 里，新税规要改三处：重复代码加霰弹式修改。在测试全绿的前提下，把 shipping_cost(order) 提取到一个模块，逐个把副本换成调用，每换一处跑一次测试。行为不变，下一条税规只需改一行。

image.en: In the gallery a fountain sculpture keeps splashing while a plumber in a hard hat untangles the knot of pipes beside it, one joint at a time. After every turn of his wrench he glances at a small traffic light: still green. A dead fish lies in front of the tangle; its smell told him where to start.
image.zh: 美术馆里，喷泉雕塑照常喷水，旁边一位戴安全帽的管道工正把一团乱麻似的管子一节一节理顺。他每拧一下扳手，就瞄一眼旁边的小红绿灯：还是绿的。乱管子前躺着一条死鱼，正是那股味道告诉他该从哪儿下手。

means.en: refactoring: improve the internal structure
means.zh: 重构：改善内部结构

means.en: external behaviour stays the same
means.zh: 外部行为保持不变

means.en: small steps, tests run after each one
means.zh: 小步前进，每步都跑测试

means.en: a code smell: long method, duplication, shotgun surgery
means.zh: 代码坏味道：过长函数、重复、霰弹式修改

summary.en: Shortcuts in code work like a loan: you ship sooner, then pay interest on every later change until you pay the principal back.
summary.zh: 代码里的捷径像贷款：先更快交付，之后每次修改都要付利息，直到把本金还清。

explain.en: Ward Cunningham's metaphor: shipping code that does not yet reflect our best understanding is like borrowing money. The principal is the work needed to clean it up; the interest is the extra time, bugs and risk paid on every change that touches it. Martin Fowler's quadrant splits debt into deliberate or inadvertent and prudent or reckless: 'ship now and refactor after the launch' is deliberate and prudent; 'what is layering?' is inadvertent and reckless. Some debt is a sound business choice, if it is recorded and repaid. Pay down debt where the interest is highest, in code that changes often, ideally while doing feature work there (the boy-scout rule) plus a steady share of capacity; code that never changes can carry debt cheaply.
explain.zh: Ward Cunningham 的比喻：交付尚未体现我们最佳理解的代码，就像借钱。本金是日后清理所需的工作；利息是每次改动这段代码时多付出的时间、缺陷和风险。Martin Fowler 的四象限按“有意/无意”和“审慎/鲁莽”划分技术债：“先上线，发布后再重构”是有意且审慎的；“分层是什么？”是无意且鲁莽的。有些债是合理的商业选择，前提是记录在案并按时偿还。优先还利息最高的债，也就是常改的代码，最好在那里做功能时顺手清理（童子军规则），再固定留出一部分产能；从不改动的代码背着债也没什么成本。

example.en: To make a launch date, a team hard-codes three currencies in eight places instead of building a currency table, and ships two weeks earlier. Every later change that involves currency now takes an extra day, and 12 such changes are planned next quarter: 12 days of interest. Building the table, the principal, would take 4 days, so paying it down first is clearly cheaper.
example.zh: 为赶上线日期，团队把三种货币硬编码在八个地方，没有建货币表，提前两周上线。此后每个涉及货币的改动都要多花一天，下季度计划了 12 个这样的改动，也就是 12 天的利息。建货币表（本金）只需 4 天，先还债显然更划算。

image.en: A developer in the gallery hauls a huge black iron ball across the floor on a heavy chain, and every step costs her effort. Beside the ball a banker in a top hat holds out a gold coin and points at a tall stack of coins that grows with each step she drags it.
image.zh: 美术馆里，一位开发者用粗铁链拖着一颗巨大的黑铁球在地上走，每一步都很吃力。铁球旁，戴高礼帽的银行家举着一枚金币，指着一摞高高的金币：她每拖一步，这摞金币就高一截。

means.en: the principal: the shortcut that must be cleaned up
means.zh: 本金：迟早要清理的捷径

means.en: interest: extra effort on every change that touches it
means.zh: 利息：每次相关改动都要多费力

means.en: record the loan and plan repayment
means.zh: 把借款记下来，计划偿还

means.en: unpaid interest keeps accumulating
means.zh: 不还的利息不断累积

summary.en: Storing data correctly, quickly and at scale: relational design and indexes, transactions under concurrency, and spreading data across machines.
summary.zh: 正确、快速、可扩展地存储数据：关系设计与索引、并发下的事务，以及把数据分布到多台机器。

summary.en: Tables, keys and indexes: how a relational schema avoids anomalies and how indexes make queries fast.
summary.zh: 表、键与索引：关系模式如何避免异常，索引如何让查询变快。

summary.en: Primary keys identify rows, foreign keys link tables, and normal forms store each fact once so updates cannot contradict each other.
summary.zh: 主键标识行，外键连接表，范式让每个事实只存一次，更新时就不会自相矛盾。

explain.en: A relational table holds rows that share the same columns. A primary key uniquely identifies each row; a foreign key references the primary key of another table, and the database can enforce that the referenced row exists. Normalisation stores each fact once. 1NF: every column holds one atomic value, with no lists or repeating groups. 2NF: no non-key column depends on only part of a composite key. 3NF: no non-key column depends on another non-key column. Redundant copies cause anomalies: an address changed in one row but not another, a customer who cannot be recorded before a first order, a customer lost with the last order. Denormalise deliberately, for read-heavy reports or caches, and accept the work of keeping copies in sync.
explain.zh: 关系表由列相同的行组成。主键唯一标识每一行；外键引用另一张表的主键，数据库可以强制被引用的行必须存在。规范化让每个事实只存一次。第一范式：每列只有一个原子值，没有列表或重复组。第二范式：非键列不能只依赖复合键的一部分。第三范式：非键列不能依赖其他非键列。冗余副本会造成异常：地址只改了一行没改另一行；客户下第一单前无法登记；删掉最后一个订单，客户也跟着没了。只在读多写少的报表或缓存场景有意反规范化，并承担同步副本的成本。

example.en: orders(id, customer_name, customer_city, product_id, price_paid) repeats Ana's city on all 40 of her orders; when she moves, one missed row gives her two cities. Split it into customers(id PK, name, city) and orders(id PK, customer_id FK → customers.id, product_id, price_paid). Her city is now stored once, and no order can point to a customer who does not exist.
example.zh: orders(id, customer_name, customer_city, product_id, price_paid) 在 Ana 的 40 个订单里都存了城市，搬家时漏改一行就有了两个城市。拆成 customers(id 主键, name, city) 和 orders(id 主键, customer_id 外键, product_id, price_paid)：城市只存一次，订单也不能指向不存在的客户。

image.en: Two reading tables stand in the library. The left one holds the customers: a giant gold key stands beside a single book that records Ana's city, once. The right one holds the orders: three books lie in a row, and a heavy chain runs from them to the left table instead of each book copying the city. The librarian gestures at the lone book: change it there and every order sees the change.
image.zh: 图书馆里摆着两张阅览桌。左桌放客户：一把巨大的金钥匙立在一本书旁，这本书只记了一次 Ana 的城市。右桌放订单：三本书并排放着，一条粗铁链从它们那儿连到左桌，而不是每本书各抄一遍城市。图书管理员指着那本书：在那里改一处，所有订单都会看到。

means.en: primary key: uniquely identifies each row
means.zh: 主键：唯一标识每一行

thing.zh: 从订单连到客户的铁链

means.en: foreign key: a checked reference to another table
means.zh: 外键：受约束的跨表引用

thing.en: the city written in one book
thing.zh: 只写在一本书里的城市

means.en: normalisation: each fact stored once
means.zh: 规范化：每个事实只存一次

means.en: no update anomalies: a change happens in one place
means.zh: 没有更新异常：改动只发生在一处

summary.en: A sorted, wide and shallow tree turns a full scan into a few page reads for lookups and range scans alike, at a cost on every write.
summary.zh: 一棵有序、宽而矮的树，让等值查找和范围扫描都只需几次页读取，代价是每次写入都要维护它。

explain.en: Most relational databases index with B+ trees. Each node is a disk page holding hundreds of sorted keys, so the fan-out is high and the tree is shallow: three or four levels cover hundreds of millions of rows. Internal nodes only route; all keys sit in the leaves, which are linked in key order. A lookup walks from the root to one leaf in O(log n) page reads, and a range query (BETWEEN, ORDER BY, a prefix LIKE 'ab%') finds its start and then follows the leaf links. Without an index the database must scan every row. Indexes are not free: every insert, delete or update of an indexed column must also update each index, and they take space, so index the columns your queries filter, join and sort by, not everything.
explain.zh: 多数关系数据库用 B+ 树做索引。每个节点是一个磁盘页，存着几百个有序的键，因此扇出大、树很矮：三四层就能覆盖数亿行。内部节点只负责导航，所有键都在叶子里，叶子按键的顺序串成链表。查找从根走到一个叶子，只需 O(log n) 次页读取；范围查询（BETWEEN、ORDER BY、前缀匹配 LIKE 'ab%'）先找到起点，再沿叶子链表往后读。没有索引就只能逐行扫描。索引并非免费：插入、删除或更新被索引的列时，每个相关索引都要同步更新，还要占空间。所以只为查询里用来过滤、连接和排序的列建索引，而不是什么都建。

example.en: A users table has 100 million rows. With a fan-out of 500, a B+ tree on email needs 3 levels (500³ = 125 million), so WHERE email = 'ana@x.io' costs about 3 or 4 page reads instead of a scan of 100 million rows. With created_at indexed, WHERE created_at BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-01-31' finds 1 January and walks the leaves to 31 January.
example.zh: users 表有 1 亿行。扇出为 500 时，email 上的 B+ 树只要 3 层（500³ = 1.25 亿），WHERE email = 'ana@x.io' 大约 3 到 4 次页读取，而不必扫描 1 亿行。created_at 有索引时，WHERE created_at BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-01-31' 先定位到 1 月 1 日，再沿叶子读到 1 月 31 日。

image.en: A golden sculpture of a wide, shallow tree stands in the library, and in front of it four book stacks, the leaves, are lined up in order. A librarian traces a path from the root down to one stack in three moves, while a mouse scampers along the tops of the stacks, reading them one after another. A porter arrives carrying a new book: it must be filed into the tree as well.
image.zh: 图书馆里立着一座金色的树形雕塑，宽而矮；树前四摞书按顺序排成一行，那是叶子。图书管理员用三步就从树根指到其中一摞，一只老鼠则沿着书摞顶上一路跑过去，挨个读。一位搬运工抱着一本新书走来：它也得归档进这棵树里。

means.en: high fan-out: 3 or 4 levels for millions of rows
means.zh: 扇出大：三四层容纳上亿行

means.en: an O(log n) lookup from root to leaf
means.zh: 从根到叶的 O(log n) 查找

means.en: a range scan along the linked leaves
means.zh: 沿叶子链表的范围扫描

means.en: every write must update the index too
means.zh: 每次写入也要更新索引

summary.en: An index on (a, b, c) serves queries that use its leftmost columns; if it holds every column a query needs, the table is never read.
summary.zh: (a, b, c) 上的索引服务于使用其最左列的查询；若它包含查询所需的全部列，就根本不用回表。

explain.en: A composite index sorts entries by several columns in order, like a phone book sorted by surname, then first name. A query can use it only through a leftmost prefix: an index on (last, first, city) serves WHERE last = ?, or last = ? AND first = ?, but usually not WHERE first = ? alone; and a range condition on one column stops the columns after it from narrowing the search. Put equality columns first and the range or sort column after them. A covering index contains every column a query reads, so the answer comes from the index alone (an index-only scan) without fetching table rows. EXPLAIN shows the chosen plan: full scan or index scan, estimated rows, and 'Using index' in MySQL or 'Index Only Scan' in PostgreSQL.
explain.zh: 复合索引按多列依次排序，就像电话簿先按姓、再按名排列。查询只能通过最左前缀使用它：(last, first, city) 上的索引能服务 WHERE last = ?、last = ? AND first = ?，但通常不能单独服务 WHERE first = ?；某列用了范围条件，后面的列就无法再缩小范围。所以等值列在前，范围列或排序列在后。覆盖索引包含查询要读的全部列，只读索引就能作答（仅索引扫描），不必回表。EXPLAIN 显示执行计划：全表扫描还是索引扫描、预估行数，以及 MySQL 的 Using index 或 PostgreSQL 的 Index Only Scan。

example.en: Query: SELECT status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 7 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10. An index on (customer_id, created_at) finds customer 7's rows already sorted, then reads 10 table rows. An index on (customer_id, created_at, status, total) covers the query, so no table rows are read at all. An index on (created_at, customer_id) is in the wrong order: it cannot jump straight to customer 7.
example.zh: 查询：SELECT status, total … WHERE customer_id = 7 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10。索引 (customer_id, created_at) 找到的行已排好序，再回表读 10 行；再加上 status, total 就覆盖了查询，不用回表；(created_at, customer_id) 顺序不对，跳不到客户 7。

image.en: A giant directory lies open on a stand, sorted by surname and then by first name. The librarian has found 'Smith, Ana' in two flips and is already dialling the number printed right there. A visitor who knows only the first name 'Ana' scratches his head: he would have to read every page. Behind them nobody touches the bookshelf, and a cat sleeps on top of it.
image.zh: 一本巨大的电话簿摊开在书架前，先按姓、再按名排序。图书管理员翻两下就找到了“Smith, Ana”，正照着上面印的号码拨电话。只知道名字叫“Ana”的访客直挠头：他得把每一页都读一遍。他们身后的书架没人去碰，一只猫在架顶睡得正香。

thing.en: directory sorted by surname, then name
thing.zh: 先按姓再按名的电话簿

means.en: a composite index on (last, first)
means.zh: (last, first) 上的复合索引

means.en: a leftmost prefix: last, or last + first
means.zh: 最左前缀：last，或 last + first

means.en: first alone skips the leftmost column: little help
means.zh: 只有 first 跳过了最左列：帮不上忙

thing.en: number printed in the book, sleeping cat
thing.zh: 书里印着号码，猫在睡觉

means.en: a covering index: the table is never touched
means.zh: 覆盖索引：根本不用回表

summary.en: Keeping data correct when many clients read and write at once: ACID, isolation levels, MVCC and locking.
summary.zh: 多个客户端同时读写时保持数据正确：ACID、隔离级别、MVCC 和锁。

summary.en: A transaction's writes happen all or not at all, keep the data valid, stay invisible to others until done, and survive crashes.
summary.zh: 事务的写入要么全做要么全不做，数据保持有效，完成前别人看不到，提交后崩溃也不丢失。

explain.en: Atomicity: all of a transaction's writes take effect or none do; on an error it rolls back. Consistency: a transaction moves the database from one valid state to another, respecting constraints such as foreign keys and CHECK (balance >= 0); the application defines most of what 'valid' means. Isolation: concurrent transactions do not see each other's intermediate states; ideally the result equals some serial order, though weaker levels are common. Durability: once COMMIT returns, the change survives a crash. Most engines build atomicity and durability on a write-ahead log: changes are appended to it and flushed to disk before the commit is acknowledged, and after a crash the log is replayed so committed work is redone and unfinished work discarded.
explain.zh: 原子性：事务的写入要么全部生效，要么全部不生效；出错或崩溃时回滚。一致性：事务把数据库从一个有效状态带到另一个有效状态，遵守外键、CHECK (balance >= 0) 等约束；“有效”的大部分含义由应用定义。隔离性：并发事务看不到彼此的中间状态，理想情况下结果等同于某种串行顺序，但数据库为性能也提供更弱的级别。持久性：COMMIT 一旦返回，改动就能挺过崩溃。多数引擎靠预写日志（WAL）实现原子性和持久性：改动先追加到日志并刷盘，再确认提交；崩溃后重放日志，重做已提交的工作，丢弃未完成的部分。

example.en: Transfer 100 from account A (balance 500) to B (balance 200): BEGIN; UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 'A'; UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE id = 'B'; COMMIT. If the server crashes after the first UPDATE, recovery rolls it back: A has 500 and B 200, never 400 and 200. After COMMIT, A has 400 and B 300, even if the power fails a second later.
example.zh: A（500）转 100 给 B（200）：BEGIN; UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 'A'; UPDATE … + 100 WHERE id = 'B'; COMMIT。第一条 UPDATE 后崩溃，恢复时回滚：A 仍是 500、B 仍是 200，不会是 400 和 200。提交后 A 是 400、B 是 300，下一秒断电也不变。

image.en: In the vault a teller carries coins from safe A to safe B. Before he moved a single coin, the clerk at the lectern wrote the whole transfer into a heavy ledger. A guard holds up a shield so the child peering in cannot see the half-finished move. If the teller trips, every coin goes back into A; once the ledger entry is signed, the transfer stands even if the lights go out.
image.zh: 金库里，出纳把金币从保险箱 A 搬到保险箱 B。他动第一枚金币之前，讲台后的文书已把整笔转账写进厚厚的账本。卫兵举起盾牌，挡住探头张望的孩子，不让他看到搬了一半的样子。出纳要是摔一跤，金币全数回到 A；账本一签字，就算灯灭了，这笔转账也算数。

thing.en: coins from A to B, all or none
thing.zh: 金币从 A 到 B，全有或全无

means.en: atomicity: every write or no write
means.zh: 原子性：要么全写，要么不写

means.en: write-ahead log: durable after COMMIT, recoverable after a crash
means.zh: 预写日志：提交即持久，崩溃可恢复

means.en: isolation: nobody sees the half-done transfer
means.zh: 隔离性：谁也看不到做了一半的转账

means.en: consistency: rules such as balance ≥ 0 hold before and after
means.zh: 一致性：余额≥0 等规则前后都成立

relation.en: when one DB is not enough

summary.en: Weaker isolation lets transactions see dirty, changing or phantom data; stronger levels prevent more anomalies at a cost in concurrency.
summary.zh: 隔离越弱，事务越可能读到脏数据、变化的数据或幻影行；隔离越强，防住的异常越多，并发代价也越大。

explain.en: The SQL standard defines four levels by the anomalies they forbid. A dirty read sees another transaction's uncommitted write. A non-repeatable read sees a row change between two reads because another transaction committed in between. A phantom is a row that appears or vanishes when a range query is rerun. Read uncommitted allows all three; read committed prevents dirty reads; repeatable read also prevents non-repeatable reads; serializable prevents all of them and more, so the outcome equals some serial order. Engines differ: PostgreSQL defaults to read committed and its repeatable read (snapshot isolation) also blocks phantoms; MySQL InnoDB defaults to repeatable read. Snapshot isolation still allows write skew, which only serializable prevents.
explain.zh: SQL 标准按禁止的异常定义了四个级别。脏读：读到另一事务尚未提交的写入。不可重复读：同一行读两次结果不同，因为中间有别的事务提交了修改。幻读：重复执行范围查询时多出或少了行。读未提交三者都允许；读已提交防脏读；可重复读再防不可重复读；可串行化全部都防，还防住更多异常，结果等同于某种串行顺序。实际引擎与标准有出入：PostgreSQL 默认读已提交，它的可重复读（快照隔离）也能防幻读；MySQL InnoDB 默认可重复读。快照隔离仍允许写偏斜（write skew），只有可串行化才能防住。

example.en: Two doctors are on call, and the rule is that at least one must stay on call. Under snapshot isolation both start transactions, each sees 2 doctors on call, and each takes itself off call. Both commit, and now nobody is on call: write skew. Under serializable the database detects the conflict and aborts one of them. Under read committed, a report that sums balances twice in one transaction can get two different totals.
example.zh: 两位医生值班，规则是至少一人在岗。在快照隔离下，两人同时开启事务，各自看到“2 人在岗”，于是都把自己设为离岗。两个事务都提交后，没人值班了：这就是写偏斜。在可串行化下，数据库会检测到冲突并中止其中一个。在读已提交下，同一事务里两次汇总余额，可能得到两个不同的总数。

image.en: A clerk in the vault counts the gold bars lying in a row: three. While he looks away, a pale ghost glides in with a fourth bar balanced on its head, ready to lay it at the end of the row. When he counts again he gets four, and the thought bubble over his head asks '3 → 4?'
image.zh: 金库里，一位职员数着排成一行的金条：三根。他一转眼，一个苍白的幽灵飘了进来，头顶着第四根金条，正要放到队尾。他再数一遍，变成了四根，头上的思考泡泡问：“3 → 4？”

means.en: a phantom: a row that appears between two identical reads
means.zh: 幻读：两次相同查询之间冒出的行

means.en: one query, two answers inside one transaction
means.zh: 同一事务里同一查询两个答案

means.en: another transaction's committed insert
means.zh: 另一事务已提交的插入

means.en: stopped by serializable (and PostgreSQL's repeatable read)
means.zh: 可串行化可防（PostgreSQL 可重复读也能）

summary.en: The database keeps several versions of each row, so every transaction reads a consistent snapshot and readers never block writers.
summary.zh: 数据库为每行保留多个版本，每个事务读取一致的快照，读写互不阻塞。

explain.en: Under multiversion concurrency control an update creates a new version of the row instead of destroying the old one; the old version stays (beside it in PostgreSQL, in an undo log in InnoDB and Oracle) until no transaction needs it. Each transaction, or each statement under read committed, reads from a snapshot: it sees only versions committed before the snapshot was taken. So readers never wait for writers and writers never wait for readers; only two writers to the same row still conflict, by blocking or by aborting one. PostgreSQL, InnoDB and Oracle all work this way. The cost is cleanup: dead versions pile up and must be reclaimed (VACUUM in PostgreSQL, purge in InnoDB), and long-running transactions hold that cleanup back.
explain.zh: 多版本并发控制下，更新会为行创建新版本，而不是销毁旧版本；旧版本一直保留（PostgreSQL 放在新版本旁边，InnoDB 和 Oracle 放在 undo 日志里），直到没有事务再需要它。每个事务（读已提交下是每条语句）从快照读数据：只看得到快照建立前已提交的版本。于是读不等写、写不等读；只有两个写者改同一行时才冲突，要么阻塞，要么中止一个。PostgreSQL、InnoDB 和 Oracle 都靠它低成本地实现读已提交和快照隔离。代价是清理：失效版本会堆积，需要回收（PostgreSQL 的 VACUUM、InnoDB 的 purge），长事务会拖住清理。

example.en: At 10:00 transaction T1 starts a long report; its snapshot sees price = 10. At 10:01 T2 sets the price to 12 and commits, creating a new version. T1 keeps reading 10 until it ends, without locking anything and without blocking T2. A transaction that starts at 10:02 sees 12. Once T1 finishes, the version holding 10 is garbage and VACUUM reclaims it.
example.zh: 10:00 事务 T1 开始跑一份长报表，它的快照里 price = 10。10:01 T2 把价格改成 12 并提交，生成新版本。T1 直到结束都读到 10，既不加锁，也不阻塞 T2。10:02 开始的事务看到 12。T1 结束后，值为 10 的版本成了垃圾，由 VACUUM 回收。

image.en: Two blackboards stand side by side in the vault. A reader with a camera studies the old one, 'v1: 10', the version that existed when he started. At the same moment a writer chalks 'v2: 12' on the new one, and neither waits for the other. A small cleaning robot stands between them, ready to wipe the old board once the last reader has left.
image.zh: 金库里并排立着两块黑板。拿相机的读者盯着旧的那块“v1: 10”，那是他开始时就存在的版本。与此同时，写者在新黑板上写下“v2: 12”，两人谁也不等谁。中间站着一个小清洁机器人，等最后一位读者离开，就去擦掉旧黑板。

means.en: several versions of the same row
means.zh: 同一行的多个版本

thing.en: reader with his camera at v1
thing.zh: 拿相机看 v1 的读者

means.en: a snapshot: sees only what was committed when it began
means.zh: 快照：只看开始时已提交的内容

thing.zh: 写 v2 的写者，谁也不等

means.en: readers do not block writers, and writers do not block readers
means.zh: 读不阻塞写，写也不阻塞读

means.en: VACUUM or purge reclaims versions no one can see
means.zh: VACUUM 或 purge 回收无人可见的版本

summary.en: Pessimistic locking takes a lock before changing a row; optimistic locking checks a version when writing and retries if someone got there first.
summary.zh: 悲观锁在修改前先锁住行；乐观锁在写入时检查版本号，若被别人抢先就重试。

explain.en: Two users who read the same row and both write it back can lose an update: the second write silently overwrites the first. Pessimistic locking prevents this by locking first: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a transaction makes other writers wait until you commit. It is simple and right when conflicts are frequent and transactions short, but locks cut concurrency and can deadlock. Optimistic locking takes no lock: each row carries a version number, and the write is a compare-and-set: UPDATE ... SET ..., version = version + 1 WHERE id = ? AND version = ?. If no row was updated, someone else changed it first; reload and retry, or report a conflict (HTTP 409 or 412). It fits rare conflicts and long think-time, such as editing a form.
explain.zh: 两个用户读了同一行又都写回时，可能丢失更新：后一次写入悄悄覆盖了前一次。悲观锁先加锁来防止：在事务里执行 SELECT ... FOR UPDATE，其他写者要等你提交。它简单可靠，适合冲突频繁、事务很短的场景，但锁会降低并发，还可能死锁。乐观锁不加锁：每行带版本号，写入是一次比较并设置：UPDATE ... SET ..., version = version + 1 WHERE id = ? AND version = ?。若没有行被更新，说明有人抢先改了，重新读取后重试，或报告冲突（HTTP 409 或 412）。它适合冲突少、思考时间长的场景，比如编辑表单。

example.en: Stock is 1 and two buyers click at once. Pessimistic: each runs SELECT stock FROM items WHERE id = 9 FOR UPDATE; the second waits, then sees 0 and gets 'sold out'. Optimistic: both read stock 1, version 5. The first runs UPDATE items SET stock = 0, version = 6 WHERE id = 9 AND version = 5 and succeeds; the second's identical UPDATE matches 0 rows, so it reloads, sees stock 0 and reports 'sold out'.
example.zh: 库存为 1，两位买家同时点击。悲观锁：各自执行 SELECT … FOR UPDATE；第二个等待后看到 0，提示“已售罄”。乐观锁：两人都读到 stock 1、version 5。第一个执行 UPDATE items SET stock = 0, version = 6 WHERE id = 9 AND version = 5，成功；第二个同样的 UPDATE 匹配 0 行，重读后看到库存为 0，提示“已售罄”。

image.en: On the left a giant padlock stands locked; its owner holds up the only key while the next customer waits, stopwatch in hand. On the right an open treasure chest has no lock at all, only a block stamped 'v5' on its rim. Two customers reached for it at once: one cheers because the stamp still read v5 when he wrote, the other shrugs and goes back to read the chest again.
image.zh: 左边立着一把锁住的巨型挂锁，锁的主人举着唯一的钥匙，下一位顾客只能拿着秒表干等。右边是一只敞开的宝箱，根本没上锁，只在箱沿放了一块印着“v5”的木块。两位顾客同时伸手：一个欢呼，因为他写入时木块上仍是 v5；另一个耸耸肩，回去重新看一遍宝箱。

means.en: pessimistic: SELECT … FOR UPDATE locks first
means.zh: 悲观锁：SELECT … FOR UPDATE 先上锁

means.en: others block until commit; deadlocks are possible
means.zh: 别人阻塞到提交为止，可能死锁

thing.en: the 'v5' block on the open chest
thing.zh: 敞开宝箱上的 v5 木块

means.en: optimistic: a version column checked at write time
means.zh: 乐观锁：写入时检查版本列

means.en: 0 rows updated: reload and retry, or return 409
means.zh: 更新了 0 行：重读重试，或返回 409

summary.en: Spreading data across machines: copies for safety and reads, partitions for size, and the trade-offs of non-relational stores.
summary.zh: 把数据分布到多台机器：副本带来安全和读能力，分区解决容量，以及非关系型存储的取舍。

summary.en: A leader takes the writes and streams them to followers, which serve reads and can take over, at the price of replication lag.
summary.zh: 主节点接收写入并把变更流式发给从节点，从节点分担读请求并可接管，代价是复制延迟。

explain.en: In leader–follower (primary–replica) replication all writes go to the leader, which records them in its log and ships the log to followers that apply the same changes in order. Followers serve reads, which scales read-heavy workloads, and hold copies for failover. With asynchronous replication the leader confirms a write before followers have it, so a follower can lag by milliseconds or, under load, minutes: users may not see their own updates, and if the leader dies, writes not yet replicated can be lost. Synchronous replication waits for at least one follower, trading latency for safety. Failover promotes a follower, ideally the most up to date, and must prevent two leaders (split brain), usually with consensus or fencing.
explain.zh: 主从复制中，所有写入都发往主节点（leader），主节点把它们记进日志，再把日志发给从节点（follower），从节点按相同顺序应用这些变更。从节点分担读请求，适合读多写少的负载，同时保存副本以便故障切换。异步复制时，主节点在从节点收到之前就确认写入，从节点可能落后几毫秒，高负载时甚至几分钟：用户可能看不到自己刚写的数据；主节点宕机时，尚未复制的写入可能丢失。同步复制至少等一个从节点确认，用延迟换安全。故障切换会提升一个从节点（最好是数据最新的），并必须防止出现两个主节点（脑裂），通常借助共识算法或隔离（fencing）。

example.en: A user changes her display name at 12:00:00; the write goes to the leader. Her profile page reads from a replica that is 2 seconds behind and still shows the old name. Fixes: read from the leader for a few seconds after a user's own write, or send her reads only to a replica whose replayed log position has passed the position of her write.
example.zh: 用户在 12:00:00 修改昵称，写入发往主节点。她的主页从一个落后 2 秒的副本读取，仍显示旧昵称。解决办法：用户自己写入后的几秒内从主节点读；或者只把她的读请求发给日志回放位置已超过那次写入的副本。

image.en: The lighthouse at the end of the pier is the leader: a sailor hands every new letter to it. Carrier pigeons fly copies out to the boats in the harbour. The sailboat already has today's copy, but the pigeon bound for the rowboat is still in mid-air, so the fisherman who asks the rowboat for news gets yesterday's and shrugs.
image.zh: 码头尽头的灯塔是主节点：水手把每封新信都交给它。信鸽把副本送到港里的船上。帆船已经收到今天的副本，飞往小划艇的信鸽却还在半空，于是向划艇打听消息的渔夫只拿到昨天的，只好耸耸肩。

means.en: the leader: all writes go here
means.zh: 主节点：所有写入都发到这里

means.en: followers serve reads and can take over on failover
means.zh: 从节点分担读，并可故障接管

means.en: asynchronous replication lag
means.zh: 异步复制的延迟

means.en: a stale read: read-your-writes can fail
means.zh: 陈旧读：读己之写可能失效

summary.en: Split one big dataset across machines by a partition key, by range or by hash, and watch for hot spots and cross-shard queries.
summary.zh: 按分区键把大数据集拆到多台机器上，可按范围或哈希划分，要提防热点和跨分片查询。

explain.en: When data or write traffic outgrows one machine, partition it: each row goes to one shard according to its partition key. Range partitioning gives each shard a key range (A–F, G–M …): range scans stay on one shard, but sequential keys such as timestamps send all new writes to the last shard. Hash partitioning uses hash(key) mod N or ranges of hash values: load spreads evenly, but range queries must ask every shard, and plain mod N moves most keys when N changes (consistent hashing fixes that). One celebrity key can still overload its shard. Queries without the partition key fan out to all shards, and cross-shard joins or transactions are slow or unsupported, so pick the key from the main access pattern, such as tenant_id.
explain.zh: 当数据量或写入流量超出一台机器的能力时，就要分区：每一行按分区键落到某个分片。范围分区给每个分片一段键区间（A–F、G–M……）：范围扫描只涉及一个分片，但时间戳这类递增键会让新写入全部涌向最后一个分片。哈希分区用 hash(key) mod N 或哈希值区间：负载均匀，但范围查询要问遍所有分片，而且简单取模在 N 变化时会搬动大部分键（一致性哈希解决这个问题）。单个明星键仍可能压垮它所在的分片。不带分区键的查询要广播到所有分片，跨分片的连接或事务要么很慢要么不支持，所以要按主要访问模式选分区键，例如 tenant_id。

example.en: A chat app stores 4 billion messages on 8 shards keyed by hash(conversation_id), so opening a conversation touches one shard. Searching all messages sent by one user, a different key, must query all 8 shards and merge the results. Had they used range partitioning on sent_at, every new message would land on the newest shard while the other 7 sat idle.
example.zh: 一个聊天应用把 40 亿条消息按 hash(conversation_id) 存到 8 个分片，打开一个会话只访问一个分片。查找某个用户发的全部消息用的是另一个键，必须查询全部 8 个分片再合并结果。要是按 sent_at 做范围分区，每条新消息都会落到最新的分片上，其余 7 个分片闲着。

image.en: Three small warehouses stand on the quay, one per shard. A sorter with a scroll reads each crate's label and points it to the warehouse its key belongs to. Crates pile up two layers high in front of the right-hand warehouse, a hot spot, while the left one has a single crate. The harbourmaster has to shout through a megaphone to all three warehouses to find one customer's crates.
image.zh: 码头上立着三座小仓库，每座是一个分片。拿着卷轴的分拣员看一眼木箱上的标签，就把它指派到键所属的仓库。右边仓库门口的木箱堆了两层，成了热点，左边却只有一只。港务长要找某位客户的箱子，只能举着扩音器朝三座仓库挨个喊。

means.en: shards: each holds part of the data
means.zh: 分片：每片只存一部分数据

means.en: the partition key decides the shard, by range or by hash
means.zh: 分区键决定分片，按范围或按哈希

means.en: a hot spot: skewed keys overload one shard
means.zh: 热点：倾斜的键压垮一个分片

means.en: a query without the key fans out to every shard
means.zh: 不带分区键的查询要问遍所有分片

summary.en: Place keys and nodes on one hash ring; each key belongs to the next node along it, so a node joining or leaving moves only nearby keys.
summary.zh: 把键和节点放在同一个哈希环上，每个键归环上的下一个节点，增删节点只搬动相邻的键。

explain.en: With hash(key) mod N, changing N from 4 to 5 remaps about 80% of the keys, a mass migration. Consistent hashing (Karger et al., 1997) maps both keys and nodes onto the same circular hash space, and each key is owned by the first node clockwise from it. When a node joins, it takes over only the keys between its predecessor and itself; when a node leaves, only its keys move to its successor. On average about K/N of K keys move. With few nodes the arcs are uneven, so each physical node is placed at many points as virtual nodes (often 100 or more), which evens out the load and lets a bigger machine take more of them. Dynamo, Cassandra and many caches and load balancers use it.
explain.zh: 用 hash(key) mod N 时，N 从 4 变成 5 会让约 80% 的键换位置，等于一次大迁移。一致性哈希（Karger 等，1997）把键和节点映射到同一个环形哈希空间，每个键归它顺时针方向遇到的第一个节点。新节点加入时，只接管它与前驱之间的键；节点离开时，只有它的键移交给后继。平均只需搬动 K 个键中的约 K/N 个。节点少时各段弧长不均，因此每台物理节点会在环上放很多个点，即虚拟节点（常见 100 个以上），既能均衡负载，也能让配置高的机器多领几个。Dynamo、Cassandra 以及许多缓存和负载均衡器都用它。

example.en: A cache cluster has 4 nodes and 1,000,000 keys, about 250,000 per node. Adding a fifth node moves only the keys on the arcs it takes over, about 200,000 in total if it gets an even share, while mod-N hashing would move about 800,000. With 200 virtual nodes per server the arcs average out, and each server's share stays close to the mean.
example.zh: 缓存集群有 4 个节点、100 万个键，每个节点约 25 万个。加入第 5 个节点，只搬它接管的那几段弧上的键，若它分到均等份额，共约 20 万个；取模哈希则要搬约 80 万个。每台服务器配 200 个虚拟节点后，弧长相互抵消，每台的负载都接近平均值。

image.en: Four rowboats float in a circle, and eight yellow ducks paddle on a smaller ring between them; each duck belongs to the next boat along the ring. A sailor pushes a fifth, orange boat into one gap. Only the ducks in that stretch of water will now swim to the orange boat; every other duck stays exactly where it is.
image.zh: 四条小划艇围成一圈，八只黄鸭在它们之间的小圈上划水；每只鸭子都归环上的下一条船。一名水手把第五条橙色小船推进一个空档。只有那一段水面上的鸭子会游向橙色小船，其余的鸭子原地不动。

means.en: nodes placed on the hash ring
means.zh: 放在哈希环上的节点

means.en: keys hashed onto the same ring; each goes to the next node
means.zh: 哈希到同一环上的键，各归下一个节点

means.en: a joining node takes only the keys just before it
means.zh: 新加入的节点只接管它前面那一段键

means.en: about K/N keys move, not nearly all as with mod N
means.zh: 只搬约 K/N 个键，而非取模时的几乎全部

summary.en: Key-value, document, wide-column and graph stores trade joins, ad-hoc queries and multi-row transactions for scale, speed or flexible schemas.
summary.zh: 键值、文档、宽列和图数据库，用连接、即席查询和多行事务，换取扩展性、速度或灵活的模式。

explain.en: 'NoSQL' covers several data models. Key-value stores (Redis, DynamoDB) get and put by key: very fast and easy to partition. Document stores (MongoDB) keep nested JSON-like documents, so data read together is stored together and fields can vary between documents. Wide-column stores (Cassandra, Bigtable, HBase) hold huge, write-heavy tables partitioned by row key and queried along planned access paths. Graph databases (Neo4j) store nodes and relationships and make multi-hop traversals cheap. The usual price: few or no joins, limited ad-hoc queries, transactions scoped to one key or document, and schema rules moved into application code. The lines blur: MongoDB has multi-document transactions, PostgreSQL has JSONB. Choose by access pattern, not fashion.
explain.zh: NoSQL 涵盖好几种数据模型。键值存储（Redis、DynamoDB）按键读写值，极快且易于分区。文档存储（MongoDB）保存嵌套的类 JSON 文档，一起读的数据存在一起，不同文档的字段可以不同。宽列存储（Cassandra、Bigtable、HBase）承载按行键分区、写入密集的超大表，按事先设计的访问路径查询。图数据库（Neo4j）存储节点和关系，多跳遍历代价很低。常见代价是：连接很少或没有，即席查询受限，事务只覆盖单个键或文档，模式约束挪进了应用代码。界限也在模糊：MongoDB 支持多文档事务，PostgreSQL 能存 JSONB。要按访问模式来选，而不是赶时髦。

example.en: A product catalogue where a shirt has sizes and a laptop has RAM fits documents: one read returns the whole product. A session cache doing 50,000 reads per second fits a key-value store. 'Friends of friends who like jazz' is a two-hop graph query. Moving money between accounts needs multi-row transactions and constraints, so it usually stays in a relational database.
example.zh: 商品目录里衬衫有尺码、笔记本电脑有内存，适合文档存储：一次读取拿到整个商品。每秒 5 万次读取的会话缓存适合键值存储。“喜欢爵士乐的朋友的朋友”是一次两跳的图查询。账户间转账需要多行事务和约束，所以通常仍放在关系数据库里。

image.en: On the quay a sailor sorts cargo into three kinds of container: tagged barrels that open only by their tag, a tower of parcels that each pack a whole order inside, and a fishing net whose knots and ropes hold everything by its connections. A cat sniffs at the barrels. Each container is quick for one kind of question and clumsy for the others.
image.zh: 码头上，一名水手把货物分进三种容器：只能凭标签打开的木桶；一座包裹塔，每个包裹都装着一整份订单；还有一张靠绳结和绳索把一切连在一起的渔网。一只猫凑过去闻木桶。每种容器只擅长回答一类问题，换一类就很笨拙。

means.en: key-value: very fast get and put by key
means.zh: 键值：按键读写，极快

means.en: document: what is read together is stored together
means.zh: 文档：一起读的数据存在一起

means.en: graph: relationships first, cheap multi-hop traversal
means.zh: 图：关系优先，多跳遍历便宜

thing.en: each container good at one question
thing.zh: 每种容器只擅长一类问题

means.en: choose by access pattern; joins and transactions get weaker
means.zh: 按访问模式选择；连接和事务变弱

summary.en: How a backend is split into layers and services, how the parts talk, how caches and queues take the load, and how the whole stays up when parts fail.
summary.zh: 后端如何分层、拆服务，各部分怎样通信，缓存和队列如何分担压力，部件出故障时整体又如何保持可用。

summary.en: How code is divided into layers and services, how services call each other, and how traffic is spread across them.
summary.zh: 代码如何分层、拆成服务，服务之间怎样调用，流量又如何分摊。

summary.en: Split a service into controller, service and repository layers; each layer calls only the layer below it.
summary.zh: 把一个服务分成控制器层、服务层和仓储层，每层只调用紧挨着的下一层。

explain.en: A layered backend separates concerns. The controller layer speaks HTTP: it parses and validates requests and turns results into responses. The service layer holds the business rules and sets transaction boundaries. The repository layer hides the database behind methods such as findById and save. Calls flow downward one layer at a time: a controller never runs SQL, and a repository never calls a controller. Clean and hexagonal architecture add dependency inversion: the service layer defines the repository interface and the database code implements it, so source-code dependencies point inward, toward the business logic. The rules can then be tested without HTTP or a database, and the storage can change without touching them.
explain.zh: 分层架构按职责切分后端。控制器层（controller）负责 HTTP：解析、校验请求，把结果转成响应。服务层（service）承载业务规则，并划定事务边界。仓储层（repository）把数据库藏在 findById、save 这类方法后面。调用自上而下、逐层进行：控制器从不直接写 SQL，仓储也从不反过来调用控制器。整洁架构和六边形架构再加上依赖倒置：仓储接口由服务层定义、由数据库代码实现，于是源码依赖都指向内侧的业务逻辑。这样，业务规则可以脱离 HTTP 和数据库单独测试，更换存储也不必改动它们。

example.en: POST /orders: OrderController validates the JSON body and calls orderService.place(command). The service checks stock, computes the total and opens a transaction, then calls orderRepository.save(order), which runs the INSERT. In a unit test the service gets an in-memory repository instead, so no database is needed.
example.zh: POST /orders：OrderController 校验 JSON 请求体，调用 orderService.place(command)；服务层检查库存、计算总价、开启事务，再调用 orderRepository.save(order) 执行 INSERT。单元测试时给服务层换上内存版仓储，就不需要数据库。

image.en: A market stall runs like a bucket brigade. A girl gives her order to the cashier in red; he passes it on to the merchant in a beret, who reads his rule book; the merchant sends the porter in a hard hat to the crates at the end of the line. The arrows on the cobbles all point one way, and the girl never gets near the crates.
image.zh: 集市摊位上，订单像救火时的水桶一样一手传一手。小女孩把订单交给穿红衣的收银员；收银员转交给戴贝雷帽、正翻规则手册的老板；老板再派戴安全帽的搬运工去队尾搬货箱。石板路上的箭头全朝一个方向，小女孩根本碰不到货箱。

means.en: controller: speaks HTTP with the client
means.zh: 控制器：与客户端讲 HTTP

thing.en: the merchant with the rule book

means.en: service layer: the business rules
means.zh: 服务层：业务规则

means.en: repository and database: data access
means.zh: 仓储与数据库：数据访问

means.en: calls go down one layer at a time, never skipping or going up
means.zh: 调用逐层向下，不跳层，不回调

summary.en: Ship everything as one deployable unit, or as many small services that deploy independently but talk over the network.
summary.zh: 整体部署为一个单元，还是拆成许多可独立部署、靠网络通信的小服务。

explain.en: A monolith ships all features as one deployable unit. Calls between modules are fast in-process function calls, one database transaction can span features, and debugging is simple. Microservices split the system by business capability into services that own their data and deploy independently, so teams release on their own schedule and scale hot parts separately. The price is distributed complexity: network latency and partial failure, consistency without shared transactions, versioned APIs, and heavier monitoring and operations. A common recommendation is to start with a modular monolith, one deployable with strict module boundaries inside, and to extract a service only when team size or scaling needs justify it.
explain.zh: 单体（monolith）把所有功能打包成一个可部署单元：模块之间是进程内的函数调用，又快又可靠；一个数据库事务就能跨多个功能；排查问题也简单。微服务按业务能力拆分系统，每个服务拥有自己的数据、独立部署，团队可以按自己的节奏发布，热点部分也能单独扩容。代价是分布式的复杂性：网络延迟和部分失败、没有共享事务时的数据一致性、API 版本管理，以及更重的监控与运维。常见建议是从模块化单体起步：只有一个部署单元，但内部模块边界严格；等团队规模或扩展需求确实需要时，再拆出服务。

example.en: A shop with 8 engineers runs one Django app whose catalog, orders and payments modules talk only through clear interfaces. Years later, with 60 engineers and Black Friday spikes at checkout, payments is extracted into its own service with its own database; orders now calls it over HTTP, with a timeout and retries.
example.zh: 一家有 8 名工程师的网店只跑一个 Django 应用，商品、订单、支付模块之间只通过清晰的接口交互。几年后团队扩到 60 人，黑五时结账流量暴涨，于是把支付拆成独立服务、配独立数据库；订单模块改为通过 HTTP 调用它，并设置超时和重试。

image.en: On the left of the market square stands a whole castle: every shop lives behind its one gate. On the right, four little tents each fly their own flag. A courier dashes toward the tents with a letter; another has tripped and lies flat on the cobbles, his letter dropped nearby.
image.zh: 集市广场左边矗立着一整座城堡：所有店铺都在它唯一的城门后面。右边是四顶小帐篷，各插一面自己的旗。一个信使举着信奔向帐篷；另一个绊倒在石板路上，摔得四仰八叉，信掉在一旁。

means.en: monolith: one unit, deployed as a whole
means.zh: 单体：一个整体，一起部署

means.en: modules inside a modular monolith
means.zh: 模块化单体内部的模块

means.en: microservices: each owned by one team and deployed alone
means.zh: 微服务：各归一个团队，独立部署

means.en: network calls between services

summary.en: A synchronous call makes the caller wait for the answer; an asynchronous message lets it carry on and handle the result later.
summary.zh: 同步调用让调用方等着拿结果；异步消息让它发完就继续，结果稍后再处理。

explain.en: In synchronous communication (REST, gRPC) the caller sends a request and blocks until a response or a timeout arrives. It is simple and gives an immediate answer, but it couples services in time: both must be up at the same moment, and along a call chain latencies add up while availabilities multiply. In asynchronous communication the caller publishes a message or event to a broker and moves on; consumers process it when they can. This removes temporal coupling and absorbs bursts, but the result comes later, data becomes eventually consistent, and you need idempotent consumers, clear ordering rules and good tracing. Rule of thumb: call synchronously when the user needs the answer now; send a message for work that can finish later.
explain.zh: 同步通信（REST、gRPC）中，调用方发出请求后就阻塞，直到收到响应或超时。它简单直接，马上有结果，但让服务在时间上耦合：双方必须同时在线；沿着调用链，延迟层层相加，可用性层层相乘。异步通信中，调用方把消息或事件交给消息代理（broker）就去忙别的，消费者有空再处理。这消除了时间耦合，也能削峰，但结果要晚些才到，数据变成最终一致，还需要幂等的消费者、明确的顺序规则和完善的链路追踪。经验法则：用户当场要答案就同步调用，可以稍后完成的工作就发消息。

example.en: Checkout calls Payments, which calls Fraud, all synchronously. If each service is 99.9% available and adds about 100 ms, the whole request is about 99.7% available (0.999³) and takes about 300 ms. The confirmation email is different: checkout publishes OrderPlaced and returns at once, and the email service consumes the event a few seconds later.
example.zh: 结账同步调用支付，支付再同步调用风控。若每个服务可用性 99.9%、各耗时约 100 ms，整个请求的可用性约为 99.7%（0.999³），耗时约 300 ms。确认邮件则不同：结账服务发布 OrderPlaced 事件后立即返回，邮件服务几秒后再消费它。

image.en: On the left, a merchant in a top hat is chained to his supplier by a heavy iron chain. He stands with a stopwatch in hand and can do nothing until the supplier, lost in thought, gives him an answer. On the right, a woman has just dropped a letter into a red post box and strolls off with an apple, already on to her next errand.
image.zh: 左边，戴高礼帽的商人被一条粗铁链和供货商拴在一起。他攥着秒表，在苦思冥想的供货商给出答复之前，什么也干不了。右边，一位女士刚把信投进红色邮筒，拿着苹果悠然走开，已经去办下一件事了。

means.en: temporal coupling: both sides must be up at once
means.zh: 时间耦合：双方必须同时在线

means.en: a synchronous caller, blocked until a reply or a timeout
means.zh: 同步调用方：阻塞到响应或超时

means.en: a message broker or queue
means.zh: 消息代理或队列

means.en: an asynchronous sender carries on without waiting
means.zh: 异步发送方不等待，继续干活

summary.en: Spread requests over a pool of identical servers and skip unhealthy ones, so capacity grows by adding machines.
summary.zh: 把请求分给一组相同的服务器并跳过不健康的，加机器就能扩容。

explain.en: A load balancer sits in front of a pool of identical, ideally stateless instances and picks one for each connection or request. Round robin takes them in turn; weighted round robin gives bigger machines more; least connections picks the instance with the fewest active requests, which helps when request costs vary; hashing a client IP or user id keeps a client on one instance. A layer-4 balancer forwards TCP connections by address and port without reading them; a layer-7 balancer understands HTTP, so it can route by path or header, terminate TLS and retry. Health checks probe each instance and take failing ones out of rotation. Scaling horizontally then means adding instances behind the balancer, which must itself be redundant.
explain.zh: 负载均衡器挡在一组相同、最好无状态的实例前面，为每个连接或请求挑一台。轮询（round robin）依次分配；加权轮询让大机器多分；最少连接（least connections）挑当前活跃请求最少的实例，适合请求耗时差别大的场景；按客户端 IP 或用户 ID 做哈希，能让同一客户端固定落到同一实例。四层（L4）均衡只按地址和端口转发 TCP 连接，不看内容；七层（L7）懂 HTTP，能按路径或请求头路由、终止 TLS、重试。健康检查定期探测各实例，把失败的移出轮转。水平扩展就是在均衡器后面加实例，而均衡器自身也要有冗余。

example.en: An L7 balancer spreads requests over three instances by round robin: requests 1 to 6 go to A, B, C, A, B, C. Instance C fails its /health check twice in a row and is removed, so request 7 goes to A, 8 to B and 9 to A. During a sale two new instances start and join the rotation as soon as their health checks pass.
example.zh: L7 负载均衡器用轮询把请求分给三台实例：请求 1 到 6 依次落到 A、B、C、A、B、C。C 连续两次 /health 检查失败被摘除，于是请求 7 去 A、8 去 B、9 又去 A。大促时新启动两台实例，健康检查一通过就加入轮转。

image.en: A line of ducks waddles up to a market warden in a teal coat. He points each duck to the next of three identical juice machines: one, two, three, one, two, three. The bulb on top of the third machine has gone dark, so he skips it and sends the next duck to the first machine instead.
image.zh: 一队鸭子摇摇摆摆走到穿青绿外套的集市管理员面前。他把每只鸭子依次指向三台一模一样的果汁售货机：一、二、三，一、二、三。第三台机器顶上的灯泡灭了，他就跳过它，把下一只鸭子派给第一台。

means.en: a pool of identical, stateless instances
means.zh: 一组相同、无状态的实例

means.en: the load balancer using round robin
means.zh: 使用轮询的负载均衡器

means.en: incoming requests
means.zh: 不断进来的请求

means.en: a failed health check: out of rotation
means.zh: 健康检查失败：移出轮转

summary.en: Keep hot data close at hand, and pass work along through queues so nobody has to wait.
summary.zh: 把热数据放在手边，用队列把活儿传下去，谁也不必干等。

summary.en: Read the cache first and fill it from the database on a miss; on a write, update the database, then delete the cached copy.
summary.zh: 先读缓存，未命中再查库并回填；写入时先更新数据库，再删除缓存。

explain.en: In cache-aside, also called lazy loading, the application manages the cache itself. On a read it looks up the key in the cache, such as Redis; a hit returns at once, and a miss reads the database, stores the result with a time-to-live (TTL) and returns it. On a write it updates the database first and then deletes the cache entry, so the next read loads a fresh copy. Deleting is safer than updating the cached value, because two concurrent writers may update the cache in the opposite order to the database. Stale reads remain possible: between the update and the delete, and when a slow reader that loaded the old row puts it back after the delete. The TTL caps how long such stale data survives.
explain.zh: 旁路缓存（cache-aside，又称懒加载）由应用自己管理缓存。读：先按 key 查缓存（如 Redis），命中立即返回；未命中就查数据库，把结果带上过期时间（TTL）写进缓存再返回。写：先更新数据库，再删除缓存条目，下次读时自然加载新值。删除比直接更新缓存更稳妥，因为两个并发写者更新缓存的先后可能与写库顺序相反。旧数据仍可能被读到：一是更新库与删缓存之间；二是某个慢读者先读到旧行，等删除完成后又把旧值写回缓存。TTL 限定了这类旧数据最多能活多久。

example.en: GET /products/42: Redis has no product:42, so the service runs SELECT … WHERE id = 42 (8 ms), stores the row with SET product:42 … EX 300 and returns it. The next 1,000 reads within five minutes come from Redis in about 0.5 ms each. When the price changes, the service updates the row and then runs DEL product:42.
example.zh: GET /products/42：Redis 里没有 product:42，服务执行 SELECT … WHERE id = 42（8 ms），用 SET product:42 … EX 300 写入缓存后返回。之后五分钟内的 1000 次读取都由 Redis 返回，每次约 0.5 ms。价格变动时，服务先更新这行数据，再执行 DEL product:42。

image.en: A glass spice jar as tall as a child stands in the middle of the kitchen, and it is empty. The chef points at it, so a kitchen boy runs back from the big barrel with a bottle to refill it. An alarm clock beside the jar will ring when the spice goes stale. In the bin sits an old jar, thrown out the moment the recipe in the barrel changed.
image.zh: 厨房中央立着一只和孩子一样高的玻璃调料罐，里面空了。厨师指着它，小帮厨便从大木桶那儿拎着一瓶调料跑回来续满。罐子旁的闹钟会在调料变味时响起。垃圾桶里躺着一只旧罐子：木桶里的配方一改，它就被扔掉了。

means.en: the cache: small, fast, close at hand
means.zh: 缓存：小、快、就在手边

means.en: the database: the source of truth
means.zh: 数据库：权威数据来源

thing.en: the boy refilling from the barrel
thing.zh: 从木桶取货续满的帮厨

means.en: a miss: read the database, then fill the cache
means.zh: 未命中：查库，再回填缓存

means.en: the TTL, which caps how long data can be stale
means.zh: TTL：限定数据最多旧多久

thing.en: the old jar in the bin

means.en: on a write, delete the cache entry
means.zh: 写入后删除缓存条目

summary.en: Three ways traffic slips past a cache to the database: keys that never exist, one hot key expiring, and many keys expiring together.
summary.zh: 三种让流量绕过缓存压到数据库的情形：查不存在的 key、热点 key 过期、大量 key 同时过期。

explain.en: Penetration: requests for keys that exist in neither the cache nor the database, from bugs or attackers, miss every time and hit the database. Fix: cache the empty result with a short TTL, or first check a Bloom filter of valid keys; it never rejects a real key, so its 'no' is certain. Breakdown, also called a cache stampede: one very hot key expires and thousands of concurrent misses rebuild it at once. Fix: let one request rebuild it behind a mutex or single-flight while others wait or get the old value, or refresh hot keys before they expire. Avalanche: many keys expire together, or the cache cluster fails, and the whole load lands on the database. Fix: add random jitter to TTLs, replicate the cache, and rate-limit or degrade under overload.
explain.zh: 缓存穿透：请求的 key 在缓存和数据库里都不存在（程序缺陷或恶意攻击），每次都未命中，直接打到数据库。对策：把空结果也缓存起来并设较短 TTL，或先查一个有效 key 的布隆过滤器（Bloom filter）：它绝不会把真实存在的 key 判为不存在，所以它说“没有”就一定没有。缓存击穿：某个极热的 key 过期，成千上万的并发请求同时去重建它。对策：用互斥锁或 single-flight 只放一个请求去重建，其余等待或先拿旧值；或在过期前提前刷新。缓存雪崩：大量 key 同时过期，或缓存集群宕机，全部流量压向数据库。对策：给 TTL 加随机抖动、缓存做高可用，过载时限流或降级。

example.en: Before a flash sale, 100,000 product pages are cached at 9:00 with a TTL of 3,600 s, so all of them expire at 10:00. With TTL = 3,600 + random(0, 600) s the expiries spread over ten minutes. Meanwhile a bot requests /products/-1 a million times; caching 'not found' for 60 s means the database sees that query about once a minute.
example.zh: 大促前，10 万个商品页在 9:00 一起写入缓存，TTL 都是 3600 秒，于是会在 10:00 同时过期；改成 3600 + random(0, 600) 秒后，过期时间分散到十分钟里。另有爬虫把 /products/-1 请求了一百万次；把“不存在”缓存 60 秒后，数据库大约每分钟才收到一次这个查询。

image.en: The house special has just sold out, and a hungry crowd stampedes toward the pantry door. A cook stands by the padlocked door holding its only key: one person in at a time. A pale ghost hovers nearby, ordering a dish that has never existed, and four alarm clocks on the floor all ring at the same moment.
image.zh: 招牌菜刚卖完，饥饿的人群就冲向储藏室的门。厨师守在挂着大锁的门旁，手握唯一的钥匙：一次只放一个人进去。一个苍白的幽灵飘在旁边，点一道从来不存在的菜；地上四只闹钟同时响了起来。

means.en: penetration: a key in neither cache nor database
means.zh: 穿透：缓存和库里都没有的 key

means.en: breakdown: a hot key expires and everyone rebuilds it
means.zh: 击穿：热点 key 过期，大家同时重建

thing.en: the cook with the only key

means.en: a mutex or single-flight: one request rebuilds
means.zh: 互斥锁或 single-flight：只放一个请求重建

means.en: avalanche: many TTLs expire together, so add jitter
means.zh: 雪崩：大量 TTL 同时到期，要加随机抖动

summary.en: Producers put messages on a queue and consumers take them off at their own pace, which decouples the two sides and absorbs bursts.
summary.zh: 生产者把消息放进队列，消费者按自己的节奏取走：两边解耦，还能削峰填谷。

explain.en: A message queue or log, such as RabbitMQ, Amazon SQS or Kafka, stores messages between producers and consumers. Producers need not know who consumes or wait for them; consumers can be slow, restarted or scaled out, and a burst just lengthens the backlog for a while instead of overloading downstream services. Kafka splits a topic into partitions and keeps order only within a partition, so messages that must stay in order share a key and land in the same partition. The members of one consumer group divide the partitions, one reader per partition, so parallelism is capped by the partition count; separate groups each get every message. If a consumer commits its offset only after processing, a crash means redelivery rather than loss.
explain.zh: 消息队列或日志（如 RabbitMQ、Amazon SQS、Kafka）把消息暂存在生产者和消费者之间。生产者不必知道谁来消费，也不用等；消费者可以慢、可以重启、可以扩容，流量突增时只是积压暂时变长，不会压垮下游。Kafka 把主题（topic）分成多个分区（partition），只保证分区内有序，所以需要保序的消息用同一个 key，落到同一分区。同一消费者组（consumer group）的成员瓜分分区，每个分区只有一个读者，所以并行度受分区数限制；不同的组则各自收到全部消息。消费者处理完再提交位移（offset），崩溃时就只会重投、不会丢消息。

example.en: At 20:00 a sale produces 5,000 order events per second, but the email service handles 1,000 per second. The topic absorbs the burst: after one minute the backlog is 240,000 messages, and it drains once traffic falls. With 12 partitions keyed by order id, up to 12 email workers can share the load, and each order's events stay in order.
example.zh: 20:00 大促，每秒产生 5000 条订单事件，邮件服务每秒只能处理 1000 条。主题扛住了峰值：一分钟后积压 24 万条，流量回落后再慢慢消化。主题按订单 ID 分成 12 个分区，最多 12 个邮件消费者可以分担负载，而同一订单的事件仍然有序。

image.en: A waiter loads order tickets onto two conveyor belts faster than anyone could cook, and a tall pile of tickets still waits beside him. Each belt carries its tickets to its own cook at the far end, who takes them one at a time at a steady pace. Nobody shouts, and nobody waits for anybody.
image.zh: 服务员往两条传送带上放点菜单，快得没人做得完，他身边还堆着高高一摞单子。每条传送带把单子送到尽头属于自己的那位厨师面前，厨师按稳定的节奏一张张取。没人吆喝，也没人等谁。

means.en: the producer
means.zh: 生产者

means.en: a topic with two partitions, each kept in order
means.zh: 有两个分区的主题，分区内有序

means.en: a consumer group: one consumer per partition
means.zh: 消费者组：每个分区一个消费者

means.en: a burst absorbed as backlog
means.zh: 被积压吸收的流量高峰

summary.en: Networks force a choice between losing messages and duplicating them; idempotent consumers make duplicates harmless.
summary.zh: 网络迫使你在丢消息和重复消息之间二选一；幂等的消费者让重复变得无害。

explain.en: A sender that gets no acknowledgement cannot tell whether the message or the ack was lost. If it never resends, delivery is at most once and messages can be lost; if it resends until acknowledged, delivery is at least once and messages can arrive twice. Exactly-once delivery cannot be guaranteed over such a network; what products such as Kafka call exactly once is exactly-once processing: at-least-once delivery plus deduplication or atomic commits. An operation is idempotent if doing it twice has the same effect as doing it once: 'set status to PAID' is, 'add $10' is not. Consumers become idempotent by recording processed message ids in the same transaction as the effect; APIs do it by storing each client-sent idempotency key with its response.
explain.zh: 发送方收不到确认时，分不清丢的是消息还是确认。从不重发，就是“至多一次”（at-most-once），可能丢消息；重发到收到确认为止，就是“至少一次”（at-least-once），可能重复。在这样的网络上无法保证“恰好一次”投递；Kafka 事务等产品所说的 exactly-once，其实是“恰好一次”的处理效果：至少一次投递，加上去重或原子提交。幂等指做两次和做一次效果相同：“把状态设为已支付”是幂等的，“余额加 10 元”不是。让消费者幂等的办法：在与业务写入相同的事务里记录已处理的消息 ID；或由客户端发送幂等键（idempotency key），服务端连同响应一起保存。

example.en: A client sends POST /payments with the header Idempotency-Key: 7f3a…, and the response is lost on the way back. The client retries with the same key. The server finds 7f3a… among its processed keys and returns the stored 201 response instead of charging the card again: two requests, one charge.
example.zh: 客户端发出 POST /payments，请求头带 Idempotency-Key: 7f3a…，响应却在回程中丢了。客户端用同一个键重试。服务端在已处理的键里查到 7f3a…，直接返回保存的 201 响应，而不会再扣一次款：两次请求，一次扣款。

image.en: A green parrot on a barrel squawks the same order twice: 'Forty-two! Forty-two!' The cook does not grab a second pan. She points at the open ledger on the counter, where ticket 42 is already ticked off, next to the one cake she has baked. The duplicate ticket has gone straight into the bin.
image.zh: 木桶上的绿鹦鹉把同一张单子喊了两遍：“四十二！四十二！”厨师没有再拿一口锅，而是指着柜台上摊开的账本：42 号早已打了勾，旁边就是她做好的那一个蛋糕。重复的单子直接进了垃圾桶。

means.en: at-least-once delivery: duplicates will happen
means.zh: 至少一次投递：一定会有重复

means.en: stored message ids or idempotency keys
means.zh: 记录已处理的消息 ID 或幂等键

means.en: the effect happens exactly once
means.zh: 效果只发生一次

means.en: the duplicate is detected and dropped
means.zh: 识别出重复并丢弃

summary.en: Choices and patterns that keep a distributed system correct and responsive when networks split and dependencies fail.
summary.zh: 网络分区、依赖出错时，让分布式系统保持正确、及时响应的取舍与模式。

title.zh: CAP 定理与一致性模型

summary.en: When a network partition splits replicas, a system must choose: refuse requests to stay consistent, or keep answering and risk stale data.
summary.zh: 网络分区把副本隔开时只能二选一：拒绝请求以保持一致，或继续应答但可能给出旧数据。

explain.en: The CAP theorem, Brewer's conjecture proved by Gilbert and Lynch in 2002, is about a replicated store when the network partitions. Consistency here means linearizability: every read sees the latest completed write, as if there were one copy. Availability means every request to a non-failed node gets a non-error response. Partitions cannot be ruled out, so the real choice is made during one: a CP system refuses or blocks some requests, while an AP system keeps answering, lets replicas diverge and reconciles later. Below linearizability sit weaker models: eventual consistency (replicas converge once writes stop), causal consistency and read-your-writes. PACELC adds the normal case: else, trade latency against consistency. CAP's C is not the C in ACID.
explain.zh: CAP 定理（Brewer 的猜想，2002 年由 Gilbert 和 Lynch 证明）讨论网络分区时的多副本存储。这里的一致性（C）指线性一致：每次读都能看到最近完成的写，就像只有一份数据；可用性（A）指每个未故障节点收到的请求都必须得到非错误响应。分区（P）无法排除，所以真正的抉择发生在分区期间：CP 系统拒绝或阻塞部分请求，AP 系统继续应答、任副本暂时分叉、事后再合并。线性一致之下还有较弱的模型：最终一致（停止写入后副本终将收敛）、因果一致、读己之写。PACELC 补上了正常情况：没有分区时，要在延迟和一致性之间权衡。注意：CAP 的 C 不是 ACID 的 C。

example.en: Five replicas hold a stock count, three in data centre A and two in B, and the link between A and B fails. A CP store such as etcd keeps accepting writes in A, which has a majority (3 of 5); writes in B fail. An AP store such as Cassandra at consistency level ONE keeps taking orders in both, so both may sell the last item; when the link returns, replicas converge (last write wins) and the oversell must be handled.
example.zh: 5 个副本保存库存数：A 机房 3 个，B 机房 2 个，两地链路断开。CP 存储（如 etcd）只在拥有多数派（5 个中的 3 个）的 A 机房继续接受写入，B 机房的写入失败。AP 存储（如一致性级别为 ONE 的 Cassandra）两边都继续接单，最后一件商品可能被卖两次；链路恢复后副本按“最后写入者胜”收敛，超卖要由业务处理。

image.en: In the control room a giant pair of scissors has snipped the cable between two server racks. At the left rack an operator shrugs at every question: no answer until the racks can talk again. At the right rack an operator cheerfully hands out a scroll, the newest copy he has, which may already be out of date.
image.zh: 控制室里，一把巨大的剪刀剪断了两台机柜之间的线缆。左边机柜的操作员对每个问题都耸耸肩：两台机柜重新连上之前，概不回答。右边机柜的操作员却乐呵呵地递出一卷文书，那是他手头最新的版本，可能早已过时。

means.en: a network partition
means.zh: 网络分区

means.en: replicas of the same data
means.zh: 同一份数据的副本

means.en: CP: refuse rather than risk a stale answer
means.zh: CP：宁可拒绝，也不给可能过时的答案

thing.en: the operator handing out a scroll

means.en: AP: always answer, maybe with stale data
means.zh: AP：总是应答，但数据可能过时

glyph.zh: 分区时 C 或 A

summary.en: Two-phase commit makes services commit together but can block; a saga chains local transactions and undoes finished steps with compensations.
summary.zh: 两阶段提交让各方一起提交，但可能阻塞；Saga 串起本地事务，失败时用补偿撤销已完成的步骤。

explain.en: Two-phase commit (2PC) gives atomicity across databases: a coordinator asks every participant to prepare and vote, then tells all of them to commit or abort. It is blocking: a participant that voted yes holds its locks until it hears the decision, so a coordinator crash can stall everyone. Microservices usually prefer a saga: a sequence of local transactions, each paired with a compensating action that undoes it semantically, such as a refund. If step k fails, the compensations for steps k−1 to 1 run in reverse order. Sagas give up isolation, so others may see intermediate states. Steps are driven by messages; the transactional outbox writes each event to an outbox table in the same local transaction as the data change, and a relay publishes it.
explain.zh: 两阶段提交（2PC）实现跨数据库的原子性：协调者先请所有参与者“准备”并投票，再统一通知提交或回滚。它会阻塞：投了赞成票的参与者在收到决定前一直持有锁，协调者一崩溃，大家可能一起卡住。微服务通常改用 Saga：一串本地事务，每一步都配一个在业务上撤销它的补偿操作，比如退款。第 k 步失败，就按相反顺序执行第 k−1 步到第 1 步的补偿。Saga 放弃了隔离性，别人可能看到中间状态。各步骤由消息驱动；事务性发件箱（transactional outbox）在修改数据的同一个本地事务里把事件写进 outbox 表，再由中继进程发布出去。

example.en: A trip-booking saga: (1) reserve the flight, (2) book the hotel, (3) charge the card. The charge is declined. The orchestrator runs the compensations in reverse: cancel the hotel booking, then release the flight seat. Every step and compensation is idempotent, because a message may be delivered twice.
example.zh: 订行程的 Saga：(1) 预留机票，(2) 预订酒店，(3) 信用卡扣款。扣款被拒。编排器按相反顺序执行补偿：先取消酒店预订，再释放机票座位。每个步骤和补偿都是幂等的，因为消息可能被投递两次。

image.en: A robot travel agent has already reserved a little airplane and booked a small hotel, but lightning strikes the safe that was to take the payment. Two red arrows curl back, from the safe to the hotel and from the hotel to the plane, and the robot trudges back toward the plane, cancelling each booking in turn.
image.zh: 机器人旅行社已经订下一架小飞机、订好一家小旅馆，可负责收款的保险箱突然遭了雷击。两支红箭头往回弯：从保险箱指向旅馆，再从旅馆指向飞机。机器人朝飞机那边往回走，逐个取消预订。

thing.en: plane, hotel and safe in a row
thing.zh: 排成一行的飞机、旅馆、保险箱

means.en: the saga's local transactions, in order
means.zh: Saga 依次执行的本地事务

means.en: step 3 fails
means.zh: 第 3 步失败

means.en: compensations run in reverse order
means.zh: 按相反顺序执行补偿

means.en: the orchestrator that drives the saga
means.zh: 驱动 Saga 的编排器

summary.en: Bound every remote call with a timeout, retry only idempotent operations, and space retries out with exponential backoff and jitter.
summary.zh: 每个远程调用都设超时；只重试幂等操作；用带抖动的指数退避拉开重试间隔。

explain.en: A call without a timeout can hang forever, holding a thread, a connection and the user's request. Give every remote call a deadline shorter than the caller's own. Many failures are transient, so retrying helps, but only for idempotent operations or requests with an idempotency key, and only for retryable errors such as timeouts, 503 or 429, never 400. Wait between attempts with exponential backoff, base × 2ⁿ up to a cap, plus random jitter so that clients which failed together do not retry in lockstep. Cap the attempts and retry at one layer only: if three layers in a call chain each try 3 times, the bottom service can get 27 calls. Such retry storms keep an overloaded service from recovering; retry budgets and circuit breakers prevent them.
explain.zh: 没有超时的调用可能永远挂着，连带占住线程、连接和用户的请求。每个远程调用都要设截止时间，并且短于调用方自己的截止时间。很多故障是暂时的，重试有用，但只能重试幂等操作或带幂等键的请求，且只针对超时、503、429 这类可重试的错误，绝不重试 400。两次尝试之间用指数退避：等待 base × 2ⁿ，设上限，再加随机抖动，免得一起失败的客户端又一起重试。限制重试次数，并且只在一层重试：调用链上三层各试 3 次，最底层的服务可能收到 27 次调用。这种重试风暴会让过载的服务无法恢复，重试预算和熔断器可以防止它。

example.en: A client calls the inventory service with a 2 s timeout and at most 4 attempts. Between attempts it waits up to 100, 200 and 400 ms (base 100 ms, doubling), drawing each actual wait at random between zero and that bound, which is called full jitter. If all four attempts fail, it reports the error instead of waiting forever.
example.zh: 客户端调用库存服务，超时 2 秒，最多尝试 4 次。两次尝试之间的等待上限依次是 100、200、400 毫秒（基数 100 毫秒，逐次翻倍），实际等待取 0 到上限之间的随机值，这叫“全抖动”。四次都失败就上报错误，而不是无限等下去。

image.en: A messenger in a helmet, stopwatch in hand, keeps knocking at a silent server rack. Between him and the rack stand four hourglasses, each bigger than the one before and set a little out of line: after every unanswered knock he waits out the next, larger one. After the fourth he will give up.
image.zh: 戴头盔的信使手握秒表，一次次敲一台毫无动静的机柜。他和机柜之间立着四只沙漏，一只比一只大，还摆得有点歪歪扭扭：每敲一次没有回应，他就等完下一只更大的沙漏。等完第四只，他就放弃。

means.en: a timeout on every call
means.zh: 每次调用都有超时

means.en: exponential backoff between attempts
means.zh: 两次尝试之间指数退避

means.en: jitter: a random spread so clients don't retry together
means.zh: 抖动：随机错开，免得客户端一起重试

means.en: a cap on attempts, then give up
means.zh: 尝试次数有上限，然后放弃

means.en: a failing dependency
means.zh: 出故障的依赖

summary.en: Cap how many requests each client may make per unit of time, and answer the excess with 429 Too Many Requests.
summary.zh: 限制每个客户端单位时间内的请求数，超出部分返回 429 Too Many Requests。

explain.en: Rate limiting protects a service from overload and abuse and shares capacity fairly between clients. A token bucket holds up to b tokens and refills at rate r; each request takes a token or is rejected, so it allows bursts of up to b and an average rate of r. A leaky bucket queues requests and releases them at a fixed rate, smoothing bursts into a steady flow. A fixed window counts requests per clock minute but can let through twice the limit around a window boundary; a sliding window, kept as a log or a weighted counter, largely avoids that. Rejected requests get HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, ideally with a Retry-After header. In a cluster the counters live in a shared store such as Redis, or each node enforces its share of the limit.
explain.zh: 限流保护服务不被过载和滥用，并在客户端之间公平分配容量。令牌桶（token bucket）最多存 b 个令牌，以速率 r 补充；每个请求取走一个令牌，没有令牌就被拒绝，所以允许最多 b 个的突发、平均速率为 r。漏桶（leaky bucket）把请求排进队列，以固定速率放出，把突发抹成匀速流。固定窗口按自然分钟计数，但在窗口交界处可能放过两倍限额的请求；滑动窗口（用日志或加权计数实现）基本可以避免。被拒绝的请求返回 HTTP 429 Too Many Requests，最好附上 Retry-After 头。集群中计数器放在 Redis 等共享存储里，或由每个节点执行限额的一部分。
