example.en: An API allows each key 10 requests per second with bursts of 20: a token bucket with b = 20 and r = 10 per second. A client that has been idle fires 30 requests at once: 20 succeed and 10 get 429 with Retry-After: 1. One second later the bucket holds 10 fresh tokens.
example.zh: 某 API 允许每个密钥每秒 10 次请求、突发 20 次，即令牌桶 b = 20、r = 每秒 10 个。一个空闲许久的客户端一口气发出 30 个请求：20 个成功，10 个收到 429 和 Retry-After: 1。一秒后，桶里又有了 10 个新令牌。

image.en: A queue of rabbits hurries toward a stone gate. The gatekeeper lets a rabbit through only if he can take a gold coin from the big bucket beside him, and new coins drop into the bucket one at a time, at a steady beat. The bucket is empty now, so a red sign reading 429 blocks the gate and the rabbits must wait.
image.zh: 一队兔子匆匆奔向一道石门。守门人每放一只兔子过去，就要从身旁的大桶里取一枚金币；新金币只会按固定节拍一枚一枚落进桶里。现在桶空了，一块写着 429 的红牌子挡住了门口，兔子们只能等着。

means.en: the token bucket; its size b sets the burst
means.zh: 令牌桶：容量 b 决定突发上限

means.en: the refill rate r: the long-run limit
means.zh: 补充速率 r：长期的速率上限

means.en: each request spends one token
means.zh: 每个请求消耗一个令牌

means.en: excess requests are rejected with 429
means.zh: 超出的请求返回 429

summary.en: After repeated failures, stop calling a broken dependency for a while, fail fast with a fallback, and probe before resuming.
summary.zh: 依赖连续出错后暂停调用：快速失败、走降级方案，试探成功再恢复。

explain.en: A circuit breaker wraps calls to one dependency and tracks their outcomes. Closed: calls pass through while the failure rate over a recent window is measured. When it crosses a threshold the breaker opens: calls fail immediately without touching the dependency, which frees threads and gives the dependency room to recover. After a cool-down it turns half-open and lets a few trial calls through; success closes it, failure opens it again. While open, degrade gracefully with a fallback such as cached data, a default value or a simpler feature. Bulkheads add isolation: each dependency gets its own connection or thread pool, so one slow dependency cannot exhaust them all, like the watertight compartments of a ship.
explain.zh: 熔断器（circuit breaker）包住对某个依赖的调用，并统计结果。关闭状态：调用正常通过，同时统计最近一个窗口内的失败率。失败率超过阈值，熔断器就打开：调用立即失败，不再碰那个依赖，既腾出线程，也给依赖留出恢复的空间。冷却一段时间后进入半开状态，放少量试探请求过去：成功就关闭，失败就重新打开。打开期间用降级方案体面地退一步：返回缓存数据、默认值或简化功能。舱壁（bulkhead）进一步隔离：每个依赖用独立的连接池或线程池，一个慢依赖拖不垮全部，就像船上的水密隔舱。

example.en: A product page calls a recommendation service. Of the last 20 calls, 12 failed, above the 50% threshold, so the breaker opens. For the next 30 s the page shows a cached best-seller list instead of waiting on timeouts. Then one trial call succeeds, the breaker closes, and personal recommendations return.
example.zh: 商品页调用推荐服务。最近 20 次调用中 12 次失败，超过 50% 的阈值，熔断器打开。接下来 30 秒，页面直接展示缓存的热销榜，不再傻等超时。之后一次试探调用成功，熔断器关闭，个性化推荐恢复。

image.en: Lightning has struck a server rack, and in front of it a giant traffic light glows red, so no more requests walk into the storm. An operator calmly carries on by candlelight. A low fence keeps the trouble away from the second rack, whose bulb still shines, and an alarm clock ticks toward the moment one test request may try again.
image.zh: 闪电劈中了一台机柜，它前面的巨型红绿灯亮起红灯，再没有请求往暴风雨里走。一名操作员举着蜡烛，从容地继续干活。一道矮栅栏把麻烦挡在另一台机柜之外，那台的灯泡依然亮着；一只闹钟滴答作响，时间一到，就放一个试探请求过去。

means.en: open breaker: calls fail fast
means.zh: 熔断打开：调用快速失败

means.en: the failing dependency
means.zh: 出故障的依赖

means.en: fallback: a degraded but working answer
means.zh: 降级：差一点但能用的结果

means.en: bulkhead: separate resources per dependency
means.zh: 舱壁：每个依赖独立资源

means.en: cool-down, then half-open trial calls
means.zh: 冷却后半开，放试探请求

summary.en: Earning confidence that the system works: many fast tests of small units, fewer tests of real parts together, and tests under heavy load.
summary.zh: 建立对系统的信心：大量快速的小单元测试，较少的真实组件联合测试，以及高负载下的测试。

summary.en: Small, fast, isolated tests that run on every change and point straight at what broke.
summary.zh: 小而快、彼此隔离的测试：每次改动都跑，一失败就指出哪里坏了。

summary.en: Write many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests and only a few end-to-end tests; cost and run time grow toward the top.
summary.zh: 大量快速的单元测试，较少的集成测试，极少的端到端测试：越往上越慢、越贵。

explain.en: The test pyramid, popularised by Mike Cohn, describes a healthy mix of automated tests. At the base are many unit tests: they run in milliseconds, need no setup and name the exact broken function. In the middle are fewer integration tests that exercise real collaborators such as a database or a message broker. At the top are a few end-to-end tests that drive the deployed system like a user; they are the most realistic but slow, costly and often flaky, and a failure rarely shows where the bug is. The anti-pattern is the ice-cream cone: mostly manual and UI tests over few unit tests. Ideal ratios are debated (the 'testing trophy' favours integration tests), but the principle holds: test each behaviour at the lowest level that can catch its bugs.
explain.zh: 测试金字塔（由 Mike Cohn 推广）描述健康的自动化测试组合。底层是大量单元测试：毫秒级运行、无需准备环境，失败时直接指出哪个函数坏了。中层是较少的集成测试，检查与数据库、消息代理等真实组件的协作。顶层是少量端到端（E2E）测试，像用户一样操作已部署的系统：最接近真实，但慢、维护成本高、常常不稳定，失败了也难以定位。反模式是“冰淇淋筒”：大量手工和 UI 测试，单元测试却很少。各层的理想比例有争议（“测试奖杯”更看重集成测试），但原则不变：每种行为都放在能发现其缺陷的最低层级去测。

example.en: A typical backend service: 1,200 unit tests run on every save and finish in 20 seconds; 150 integration tests against a real PostgreSQL take 3 minutes in CI; 15 end-to-end checkout journeys take 12 minutes before each release. When a pricing rule breaks, a unit test names the function within seconds.
example.zh: 一个典型的后端服务：1200 个单元测试每次保存都跑，20 秒跑完；150 个连真实 PostgreSQL 的集成测试在 CI 里跑 3 分钟；15 条端到端下单流程在每次发布前跑 12 分钟。某条计价规则出错时，单元测试几秒内就能指出是哪个函数。

image.en: A lab assistant in a white coat has built a pyramid of giant toy bricks: five green bricks at the base, three blue bricks on top of them, and a single gold bar at the peak. She times the bottom row with her stopwatch, and it is done in a blink. A turtle sits on the gold bar at the top, in no hurry at all.
image.zh: 穿白大褂的实验员用巨型积木搭了一座金字塔：底层五块绿砖，上面三块蓝砖，塔尖是一根金条。她用秒表给底层计时，一眨眼就跑完了。塔尖的金条上趴着一只乌龟，一点也不着急。

thing.en: five green bricks at the base

means.en: many fast, cheap unit tests
means.zh: 大量快速、便宜的单元测试

means.en: fewer integration tests
means.zh: 较少的集成测试

thing.en: the gold bar at the top

means.en: a few costly end-to-end tests
means.zh: 少量昂贵的端到端测试

means.en: end-to-end tests are slow
means.zh: 端到端测试很慢

means.en: fast feedback from the base
means.zh: 底层反馈快

summary.en: Test one small unit in isolation, replacing slow or unpredictable collaborators with stubs, mocks or fakes.
summary.zh: 隔离地测试一个小单元，用桩、mock 或伪实现替换又慢又不可控的协作者。

explain.en: A unit test checks one function or class in isolation and runs in milliseconds. It follows arrange–act–assert: set up inputs and collaborators, call the code once, check the outcome. Collaborators that are slow or nondeterministic, such as databases, clocks or payment gateways, are replaced by test doubles. A stub returns canned answers. A mock is programmed with expected calls and fails the test if the interaction differs. A fake is a light working implementation, such as an in-memory repository. Dependency injection makes the swap easy. The danger is over-mocking: tests that pin every internal call break on each refactor, yet pass while the real integration is broken. Prefer asserting on results and state, and mock only interfaces you own.
explain.zh: 单元测试隔离地检查一个函数或类，毫秒级完成。它遵循“准备—执行—断言”（arrange–act–assert）：准备输入和协作者，调用一次被测代码，检查结果。数据库、时钟、支付网关这类又慢又不确定的协作者，用测试替身（test double）代替：桩（stub）返回预设答案；mock 预设期望的调用，交互不符就让测试失败；伪实现（fake）是能真正工作的轻量实现，比如内存版仓储。依赖注入让替换变得容易。风险是过度 mock：把每个内部调用都钉死的测试，一重构就坏，真实集成坏了却照样通过。应优先断言结果和状态，只 mock 自己拥有的接口。

example.en: Testing applyDiscount(order, clock): arrange a $200 order and a fake clock fixed on Black Friday; act by calling applyDiscount; assert that the 20% discount gives a total of $160. A stub price service returns 200 for every product, and a mock mailer verifies that exactly one 'discount applied' email was requested.
example.zh: 测试 applyDiscount(order, clock)：准备一笔 200 元的订单和一个固定在黑五当天的伪时钟；执行 applyDiscount；断言打 8 折后总价为 160 元。桩价格服务对所有商品都返回 200，mock 邮件发送器验证恰好请求发送了一封“折扣已生效”邮件。

image.en: Under a giant microscope lies a single brass gear, taken out of its machine. Its real neighbours have been swapped for stand-ins: a cardboard cut-out of a filing cabinet that always gives the same answer, and a huge eye on a stand that watches every call the gear makes. Beside the microscope a scientist checks the result with a magnifying glass.
image.zh: 巨大的显微镜下躺着一只黄铜齿轮，它被单独从机器上拆了下来。它真正的邻居都换成了替身：一块印着文件柜的纸板，永远给出同一个答案；一只立在架子上的大眼睛，盯着齿轮发出的每一次调用。显微镜旁，科学家举着放大镜检查结果。

means.en: the unit under test, isolated
means.zh: 被测单元，单独隔离

means.en: a stub: returns canned answers
means.zh: 桩：返回预设答案

means.en: a mock: verifies the calls made
means.zh: mock：验证发生了哪些调用

means.en: assert: check the outcome
means.zh: 断言：检查结果

summary.en: Write a failing test first, make it pass with the simplest code, then refactor, in cycles of a few minutes.
summary.zh: 先写一个失败的测试，用最简单的代码让它通过，再重构；几分钟一个循环。

explain.en: Test-driven development, popularised by Kent Beck, works in short cycles. Red: write a small test for the next bit of behaviour and watch it fail, which shows the test can catch a bug. Green: write the simplest code that passes, however crude. Refactor: clean up names, duplication and structure while every test stays green. Writing the test first means using the API before it exists, which pushes toward small units with explicit inputs and injectable dependencies; code that is hard to test is often a design warning. TDD also leaves a regression suite behind. Its benefits are debated, since studies report mixed results, and many teams use it selectively: more for logic-heavy code, less for UI or exploratory work.
explain.zh: 测试驱动开发（TDD，由 Kent Beck 推广）以很短的循环推进。红：为下一小步行为写一个测试，看着它失败，证明它能抓到缺陷。绿：写最简单的代码让它通过，粗糙也无妨。重构：在所有测试保持通过的前提下整理命名、去除重复、改善结构。先写测试，等于在 API 存在之前就先当它的调用者，这会推动代码拆成输入明确、依赖可注入的小单元；难测的代码往往是设计在报警。TDD 还顺带留下一套回归测试。它的收益有争议，研究结论不一，许多团队选择性使用：多用于逻辑密集的代码，少用于 UI 或探索性工作。

example.en: Red: assert fizzbuzz(3) == 'Fizz' fails because fizzbuzz does not exist yet. Green: def fizzbuzz(n): return 'Fizz' passes. Red again: assert fizzbuzz(5) == 'Buzz' fails, so add a check for n % 5 == 0. Once tests for 3, 5, 15 and 7 all pass, refactor: move the rules into a list of (divisor, word) pairs.
example.zh: 红：assert fizzbuzz(3) == 'Fizz' 失败，因为函数还不存在。绿：def fizzbuzz(n): return 'Fizz'，通过。再红：assert fizzbuzz(5) == 'Buzz' 失败，于是加上 n % 5 == 0 的判断。等 3、5、15、7 的测试全部通过，再重构：把规则提取成（除数，单词）列表。

image.en: Three giant flasks stand on the lab floor, joined by curved arrows that run round and round. On the blackboard by the red flask the scientist has written the test first, and the brew fails it. The green flask bubbles: it passes. Now she stands by the blue flask with a wrench, tidying up the apparatus before the next lap.
image.zh: 实验室地上立着三只巨大的烧瓶，弯弯的箭头把它们连成一圈。红烧瓶旁的黑板上，科学家先写好了测试，药水没通过。绿烧瓶咕嘟冒泡：通过了。此刻她拿着扳手站在蓝烧瓶旁，在下一圈开始前整理仪器。

thing.en: the red flask and the blackboard

means.en: red: write a failing test first
means.zh: 红：先写一个会失败的测试

means.en: green: the simplest code that passes
means.zh: 绿：用最简单的代码通过

thing.en: the blue flask and the wrench

means.en: refactor while all tests stay green
means.zh: 重构：所有测试保持通过

means.en: short cycles, repeated every few minutes
means.zh: 小步循环，几分钟一圈

summary.en: Tests that put real parts together and push the whole system to its limits.
summary.zh: 把真实部件放在一起测试，并把整个系统推到极限。

summary.en: Run your code against real dependencies, such as a database in a container, to catch the bugs that live between components.
summary.zh: 让代码连上真实依赖（如容器里的数据库）运行，抓住藏在组件之间的缺陷。

explain.en: Unit tests replace collaborators with doubles, so they miss wrong SQL, mismatched types, broken migrations and bad configuration. Integration tests run the code against real dependencies. Tools such as Testcontainers start a throwaway PostgreSQL, Redis or Kafka in Docker for the test run, so every developer and CI job uses the same version. Test data needs discipline: each test creates what it needs and leaves no trace, by rolling back its transaction or truncating tables, so no test depends on another's leftovers or on run order. Integration tests are slower and prone to flakiness: shared state, timing and network hiccups make them fail now and then for no code reason. Quarantine and fix flaky tests quickly, or people learn to ignore red builds.
explain.zh: 单元测试用替身代替协作者，因此发现不了 SQL 写错、列类型不匹配、迁移脚本有误、序列化出错或连接配置不对这类问题。集成测试让代码连上真实依赖运行。Testcontainers 等工具在测试时用 Docker 启动一次性的 PostgreSQL、Redis 或 Kafka，每位开发者、每个 CI 任务用的都是同一版本。测试数据要守规矩：每个测试自己准备数据、结束后不留痕迹（如回滚事务或清空表），不依赖别的测试的残留或执行顺序。集成测试更慢，也更容易不稳定（flaky）：共享状态、时序和网络抖动会让它偶尔无故失败。不稳定的测试要尽快隔离并修好，否则大家就会对红色构建视而不见。

example.en: A repository test starts postgres:16 with Testcontainers, applies the Flyway migrations, inserts two users and calls findByEmail('Ann@x.com'). It fails: the real SQL compares emails case-sensitively, while the in-memory fake used in unit tests ignored case and hid the bug. Each test runs inside a transaction that is rolled back afterwards.
example.zh: 仓储测试用 Testcontainers 启动 postgres:16，执行 Flyway 迁移，插入两个用户，再调用 findByEmail('Ann@x.com')。测试失败了：真实 SQL 比较邮箱时区分大小写，而单元测试用的内存伪实现忽略大小写，把缺陷藏了起来。每个测试都在一个事务里运行，结束后回滚。

image.en: In the arena a runner in a red tunic is chained to a real elephant for a three-legged race. No cardboard stand-in this time: when the elephant stumbles, so does he. Behind them stands the blue shipping crate the elephant arrived in, and a giant die lies on the sand to remind everyone that some races are lost by pure chance.
image.zh: 竞技场上，一名穿红衣的跑者和一头真大象拴在一起跑两人三足。这回可不是纸板替身：大象一绊，他也跟着踉跄。他们身后是运来大象的蓝色货箱；沙地上躺着一颗巨大的骰子，提醒大家有些比赛纯属运气不好才输。

thing.en: the runner chained to the elephant
thing.zh: 和大象拴在一起的跑者

means.en: your code running against a real dependency
means.zh: 代码连着真实依赖运行

means.en: the real database (PostgreSQL's mascot)
means.zh: 真实的数据库（PostgreSQL 的吉祥物）

means.en: a throwaway container started for the tests
means.zh: 为测试启动的一次性容器

means.en: flakiness: failures by chance, not by code
means.zh: 不稳定：失败来自偶然，而非代码

summary.en: Each consumer records what it needs from an API, and the provider checks every change against those contracts before it ships.
summary.zh: 消费方记录下自己对 API 的需求，提供方每次改动在发布前都要对照这些契约验证。

explain.en: End-to-end tests that deploy every service are slow and brittle, yet no service may break its callers. In consumer-driven contract testing, for example with Pact, each consumer's tests run against a mock provider and record the requests the consumer sends and the response fields it actually uses. The resulting contract is shared, often through a broker. The provider's build replays every consumer's requests against the real provider and checks the responses. A change that renames or removes a field some consumer uses fails the provider's own pipeline, before deployment. Each side is tested alone, in seconds. Contracts check the shape and meaning of messages, not whole business flows, so they complement integration and end-to-end tests.
explain.zh: 服务之间互相调用时，把所有服务都部署起来跑端到端测试又慢又脆，可哪个服务都不能弄坏它的调用方。在消费者驱动的契约测试（如 Pact）中，消费方的测试对着一个模拟的提供方运行，记录下它发出的请求和它真正用到的响应字段。生成的契约被共享出去，通常放在一个 broker 里。提供方构建时，把每个消费方的请求重放给真实的提供方，并检查响应。如果改动重命名或删除了某个消费方在用的字段，提供方自己的流水线就会失败，根本到不了部署。双方各自独立测试，几秒钟完成，无需共享测试环境。契约只检查消息的结构和含义，不覆盖完整的业务流程，所以它是集成测试和端到端测试的补充。

example.en: The mobile app's contract says GET /users/42 returns 200 with a JSON body containing id (a number) and name (a string). The users team renames name to fullName. Their CI replays the app's contract, the check fails on the missing name field, and the team ships fullName alongside name instead of breaking the app in production.
example.zh: 移动端的契约写明：GET /users/42 返回 200，JSON 中包含 id（数字）和 name（字符串）。用户服务团队把 name 改名为 fullName。他们的 CI 重放移动端的契约，因缺少 name 字段而失败，于是团队改为同时保留 name 和 fullName，而不是在生产环境把 App 弄坏。

image.en: In the arena, a challenger with a pencil has cut a giant blue jigsaw piece, exactly the shape he needs. The robot champion brings its own piece, painted red, but its tab no longer matches. The referee peers over the two pieces with a magnifying glass and stops the match before the first blow.
image.zh: 竞技场上，拿铅笔的挑战者剪出了一块巨大的蓝色拼图，正是他需要的形状。机器人卫冕者带来自己的红色拼图，凸起却已对不上。裁判举着放大镜从两块拼图后面探出头来，在第一招之前就叫停了比赛。

means.en: the consumer's contract: the fields it relies on
means.zh: 消费方契约：它依赖的字段

means.en: the provider's changed API
means.zh: 提供方改动后的 API

thing.en: the tab that no longer fits

means.en: a breaking change, such as a renamed field
means.zh: 破坏性改动，比如字段改名

means.en: the provider's build fails before deployment
means.zh: 提供方构建失败，到不了部署

relation.zh: 在提供方 CI 中跑

summary.en: Raise traffic step by step while watching latency percentiles, to find the system's capacity and the bottleneck that limits it.
summary.zh: 逐级加大流量、盯住延迟百分位，找出系统容量和限制容量的瓶颈。

explain.en: A load test drives realistic traffic at the expected level and checks the targets, for example p99 latency under 300 ms at 2,000 requests per second. A stress test keeps raising the load past that until something breaks, to find the capacity limit and see how the system fails and recovers; a soak test holds a steady load for hours to expose leaks. Ramp up in steps and watch percentiles rather than averages: as utilisation nears 100%, queues build up and tail latency shoots up. At the knee of the curve, use metrics and profiling to find the bottleneck, the first resource to saturate, such as CPU, a connection pool, a lock or a downstream service. Fix it and the next bottleneck appears. Common tools are k6, Gatling, JMeter and Locust.
explain.zh: 负载测试（load test）按预期水平施加贴近真实的流量，检查指标是否达标，例如每秒 2000 个请求时 p99 延迟低于 300 ms。压力测试（stress test）继续加压，直到系统出问题，以找出容量上限，并观察它如何失败、如何恢复；浸泡测试（soak test）长时间保持稳定负载，暴露泄漏等问题。要逐级加压，看百分位而不是平均值：利用率接近 100% 时，队列堆积，尾延迟急剧上升。在曲线的拐点处，借助指标和性能剖析找到瓶颈，也就是第一个饱和的资源：CPU、连接池、锁或下游服务。修好它，下一个瓶颈又会出现。常用工具有 k6、Gatling、JMeter、Locust。

example.en: Ramping from 500 to 3,000 requests per second in steps of 500: p99 latency stays near 120 ms up to 2,000 rps, reaches 400 ms at 2,500 and passes 2 s at 3,000, while the median is still 60 ms. CPU sits at 40%, but all 50 database connections are busy: the connection pool is the bottleneck.
example.zh: 从每秒 500 个请求逐级加到 3000，每级加 500：p99 延迟在 2000 rps 以内都在 120 ms 左右，2500 时升到 400 ms，3000 时超过 2 秒，而中位数仍只有 60 ms。CPU 只用了 40%，但 50 个数据库连接全部占满：连接池才是瓶颈。

image.en: In the arena, an engineer in a hard hat keeps sending cars onto an arched bridge, more every minute, and times each crossing with her stopwatch. The chart beside the bridge shoots up. The bridge itself holds; the cars stand nose to tail at the narrow stone gate at the far end, the real bottleneck.
image.zh: 竞技场上，戴安全帽的工程师不断把汽车放上拱桥，每分钟都比上一分钟多，并用秒表给每次过桥计时。桥边的图表一路飙升。桥本身撑得住；车辆却在桥尽头那道窄窄的石门前首尾相接地堵着，那才是真正的瓶颈。

means.en: ramping the load step by step
means.zh: 逐级加压

means.en: latency measured per request
means.zh: 逐个请求测量延迟

means.en: tail latency explodes near capacity: the knee
means.zh: 接近容量时尾延迟激增：拐点

thing.en: cars jammed at the narrow gate

means.en: the bottleneck, often not where you expect
means.zh: 瓶颈，往往不在你以为的地方

summary.en: Knowing who is asking, deciding what they may do, and keeping attackers out of code, secrets and data.
summary.zh: 弄清是谁在请求、决定他能做什么，并把攻击者挡在代码、密钥和数据之外。

summary.en: Who may enter the palace and what each guest may touch: authentication, authorization, sessions and delegated access.
summary.zh: 谁能进宫、每位来客能碰什么：认证、授权、会话与委托授权。

summary.en: Authentication proves who is asking; authorization decides what that identity may do. Check both on every request.
summary.zh: 认证确认“你是谁”，授权决定“你能做什么”，每个请求都要检查。

explain.en: Authentication (authn) verifies an identity: a password, a passkey, a signed token or a client certificate. Authorization (authz) takes that verified identity and decides whether this action on this resource is allowed. They fail differently: 401 Unauthorized really means "we don't know who you are", 403 Forbidden means "we know, and the answer is no". Role-based access control (RBAC) gives users roles and roles permissions, so policy changes in one place. Enforce authorization on the server for every request and every object, not just by hiding buttons in the UI: missing per-object checks (IDOR) are among the most common API flaws.
explain.zh: 认证（authentication）核实身份：口令、通行密钥、签名令牌或客户端证书。授权（authorization）拿着已核实的身份，判断这个操作能否作用于这个资源。两者失败的含义不同：401 Unauthorized 其实是“不知道你是谁”，403 Forbidden 是“知道你是谁，但不行”。基于角色的访问控制（RBAC）给用户分配角色、给角色分配权限，改策略只改一处。授权必须在服务端对每个请求、每个对象都检查，而不是只在界面上把按钮藏起来：缺少逐对象检查（IDOR）是最常见的 API 漏洞之一。

example.en: GET /invoices/1042 arrives with a valid token for alice, so she is authenticated. The server loads invoice 1042, sees owner = bob and alice's role = customer, and returns 403 (or 404, to hide that it exists). Without that ownership check alice could step through 1043, 1044, … and read everyone's invoices. A user with the admin role and the permission invoices:read:any would pass.
example.zh: GET /invoices/1042 带着 alice 的有效令牌到达，认证通过。服务端读出 1042 号发票，发现属主是 bob，而 alice 的角色是 customer，于是返回 403（或返回 404，连它存在都不透露）。少了这道属主检查，alice 把编号改成 1043、1044……就能读遍所有人的发票。拥有 admin 角色和 invoices:read:any 权限的用户才能放行。

image.en: At the palace gate a helmeted guard peers through a huge magnifying glass at a visitor: who are you? The visitor in a blue cap is let through and strides towards the golden throne, but a second guard plants his shield across the path. Everyone knows who he is now; his plaque just says "guest", and guests do not sit on the throne.
image.zh: 宫门口，戴头盔的卫兵举着巨大的放大镜端详来客：你是谁？戴蓝帽的来客被放了进去，大步走向金色王座，第二名卫兵却用盾牌拦在路上。大家都知道他是谁了，可他的牌子上写着“访客”，访客不能坐王座。

thing.en: guard with the magnifier at the gate

means.en: authentication: verify who is asking
means.zh: 认证：核实请求者身份

thing.en: guard with the shield before the throne

means.en: authorization: decide per action and resource
means.zh: 授权：按操作和资源逐一裁决

means.en: a role in RBAC that grants permissions
means.zh: RBAC 里的角色，决定权限

means.en: the protected resource
means.zh: 受保护的资源

summary.en: Store only a slow, salted hash of each password, so a stolen database does not hand over the passwords.
summary.zh: 只存加盐的慢哈希，数据库被盗也拿不到明文密码。

explain.en: Never store passwords in plaintext or with reversible encryption. Store the output of a password-hashing function: a unique random salt per user plus a deliberately slow, tunable algorithm such as bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2id (PBKDF2 where compliance requires it). The salt defeats precomputed rainbow tables and makes identical passwords hash differently; the cost factor makes every guess expensive. Fast hashes like SHA-256 are the wrong tool precisely because a GPU computes billions per second. To log in, recompute the hash with the stored salt and compare in constant time. Rate-limit login attempts against online guessing, and rehash with a higher cost when a user next logs in.
explain.zh: 绝不能存明文密码，也不要用可逆加密。应当存密码哈希函数的输出：每个用户一个随机盐（salt），再配上刻意放慢、代价可调的算法，如 bcrypt、scrypt、Argon2id（合规要求时用 PBKDF2）。盐让预先算好的彩虹表失效，也让相同密码的哈希各不相同；代价因子让每一次猜测都很贵。SHA-256 这类快速哈希恰恰不合适，因为 GPU 每秒能算几十亿次。登录时用存下的盐重新计算并做常数时间比较。登录接口要限流，防止在线猜测；用户下次登录时可用更高代价重新哈希。

example.en: bcrypt with cost 12 stores one 60-character string: "$2b$12$", then a 22-character salt and a 31-character hash. Each +1 in cost doubles the work, since bcrypt runs 2^cost rounds of its expensive key setup; cost 12 takes roughly a quarter of a second on a typical server core. A user pays that once per login, while an attacker pays it for every single guess.
example.zh: 代价为 12 的 bcrypt 存一个 60 字符的串：“$2b$12$”，接着是 22 字符的盐和 31 字符的哈希。代价每加 1，工作量翻倍，因为 bcrypt 要执行 2^cost 轮昂贵的密钥设置；代价 12 在普通服务器单核上约需四分之一秒。用户每次登录只付一次，攻击者每猜一次都要付一次。

image.en: A courtier feeds a scroll with a password into a creaking windmill, and a pinch from the big jar of white salt goes in with every scroll. Out the other side comes only grey powder in a bucket. A hooded thief has stolen the bucket and sits glaring at his stopwatch, because each guess he tries must crawl through the same slow mill.
image.zh: 一位侍从把写着密码的卷轴塞进吱呀作响的风车磨坊，每塞一卷，都从白盐大罐里撒进一撮盐。另一头只出来一桶灰色粉末。戴兜帽的小偷偷走了这桶粉末，却只能盯着秒表发愁：他每猜一次，都得让风车慢慢磨一遍。

means.en: a slow, one-way hash function (bcrypt, Argon2)
means.zh: 单向、刻意放慢的哈希（bcrypt、Argon2）

means.en: a random per-user salt that defeats rainbow tables
means.zh: 每个用户的随机盐，让彩虹表失效

means.en: the stored hash: useless to read back
means.zh: 存下的哈希，无法还原

means.en: the cost factor that makes each guess slow
means.zh: 代价因子让每次猜测都慢

summary.en: A session id points to state kept on the server; a signed token like a JWT carries its claims itself and is hard to revoke before it expires.
summary.zh: 会话 id 指向服务端存的状态；JWT 这类签名令牌自带声明，过期前很难撤销。

explain.en: After login the server must recognise later requests. With a server-side session it keeps the user's state in a session store and gives the client only a random, unguessable session id, usually in a cookie; logout simply deletes the record. A self-contained token such as a JWT carries the claims (user id, roles, expiry) and a signature (HMAC, RSA or ECDSA), so any service with the key can verify it without a lookup. The signature stops tampering but hides nothing: a JWT is encoded, not encrypted. Since nothing is looked up, a stolen JWT stays valid until exp, so keep access tokens short-lived and pair them with revocable refresh tokens. In browsers keep credentials in httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies, out of reach of page scripts.
explain.zh: 登录之后，服务端得认出后续请求。服务端会话把用户状态存在会话存储里，只给客户端一个随机、猜不到的会话 id，通常放在 Cookie 里；登出就是删掉那条记录。JWT 这类自包含令牌自带声明（用户 id、角色、过期时间）和签名（HMAC、RSA 或 ECDSA），任何持有密钥的服务都能直接验证，无需查库。签名防篡改，却不保密：JWT 只是编码，不是加密。正因为不查库，被盗的 JWT 在 exp 之前一直有效，所以访问令牌要短命，再配上可撤销的刷新令牌。浏览器里把凭证放进 httpOnly、Secure、SameSite 的 Cookie，页面脚本读不到。

example.en: A JWT is header.payload.signature, each part base64url. The payload {"sub":"42","role":"user","exp":1767225600} decodes in any browser, so never put secrets in it. Change "user" to "admin" and the HMAC-SHA256 signature no longer matches, so the server rejects the token. A 15-minute access token plus a 30-day refresh token in an httpOnly cookie limits what a thief can do.
example.zh: JWT 由 header.payload.signature 三段 base64url 组成。载荷 {"sub":"42","role":"user","exp":1767225600} 在任何浏览器里都能解码，别放秘密。把 "user" 改成 "admin"，HMAC-SHA256 签名就对不上，服务端拒收。15 分钟的访问令牌加放在 httpOnly Cookie 里的 30 天刷新令牌，能限制令牌被盗后的损失。

image.en: Two ways to remember a guest. On the left a clerk keeps a thick ledger and hands the visitor nothing but a ticket with the number 7; to forget him she simply tears out his page. On the right the king slams a giant red seal onto a scroll and a messenger races off with it: anyone can read it, nobody can forge it, and the king cannot call it back until it expires.
image.zh: 记住来客有两种办法。左边，书记员守着一本厚账簿，只递给来客一张写着 7 的小票；想忘掉他，撕掉那一页就行。右边，国王把巨大的红印章重重盖在卷轴上，信使抓起就跑：谁都能读，谁都伪造不了，可在过期之前，国王也追不回来。

means.en: server-side session: state on the server, only an id on the client
means.zh: 服务端会话：状态在服务端，客户端只拿 id

means.en: easy revocation: delete the session record
means.zh: 撤销容易：删掉会话记录

means.en: the signature that makes a JWT tamper-proof
means.zh: 签名让 JWT 无法篡改

thing.en: the messenger who cannot be recalled

means.en: a JWT stays valid until exp; keep it short-lived
means.zh: JWT 在过期前一直有效，要短命

summary.en: OAuth 2.0 lets a user grant an app limited access to an API without sharing a password; OpenID Connect adds an ID token saying who logged in.
summary.zh: OAuth 2.0 让用户不交出密码就授予应用有限权限；OIDC 再加一张说明“谁登录了”的 ID 令牌。

explain.en: In OAuth 2.0 the resource owner (the user) approves, at an authorization server, a client app's request for specific scopes; the client then gets an access token that the resource server (the API) accepts. The password never reaches the client. Web and mobile apps should use the authorization-code flow: the browser comes back with a short-lived one-time code, which the client exchanges for tokens over a back channel. PKCE guards that exchange: the client first sends a hash of a random code_verifier and must show the verifier to redeem the code, so an intercepted code is useless. OAuth alone is delegated authorization, not login. OpenID Connect adds an ID token, a signed JWT naming the user (sub, iss, aud), which the client checks to log the user in.
explain.zh: 在 OAuth 2.0 中，资源所有者（用户）在授权服务器上批准客户端应用申请的若干权限范围（scope），客户端随后拿到访问令牌，资源服务器（API）凭它放行。用户密码始终不经过客户端。网页和移动应用应使用授权码流程：浏览器带着一次性、短时效的授权码跳回，客户端再通过后端通道用它换取令牌。PKCE 保护这次兑换：客户端先发出随机 code_verifier 的哈希，兑换时必须出示原值，截获的授权码因此毫无用处。OAuth 本身是委托授权，不是登录。OpenID Connect 在其上增加 ID 令牌，一个写明用户身份（sub、iss、aud）的签名 JWT，客户端验证后据此登录。

example.en: A photo-printing site offers "Sign in with" a large provider. It redirects there with response_type=code, scope=openid plus a read-only photos scope, and code_challenge = BASE64URL(SHA-256(code_verifier)). After the user consents, the browser returns with ?code=…; the site posts the code and the code_verifier to the token endpoint and receives an ID token (who the user is) and an access token that can read photos but not delete them.
example.zh: 照片冲印网站提供“用某大平台登录”。它把用户重定向过去，带上 response_type=code、scope=openid 和一个只读照片权限，以及 code_challenge = BASE64URL(SHA-256(code_verifier))。用户同意后浏览器带着 ?code=… 回来；网站把授权码和 code_verifier 提交给令牌端点，拿到 ID 令牌（用户是谁）和只能读、不能删照片的访问令牌。

image.en: A traveller wants a valet to fetch her car, but she will not hand over her silver master key. At the royal key desk a key-master in a wizard's hat checks with her, then gives the valet a single giant gold key that only starts the car, plus a medal engraved with her name. The valet heads for the car; her master key never leaves her hand.
image.zh: 女旅客想让代客泊车的人去取车，但不肯交出自己的银色总钥匙。王室钥匙台前，戴巫师帽的掌钥官先向她确认，再交给泊车员一把巨大的金钥匙，只能发动这辆车，外加一枚刻着她名字的奖章。泊车员走向汽车，她的总钥匙始终握在手里。

means.en: the authorization server that asks the user for consent
means.zh: 授权服务器，征得用户同意

means.en: the access token, limited by scope
means.zh: 访问令牌，受 scope 限制

means.en: the OIDC ID token: who logged in
means.zh: OIDC 的 ID 令牌：谁登录了

means.en: the password never reaches the client app
means.zh: 密码从不交给客户端

means.en: the resource server and the user's data
means.zh: 资源服务器和用户数据

summary.en: The common attacks and the basic hygiene that blocks them: injection, privileges and secrets, encryption.
summary.zh: 常见攻击和挡住它们的基本功：注入、权限与密钥、加密。

title.zh: 注入攻击：SQL 注入与 XSS

summary.en: Injection happens when untrusted input is spliced into code; keep data apart from code with parameterised queries and output encoding.
summary.zh: 把不可信输入拼进代码就会被注入；用参数化查询和输出编码把数据和代码分开。

explain.en: Built by string concatenation, a command no longer shows where your code ends and the user's data begins. In SQL injection, input like ' OR '1'='1 rewrites the WHERE clause. The fix is parameterised queries (prepared statements): the query structure is sent first and values are bound separately, so they are never parsed as SQL. ORMs do this unless you use raw strings. In cross-site scripting (XSS), input like a <script> tag lands in a page and runs in other users' browsers with their session. The fix is context-aware output encoding (HTML, attribute, JavaScript, URL), which template engines apply by default. A Content Security Policy adds defence in depth by telling the browser which scripts may run. Input validation helps but replaces neither fix.
explain.zh: 用字符串拼接构造命令时，解释器分不清你的代码在哪里结束、用户的数据从哪里开始。SQL 注入里，' OR '1'='1 这样的输入会改写 WHERE 子句。解法是参数化查询（预编译语句）：先发送查询结构，值单独绑定，永远不会被当成 SQL 解析。ORM 默认就这样做，除非你退回去拼原始字符串。跨站脚本（XSS）里，<script> 之类的输入落进页面，在其他用户的浏览器里带着他们的会话运行。解法是按上下文做输出编码（HTML、属性、JavaScript、URL），现代模板引擎默认会做。内容安全策略（CSP）是纵深防御，告诉浏览器哪些脚本可以运行。输入校验有帮助，但替代不了这两项。

example.en: "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'" with name = x' OR '1'='1 becomes WHERE name = 'x' OR '1'='1', which matches every row. The safe form is cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s", (name,)): the database receives the value as data. For XSS, a comment <script>steal()</script> rendered as <script>steal()</script> is harmless text, and a CSP of script-src 'self' blocks inline scripts as well.
example.zh: 拼接时输入 x' OR '1'='1，条件就变成 name = 'x' OR '1'='1'，匹配所有行。安全写法是 execute("… WHERE name = %s", (name,))，值只当数据。XSS 方面，评论里的 <script> 被编码成 <script> 就只是文字；CSP 设为 script-src 'self' 还能拦住内联脚本。

image.en: In the forge a robot smithing arm obeys whatever is chalked on the order board. A hooded prankster has tacked ' OR '1'='1 onto a customer's name, and the arm dutifully smashes open the treasure chest, spilling every gold coin. In front sits a sealed green jar: a customer's words handed over this way can only be weighed, never read as an order.
image.zh: 锻造坊里，机械臂照着订单黑板上写的字干活。戴兜帽的捣蛋鬼在顾客名字后面添了 ' OR '1'='1，机械臂便老老实实砸开宝箱，金币撒了一地。前面摆着一只封好的绿色玻璃罐：顾客的话装进罐子交过去，只能被称重，永远不会被当成命令。

thing.en: the robot arm obeying the board

means.en: an interpreter: SQL engine or browser
means.zh: 解释器：SQL 引擎或浏览器

means.en: untrusted input spliced into code
means.zh: 被拼进代码的不可信输入

thing.en: the smashed chest and spilled gold

means.en: every row leaked
means.zh: 整张表的数据泄露

means.en: a bound parameter: data never parsed as code
means.zh: 绑定参数：数据不会被当代码解析

summary.en: Give every person and service only the permissions it needs, and keep secrets in a secret manager, never in code.
summary.zh: 每个人、每个服务只拿必需的权限；密钥放进密钥管理服务，绝不写进代码。

explain.en: Least privilege limits the blast radius of a bug or a breach: a service that may only read one bucket cannot drop the database, however badly it is compromised. Apply it to people, services and CI jobs alike: narrow roles, separate accounts per environment, short-lived credentials instead of permanent keys, and access that expires. Secrets such as database passwords, API keys and signing keys belong in a secret manager (for example HashiCorp Vault or a cloud secrets service), injected at runtime and audited, not in source code, images or logs. Rotate them regularly and at once after a leak. Never commit a key: git history keeps it, and bots scan public repositories for credentials within minutes. The only real fix for a leaked key is to revoke it.
explain.zh: 最小权限原则限制了漏洞或入侵的“爆炸半径”：只能读一个存储桶的服务，哪怕被彻底攻破也删不了数据库。它同样适用于人、服务和 CI 任务：角色要窄，每个环境分开账号，用短期凭证代替永久密钥，权限到期自动收回。数据库密码、API 密钥、签名密钥等机密应放在密钥管理服务里（如 HashiCorp Vault 或云厂商的密钥服务），运行时注入并留审计记录，不能出现在源码、镜像或日志里。定期轮换，泄露后立即轮换。绝不提交密钥：git 历史会一直留着它，机器人几分钟内就会扫描公开仓库里的凭证。密钥泄露后唯一可靠的补救是吊销它。

example.en: A thumbnail service reads images from one bucket and writes thumbnails to another. Its role allows s3:GetObject on uploads/* and s3:PutObject on thumbs/*, nothing more. It fetches its database password from the secret manager at start-up, and the password rotates every 30 days. When a scanner flags a commit containing an access key starting AKIA…, the team revokes the key first and cleans the history afterwards.
example.zh: 缩略图服务从一个桶读图片，往另一个桶写缩略图。它的角色只允许对 uploads/* 执行 s3:GetObject、对 thumbs/* 执行 s3:PutObject，别无其他。数据库密码在启动时从密钥管理服务取得，每 30 天轮换一次。扫描器发现某次提交里有以 AKIA… 开头的访问密钥时，团队先吊销密钥，再清理历史。

image.en: The forge master opens a steel safe full of keys and gives his apprentice exactly one small key, for the one door he must open today. At the anvil a smith hammers an old key into a new shape. On a public notice post someone has pinned a key for all to see, and a black crow is already flapping off with it.
image.zh: 锻造坊主人打开装满钥匙的钢制保险箱，只给学徒一把小钥匙，刚好开今天要开的那扇门。铁砧旁，铁匠把一把旧钥匙锤成新的形状。公告柱上有人把钥匙钉出来给大家看，一只黑乌鸦已经叼着它扑棱棱飞走了。

means.en: a secret manager: secrets stored, injected, audited
means.zh: 密钥管理服务：集中存放、注入、审计

means.en: least privilege: only what this job needs
means.zh: 最小权限：只给这份工作所需

thing.en: re-forging a key on the anvil

means.en: rotation of secrets
means.zh: 密钥轮换

thing.en: the crow stealing the posted key

means.en: a committed key is found and abused fast
means.zh: 提交到仓库的密钥很快被盗用

title.en: Encryption in Transit and at Rest

summary.en: TLS protects data moving across networks, disk and database encryption protect stored data, and both depend on managing keys well.
summary.zh: TLS 保护网络上传输的数据，磁盘和数据库加密保护存储的数据，两者都离不开密钥管理。

explain.en: Encryption in transit means TLS on every connection, including internal service-to-service traffic; mutual TLS also authenticates the client. TLS provides confidentiality, integrity and, through certificates, server authentication. Encryption at rest protects disks, backups and snapshots if the media is stolen. It does not stop an attacker who queries through the running application, which decrypts transparently. Either way the real secret is the key: keep it in a key management service or HSM, apart from the data, use envelope encryption (data keys encrypted by a master key) and rotate keys. Hashing is not encryption: encryption is reversible with the key, hashing is one-way, so passwords are hashed while data you must read back is encrypted.
explain.zh: 传输加密就是每条连接都用 TLS，包括内部服务之间的流量；双向 TLS（mTLS）还能认证客户端。TLS 提供机密性、完整性，并借助证书认证服务器。静态加密在磁盘、备份或快照被盗时保护数据，但挡不住通过正在运行的应用来查询的攻击者，因为应用会透明地解密。无论哪种，真正的秘密都是密钥：放在密钥管理服务（KMS）或硬件安全模块里，与数据分开；用信封加密（数据密钥由主密钥加密）并定期轮换。哈希不是加密：加密凭密钥可逆，哈希单向，所以密码要哈希，需要读回的数据才加密。

example.en: With envelope encryption, a file is encrypted with a fresh 256-bit AES data key; that data key is encrypted by a master key held in KMS and stored next to the file. Reading the file means asking KMS to decrypt the small data key, a call that is logged and can be denied. Meanwhile curl -v https://api.example.com shows the TLS 1.3 handshake and the certificate chain before a single HTTP byte is sent.
example.zh: 信封加密时，文件用一把新生成的 256 位 AES 数据密钥加密；这把数据密钥再由 KMS 中的主密钥加密，和文件存在一起。读文件就得请 KMS 解密那把小小的数据密钥，这次调用会被记录，也可以被拒绝。另外，curl -v https://api.example.com 会在发送任何 HTTP 字节之前显示 TLS 1.3 握手和证书链。

image.en: A porter hurries over an arched bridge with a chest, a giant padlock clamped on it. A huge eyeball on the bank stares at the passing cargo but sees only iron. On the far side another chest sits padlocked in storage, and a watchdog guards the one gold key, kept well apart from every chest.
image.zh: 搬运工扛着箱子匆匆走过拱桥，箱子上扣着一把巨大的挂锁。岸边一只巨大的眼球盯着过往的货物，却只看得见铁锁。对岸另一只箱子锁着存放，一条看门狗守着唯一的金钥匙，钥匙离所有箱子都远远的。

thing.en: the padlocked chest on the bridge

means.en: encryption in transit: TLS
means.zh: 传输加密：TLS

thing.en: the eyeball that sees only iron

means.en: an eavesdropper on the network
means.zh: 网络上的窃听者

means.en: encryption at rest: disks, backups
means.zh: 静态加密：磁盘、备份

thing.en: the dog guarding the far-off key

means.en: key management: keys kept apart from data
means.zh: 密钥管理：密钥与数据分开

summary.en: Shipping changes to production safely and often, then seeing how the running system behaves and recovering when it fails.
summary.zh: 安全、频繁地把变更送上生产，看清运行中的系统，出故障时迅速恢复。

summary.en: An assembly line from commit to production: integrate, package, release and run.
summary.zh: 从提交到生产的装配线：集成、打包、发布、运行。

summary.en: Everyone merges small changes into main often, and every push is built and tested automatically, so main stays green.
summary.zh: 人人频繁把小改动合进主干，每次推送都自动构建和测试，让主干保持绿色。

explain.en: Continuous integration means developers merge their work into a shared main branch at least daily, in small batches, instead of letting long-lived branches drift apart. Every push triggers an automated pipeline that compiles, runs unit and integration tests, lints and scans dependencies, and reports within minutes. A broken main is the team's top priority: fix it or revert it, because a red main blocks everyone and hides new failures. Small, frequent merges keep conflicts small and make it obvious which change broke what. Speed matters: if the pipeline takes an hour, people batch their changes and the benefit fades. CI is a practice, not a server: running a CI tool on branches merged once a month is not continuous integration.
explain.zh: 持续集成指开发者至少每天一次、小批量地把工作合进共享主干，而不是让长期分支越走越远。每次推送都会触发自动流水线：编译、跑单元测试和集成测试、代码检查、依赖扫描，几分钟内给出结果。主干一旦变红就是全队头等大事：要么修好，要么回滚，因为红色主干会挡住所有人，还会掩盖新的失败。小而频繁的合并让冲突小，也让“谁弄坏了什么”一目了然。速度很关键：流水线要跑一小时，大家就会攒着改动一起提，好处随之消失。CI 是一种做法，不是一台服务器：一个月才合并一次的分支，跑再多 CI 工具也不算持续集成。

example.en: A workflow runs on every pull request and every push to main: checkout, install dependencies, ruff, then pytest against a PostgreSQL service container, in about six minutes. Branch protection requires the check to pass before merging. When a merge turns main red at 14:05, its author reverts it at 14:12 and fixes it on a branch, so nobody else stays blocked.
example.zh: 工作流在每个拉取请求和每次推送到 main 时运行：检出代码、安装依赖、跑 ruff，再连着一个 PostgreSQL 服务容器跑 pytest，大约六分钟。分支保护要求检查通过才能合并。14:05 有次合并让主干变红，作者 14:12 就把它回滚，再到分支上修复，别人不必干等。

image.en: Workers drop small crates onto a long conveyor belt one after another, never one giant crate. The belt carries each crate past a robot arm that rattles and inspects it, and a red crate that failed is flung off the line onto the floor. At the end of the belt a traffic light glows green, and the whole factory works to keep it that way.
image.zh: 工人们一个接一个地把小木箱放上长长的传送带，从不放一个巨型箱子。传送带载着每只箱子经过机械臂，机械臂摇一摇、查一查，没通过的红箱子被甩下生产线，掉在地上。传送带尽头的红绿灯亮着绿灯，整座工厂都在努力让它一直绿着。

means.en: small commits merged often
means.zh: 小而频繁的提交

means.en: the automated build and tests on every push
means.zh: 每次推送都自动构建与测试

means.en: a failing change: fix or revert it at once
means.zh: 失败的改动，立刻修或回滚

means.en: main is always green
means.zh: 主干始终是绿色

summary.en: Continuous delivery keeps every green build releasable at the press of a button; continuous deployment removes the button.
summary.zh: 持续交付让每个绿色构建都能一键发布；持续部署连这一键也省了。

explain.en: Continuous delivery extends CI: every change that passes produces a versioned artifact that goes through further stages (staging, acceptance and security tests) and can reach production at any time through an automated, repeatable process. Whether to release is a business decision, often a button. Continuous deployment goes one step further: every change that passes all stages goes to production with no human approval. Both rely on building once and promoting the same artifact through every environment, keeping configuration outside the artifact, automated rollback, and small batches that make each release low-risk. Releasing often makes releases boring; releasing rarely makes them dangerous.
explain.zh: 持续交付是 CI 的延伸：每个通过检查的改动都产出一个带版本号的制品，再经过预发环境、验收测试、安全检查等阶段，随时可以通过自动化、可重复的流程上线。发不发布由业务决定，往往就是按一个按钮。持续部署再进一步：通过全部阶段的改动无须人工批准，直接上生产。两者都依赖“一次构建，多处部署”，即同一个制品经过每个环境；配置与制品分离；自动回滚；以及让每次发布都低风险的小批量。发布得勤，发布就变得平淡；发布得少，发布就变得危险。

example.en: A commit at 10:00 builds image api:4f2c1e9, passes the tests, deploys to staging and passes smoke tests by 10:25. Under continuous delivery it waits on the release dashboard until the product owner presses Deploy at 15:00. Under continuous deployment it reaches production at 10:30 without anyone touching it. Either way, production runs exactly the image that was tested.
example.zh: 10:00 的一次提交构建出镜像 api:4f2c1e9，通过测试，部署到预发环境，10:25 冒烟测试通过。持续交付下，它在发布面板上等着，直到产品负责人 15:00 按下“部署”；持续部署下，10:30 它就自动到了生产环境，没人碰过。无论哪种，生产上跑的都正是测试过的那个镜像。

image.en: Three identical rockets stand fuelled on the launch pad, one for each green build, every one ready to fly. A giant hand hovers over them, choosing the moment to press go: that is delivery. At the right a robot has stopped waiting for anyone, and its rocket lifts off on a tongue of flame the moment it passes inspection: that is deployment.
image.zh: 三枚一模一样的火箭加满燃料立在发射台上，每个绿色构建一枚，随时可以起飞。一只巨手悬在上方，挑选按下发射键的时机：这是持续交付。右边的机器人不再等任何人，火箭一通过检查就喷着火焰升空：这是持续部署。

means.en: every green build is a release candidate
means.zh: 每个绿色构建都是候选发布

means.en: continuous delivery: a human decides when
means.zh: 持续交付：由人决定何时发布

thing.zh: 机器人那枚升空的火箭

means.en: continuous deployment: no human gate
means.zh: 持续部署：没有人工关卡

summary.en: An image packages a process with everything it needs in read-only layers; a container is that image running in isolation on a shared kernel.
summary.zh: 镜像把进程和它所需的一切装进只读分层；容器是镜像在共享内核上隔离运行的实例。

explain.en: A container image bundles an application with its runtime, libraries and files, so it runs the same on a laptop, in CI and in production. Images are stacks of read-only layers, roughly one per build step; layers are content-addressed and cached, so after a code change the base and dependency layers are reused, and images share them on disk. A container is a running instance: an ordinary process given its own view of the system by Linux namespaces, limited by cgroups, with a thin writable layer, lost when it is removed. A virtual machine boots its own guest kernel on a hypervisor; containers share the host kernel, so they start in about a second and cost megabytes, but isolate less strongly. Keep images small and never bake secrets into a layer.
explain.zh: 容器镜像把应用和它的运行时、库、文件打包在一起，在笔记本、CI 和生产上运行得一模一样。镜像由一层层只读分层叠成，大致每个构建步骤一层；分层按内容寻址并缓存，改了代码后基础层和依赖层可以复用，不同镜像也能在磁盘上共享它们。容器是镜像的运行实例：一个普通进程，靠 Linux 命名空间（namespace）获得独立视图，由 cgroups 限制资源，顶上有一层薄薄的可写层，容器删除时随之丢弃。虚拟机在虚拟化层上启动自己的客户机内核；容器共享宿主机内核，所以一秒左右甚至更快就能启动，只占几兆内存，但隔离较弱。镜像要小、版本要钉死，绝不能把密钥打进某一层。

example.en: A Dockerfile: FROM python:3.12-slim; COPY requirements.txt .; RUN pip install -r requirements.txt; COPY . .; CMD ["gunicorn", "app:app"]. Because COPY . . comes last, a code change rebuilds only the final layer and the dependency layer comes from cache. docker run -p 8000:8000 app starts in about a second, and three containers from the same image share every read-only layer.
example.zh: Dockerfile 写 FROM python:3.12-slim；COPY requirements.txt .；RUN pip install -r requirements.txt；COPY . .；CMD ["gunicorn", "app:app"]。COPY . . 在最后，改代码只重建最后一层，依赖层走缓存。docker run app 约一秒启动，同镜像的三个容器共享所有只读层。

image.en: On the factory floor stands a giant stack of slabs, the image: base system at the bottom, libraries in the middle, the app on top. A worker carries copies to one long table, where three glass jars of water stand side by side, a goldfish bobbing at the brim of each: separate jars, same table. Beside them squats a whole little house with its own roof, the heavyweight virtual machine.
image.zh: 工厂地上立着一摞巨大的厚板，那就是镜像：底层是基础系统，中间是库，最上面是应用。工人把复制品搬到一张长桌上，桌上并排放着三个盛水的玻璃罐，每个罐口都有一条金鱼在晃：罐子各自独立，桌子却是同一张。旁边蹲着一整栋带屋顶的小房子，那是笨重的虚拟机。

means.en: the image: read-only layers, base to app
means.zh: 镜像：从基础到应用的只读分层

thing.en: three jars, each with a goldfish
thing.zh: 三个罐子，各有一条金鱼

means.en: containers: isolated processes from one image
means.zh: 容器：同一镜像跑出的隔离进程

means.en: the host kernel all containers share
means.zh: 所有容器共享的宿主机内核

thing.en: the little house with its own roof

means.en: a VM: a whole guest OS and kernel
means.zh: 虚拟机：一整套客户机系统和内核

summary.en: You declare the desired state, such as three replicas of an image, and Kubernetes controllers keep working until the cluster matches it.
summary.zh: 你声明期望状态（比如某镜像跑三个副本），Kubernetes 的控制器就不停调整，直到集群与之相符。

explain.en: Kubernetes runs containers across a cluster of machines. Its smallest unit is the pod: one or more containers that share a network address and volumes and are scheduled together onto a node. You rarely create pods by hand. A Deployment declares the desired state, say three replicas of image api:1.4, and controllers keep reconciling: if a pod or a whole node dies, a replacement pod is scheduled; change the image and pods are replaced in a rolling update. Pods come and go with new IP addresses, so a Service gives a stable name and virtual IP that load-balances across the pods whose labels match. A HorizontalPodAutoscaler adjusts the replica count from metrics such as CPU. The whole system is a set of control loops comparing desired with actual state.
explain.zh: Kubernetes 在一组机器组成的集群上运行容器。最小单位是 Pod：一个或几个共享网络地址和存储卷、被一起调度到某个节点上的容器。很少直接手建 Pod。Deployment 声明期望状态，比如镜像 api:1.4 跑三个副本，控制器便持续调和（reconcile）：Pod 或整个节点挂了，就调度新的 Pod；换了镜像，就滚动更新逐个替换。Pod 来来去去、IP 会变，所以用 Service 提供稳定的名字和虚拟 IP，在标签匹配的 Pod 之间做负载均衡。HorizontalPodAutoscaler 按 CPU 等指标调整副本数。整个系统就是一组不断比较“期望”与“实际”的控制循环。

example.en: kubectl apply -f deploy.yaml with replicas: 3 and image: api:1.4 creates three pods. kubectl delete pod api-7d9c-x2k4 leaves two, and within seconds the ReplicaSet starts a third. A Service named api selects the label app=api, so other pods call http://api no matter which pods currently exist. Under heavy load an autoscaler with a 70% CPU target grows the Deployment from 3 to 6 replicas.
example.zh: kubectl apply -f deploy.yaml（3 个副本，镜像 api:1.4）创建三个 Pod。kubectl delete pod api-7d9c-x2k4 删掉一个，几秒内 ReplicaSet 就补上第三个。Service api 选中标签 app=api，别的 Pod 访问 http://api 即可，不管此刻是哪些 Pod。高负载下，CPU 目标 70% 的自动扩缩容把副本从 3 扩到 6。

image.en: A blackboard by the pen reads "want: 3", but only two sheep stand inside. Nobody gives an order: the sheepdog simply notices the gap and herds a fresh sheep in through the opening. A signpost marked "svc" points visitors to the pen, whichever sheep happen to be inside today.
image.zh: 羊圈旁的黑板上写着“want: 3”，圈里却只有两只羊。没人下命令，牧羊犬自己发现少了一只，把一只新羊赶进圈口。一块写着“svc”的路牌把来客引向羊圈，不管今天圈里是哪几只羊。

means.en: the desired state in a Deployment
means.zh: Deployment 里的期望状态

means.en: pods: replaceable replicas
means.zh: Pod：可替换的副本

thing.en: the sheepdog herding a new sheep

means.en: a controller reconciling actual to desired
means.zh: 控制器让实际趋向期望

means.en: a Service: a stable name in front of changing pods
means.zh: Service：变动 Pod 前的稳定入口

summary.en: Instruments for looking inside a running system: logs, metrics, traces and the targets they serve.
summary.zh: 观察运行中系统的仪器：日志、指标、追踪，以及它们服务的目标。

summary.en: Log events as machine-readable key-value records, such as JSON with a request id, so they can be searched, filtered and joined.
summary.zh: 把事件记成机器可读的键值记录（如带请求 id 的 JSON），方便搜索、过滤和关联。

explain.en: A structured log line is a record, not a sentence: a timestamp, a level, a message and named fields such as request_id, user_id, route and duration_ms, usually one JSON object per line. A log platform (OpenSearch, Loki or a cloud log service) can then filter level=error AND route=/checkout, count by any field, or pull every line of one request by its request id, which each service copies from the incoming request into every log call. Levels separate signal from noise: DEBUG off in production, INFO for business events, WARN for degraded behaviour, ERROR for failures that need attention. Never log secrets or sensitive personal data such as passwords, tokens or full card numbers: logs are copied widely and kept long, so redact at the source.
explain.zh: 结构化日志是一条记录，不是一句话：时间戳、级别、消息，再加 request_id、user_id、route、duration_ms 等具名字段，通常每行一个 JSON 对象。日志平台（OpenSearch、Loki 或云日志服务）于是能筛出 level=error 且 route=/checkout 的行，按任意字段计数，或凭请求 id 拉出同一请求的全部日志；每个服务都把收到的请求 id 带进自己的每一次打日志。级别用来区分信号与噪声：生产环境关掉 DEBUG，INFO 记业务事件，WARN 记降级行为，ERROR 记需要处理的失败。绝不记录密码、令牌、完整卡号等机密或敏感个人数据：日志会被到处复制、长期保存，要在源头脱敏。

example.en: Instead of "User 42 failed to pay 19.99", emit {"ts":"2026-10-23T14:05:12Z","level":"error","msg":"payment failed","request_id":"7f3a9c","user_id":42,"amount":19.99,"reason":"card_declined"}. A search for request_id=7f3a9c then shows the gateway, order and payment lines of that one request in order. The card number never appears; at most its last four digits.
example.zh: 别写“User 42 failed to pay 19.99”，而是输出 {"level":"error","msg":"payment failed","request_id":"7f3a9c","user_id":42,"reason":"card_declined"}，外加时间戳。搜索 request_id=7f3a9c，就能按顺序看到这个请求在网关、订单、支付里的日志。卡号从不出现，最多记末四位。

image.en: Under the dome an owl scribe fills a giant ledger, but every entry is a tidy form with labelled boxes, not a scrawl. Before it stand rows of envelopes, and an astronomer with a magnifying glass pulls out the three red ones at once: they all carry the same request number, so one request's whole story falls into his hands.
image.zh: 穹顶下，一只猫头鹰书记员在巨大的账簿上记录，每一条都是填好格子的整齐表单，而不是潦草的句子。账簿前排着一列列信封，拿放大镜的天文学家一下就抽出三封红信封：它们写着同一个请求号，一个请求的来龙去脉便全在他手里。

means.en: structured records: named fields, one JSON per line
means.zh: 结构化记录：具名字段，每行一个 JSON

means.en: the logger, writing levels and context
means.zh: 日志器，记下级别和上下文

means.en: lines sharing one request id
means.zh: 共享同一请求 id 的日志

means.en: search and filter by field
means.zh: 按字段搜索和过滤

summary.en: Metrics are cheap numeric time series (counters, gauges, histograms); alert on symptoms users feel, using percentiles rather than averages.
summary.zh: 指标是廉价的数值时间序列（计数器、仪表、直方图）；按用户能感到的症状告警，看百分位而非平均值。

explain.en: A metric is a number sampled over time, with a few labels. A counter only goes up (requests served, errors) and you graph its rate; a gauge goes up and down (queue length, memory in use); a histogram counts observations in buckets (request latency) so you can estimate percentiles such as p50, p95 and p99. Averages hide the tail: the mean can look healthy while one user in fifty waits seconds. Two checklists help: RED for services (Rate, Errors, Duration) and USE for resources (Utilization, Saturation, Errors). Alert on symptoms users feel, such as error rate or p99 latency above target for several minutes, rather than on every possible cause like high CPU. Every page should be urgent and actionable, or people learn to ignore pages.
explain.zh: 指标是随时间采样的数值，带少量标签。计数器（counter）只增不减（请求数、错误数），画图时看它的速率；仪表（gauge）可升可降（队列长度、内存占用）；直方图（histogram）把观测值计入桶中（如请求延迟），从而估算 p50、p95、p99 等百分位。平均值会掩盖长尾：均值看着健康，每五十个用户里却可能有一个要等好几秒。两份清单可用：服务看 RED（速率、错误、耗时），资源看 USE（利用率、饱和度、错误）。按用户能感到的症状告警，比如错误率或 p99 延迟持续几分钟超标，而不是对高 CPU 之类的每个可能原因都告警。每一次呼叫都应紧急且可处理，否则大家会学会无视告警。

example.en: http_requests_total{route="/checkout",status="500"} is a counter; its rate over 5 minutes gives errors per second. Latency goes into a histogram with buckets at 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5 and 5 s. If 980 of 1,000 requests take 100 ms and 20 take 3 s, the mean is 158 ms and looks fine, but p99 is 3 s. A rule "p99 > 1 s for 10 minutes" pages the on-call engineer.
example.zh: http_requests_total{route="/checkout",status="500"} 是计数器，取 5 分钟速率就是每秒错误数。延迟放进桶边界为 0.1、0.25、0.5、1、2.5、5 秒的直方图。1000 个请求里 980 个 100 毫秒、20 个 3 秒，均值 158 毫秒，看着没事，p99 却是 3 秒。规则“p99 > 1 秒持续 10 分钟”会呼叫值班工程师。

image.en: Three instruments stand under the dome: a stack of gold coins that only ever grows, a thermometer whose red line rises and falls, and a framed bar chart of latency buckets. The on-call engineer sleeps on a bench, until the big bell above the chart starts swinging: users are waiting too long, so this is worth waking up for.
image.zh: 穹顶下立着三件仪器：一摞只会越堆越高的金币，一支红线忽高忽低的温度计，还有一幅画着延迟分桶的柱状图。值班工程师躺在长椅上睡觉，直到柱状图上方的大钟摇响：用户等得太久了，这才值得把人叫醒。

means.en: a counter: only goes up, graph its rate
means.zh: 计数器：只增不减，看速率

means.en: a gauge: a value that rises and falls
means.zh: 仪表：可升可降的当前值

means.en: a histogram, the source of p99
means.zh: 直方图，算 p99 的来源

means.en: an alert on a user-facing symptom
means.zh: 针对用户可感症状的告警

summary.en: A trace follows one request across services as a tree of timed spans, linked by ids passed along with every call, so the slow hop stands out.
summary.zh: 追踪用随调用传递的 id 把一个请求在各服务里的计时跨度连成树，慢的那一跳一眼可见。

explain.en: One request may fan out into dozens of calls across services, and no single service's logs show where the time went. Tracing gives the request a trace id at the edge and records a span for each unit of work: service, operation, start, duration, status and the id of its parent span. The ids travel with every outgoing call, typically in the W3C traceparent header or in message metadata, and a tracing library such as OpenTelemetry creates child spans and exports them. A backend such as Jaeger or Tempo assembles the spans into a waterfall: the root span covers the whole request, children show what ran in sequence or in parallel, and the longest bar is the bottleneck. Sampling keeps the cost down; logs carrying the trace id link straight to it.
explain.zh: 一个用户请求可能扇出成跨服务的几十次调用，单看各服务自己的日志，看不出时间花在了哪里。追踪在入口给请求分配 trace id，并为每段工作记录一个跨度（span）：服务、操作、开始时间、耗时、状态，以及父跨度的 id。这些 id 随每次外发调用传下去，通常放在 W3C traceparent 请求头或消息元数据里，由 OpenTelemetry 之类的库创建子跨度并上报。Jaeger、Tempo 等后端把跨度拼成瀑布图：根跨度覆盖整个请求，子跨度显示哪些调用串行、哪些并行，最长的那条就是瓶颈。采样能控制成本；日志里带上 trace id，就能一键跳到对应的追踪。

example.en: A checkout takes 1,200 ms. Its trace: gateway 1,200 ms → order-service 1,150 ms, which calls inventory (80 ms) and then pricing (950 ms); inside pricing one SQL query on a missing index takes 900 ms. Dashboards only said "checkout is slow"; the waterfall names the culprit. The ids crossed each hop in a header like traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01.
example.zh: 一次结账耗时 1200 毫秒。追踪显示：网关 1200 毫秒 → 订单服务 1150 毫秒，它先调库存（80 毫秒），再调定价（950 毫秒）；定价里一条缺索引的 SQL 就花了 900 毫秒。仪表盘只能说“结账慢”，瀑布图却直接点出元凶。这些 id 靠 traceparent 请求头逐跳传递。

image.en: Toy bricks hang in mid-air in a staircase waterfall: a long row of blue bricks for the whole request, a short teal row beneath it for a quick call, and a long red row lower still. On the red row a turtle crawls along at its own pace. An astronomer swings his brass telescope away from the stars and onto the turtle: there is the slow hop.
image.zh: 玩具积木悬在半空，排成阶梯状的瀑布：最上面一长排蓝积木是整个请求，下面一小排青色积木是一次很快的调用，再往下是一长排红积木。红积木上，一只乌龟慢吞吞地爬着。天文学家把黄铜望远镜从星空转向乌龟：慢的那一跳就在这儿。

thing.en: the long blue row on top

means.en: the root span: the whole request
means.zh: 根跨度：整个请求

means.en: child spans for downstream calls
means.zh: 下游调用的子跨度

thing.en: the turtle on the red row

means.en: the slow hop that dominates latency
means.zh: 主导延迟的慢调用

means.en: the trace viewer's waterfall
means.zh: 追踪界面的瀑布图

summary.en: An SLI measures what users feel, an SLO sets its target, and the error budget is the unreliability you may spend before slowing down.
summary.zh: SLI 度量用户的感受，SLO 设定目标，错误预算是放慢脚步之前可以花掉的不可靠度。

explain.en: A service level indicator (SLI) is a measured ratio of good events, such as the share of requests served successfully in under 300 ms. A service level objective (SLO) is the target for that SLI over a window, such as 99.9% over 30 days. An SLA is a contract with penalties, usually looser than the SLO. The error budget is what the SLO leaves over: 0.1% of 30 days is 43.2 minutes of total outage. While budget remains, the team ships features and takes risks; once it is spent, an agreed policy shifts effort to reliability, such as freezing risky launches. The budget turns the speed-versus-stability argument into arithmetic. 100% is the wrong target: users cannot tell 99.999% from 100% through their own networks, and each extra nine costs far more.
explain.zh: 服务水平指标（SLI）是“好事件”的实测比例，比如 300 毫秒内成功返回的请求占比。服务水平目标（SLO）是该 SLI 在一个时间窗口内的目标，比如 30 天 99.9%。SLA 是带赔偿条款的合同，通常比内部 SLO 宽松。错误预算就是 SLO 留下的余量：30 天的 0.1% 是 43.2 分钟的完全宕机。预算还有，团队就放心发功能、承担风险；预算花光，就按事先约定把精力转向可靠性，比如冻结高风险发布。预算把“求快还是求稳”的争论变成了算术。100% 是错误的目标：用户隔着自己的网络分不出 99.999% 和 100%，而每多一个 9 代价都要高得多。

example.en: An API serves 10 million requests a month under a 99.9% success SLO, so its budget is 10,000 failed requests. A bad deploy fails 2% of traffic for 3 hours: about 13,900 requests an hour, so roughly 830 failures, or 8% of the month's budget. In time terms, three nines allow 43 minutes of downtime per 30 days; four nines allow only 4.3 minutes.
example.zh: 某 API 每月处理 1000 万个请求，SLO 为 99.9% 成功，预算就是 1 万个失败请求。一次糟糕的部署让 2% 的流量失败了 3 小时：每小时约 13900 个请求，共约 830 次失败，花掉当月预算的 8% 左右。换成时间：三个 9 每 30 天允许宕机 43 分钟，四个 9 只允许 4.3 分钟。

image.en: A giant hourglass holds the month's error budget: 43 minutes of red sand, and every outage spills a little more through. A developer in a cap hurries up with a parcel to ship, glances at the glass and sees sand left, so the release door stands open for him. A heavy chain lies ready at the threshold, to bar the door the moment the sand runs out.
image.zh: 巨大的沙漏装着这个月的错误预算：43 分钟的红沙，每出一次故障就漏下一些。戴帽子的开发者抱着要发货的包裹匆匆赶来，瞥一眼沙漏，沙子还有，发布之门便为他敞开。门槛边放着一条沉重的铁链，沙子一漏完就把门锁上。

thing.en: the giant hourglass of red sand

means.en: the error budget: 43 min per 30 days at 99.9%
means.zh: 错误预算：99.9% 时每 30 天 43 分钟

means.en: failures spend the budget
means.zh: 故障消耗预算

means.en: budget left: keep shipping
means.zh: 预算尚存，继续发布

means.en: budget gone: freeze risky releases
means.zh: 预算耗尽，冻结高风险发布

means.en: the SLO target for the SLI
means.zh: SLI 的 SLO 目标

summary.en: Opening night every day: releasing in small steps, undoing quickly and learning from failures.
summary.zh: 天天都是首演：小步发布、快速回退、从事故中学习。

title.zh: 蓝绿发布与金丝雀发布

summary.en: Blue-green switches all traffic between two identical environments; a canary sends a small share to the new version first and watches its metrics.
summary.zh: 蓝绿发布在两套相同环境间整体切换流量；金丝雀发布先放一小部分流量给新版本，盯着指标看。

explain.en: In a blue-green deployment two production environments stand side by side. Blue serves users while green gets the new version and is checked in place; then the router flips all traffic to green. Rollback is flipping back, as long as blue stays up and both versions work with the same database. The price is double capacity during the switch. A canary release sends a small slice of real traffic, say 1% or 5%, to the new version, compares its error rate and latency with the old one, and widens the slice step by step only while the metrics stay healthy, aborting automatically if they degrade. A rolling update, the Kubernetes default, replaces instances a few at a time and is a cheaper middle ground. All three limit the blast radius of a bad release.
explain.zh: 蓝绿部署让两套生产环境并排而立：蓝色服务用户，绿色装上新版本并就地验证，然后路由器把全部流量切到绿色。回滚就是再切回去，前提是蓝色还在运行，且两个版本都能用同一个数据库。代价是切换期间要双倍容量。金丝雀发布把一小部分真实流量（比如 1% 或 5%）交给新版本，与旧版本比较错误率和延迟，只有指标健康才逐步放大比例，一旦变差就自动中止。滚动更新是 Kubernetes 的默认方式，每次替换几个实例，是更省资源的折中。三者都在缩小坏版本的影响范围。

example.en: Version 2.4 goes to a 5% canary. After 15 minutes its 5xx rate is 0.08% against 0.07% for 2.3, and p99 is 210 ms against 205 ms, so the rollout continues to 25%, 50% and 100%. Version 2.5 shows 2.1% errors at 5%, and the rollout tool rolls it back automatically: only one user in twenty was exposed, for a few minutes, instead of everyone.
example.zh: 2.4 版先以 5% 流量做金丝雀。15 分钟后它的 5xx 率是 0.08%，2.3 版是 0.07%；p99 为 210 毫秒对 205 毫秒，于是继续放量到 25%、50%、100%。2.5 版在 5% 时错误率达 2.1%，发布工具自动回滚：只有二十分之一的用户受影响几分钟，而不是所有人。

Before the waiting crowd follows, a small yellow canary hops onto the green stage alone, and everyone watches to see whether it keeps singing.

summary.en: A feature flag lets code reach production switched off and be turned on later, for some users or all, without a new deploy.
summary.zh: 功能开关让代码关着上线，之后再对部分或全部用户打开，无须重新部署。

explain.en: A feature flag is a runtime condition around new code: if flags.enabled("new_checkout", user) … else …. Deployed code can stay dark until the team releases it, so deploying and releasing become separate decisions, and unfinished work can merge into main behind a flag, supporting trunk-based development. Flags can target staff first, then 10% of users, then everyone; they power A/B tests; and a kill switch turns a misbehaving feature off in seconds. The cost is complexity: each flag doubles the paths through its code, so test both sides, give every release flag an owner and an expiry date, and delete it once the feature is fully on. Stale flags are technical debt; reusing an old flag contributed to Knight Capital's loss of about $440 million in 2012.
explain.zh: 功能开关（feature flag）是包在新代码外面的运行时条件：if flags.enabled("new_checkout", user) … else …。代码部署后可以先“暗着”，等团队决定再发布，于是部署和发布变成两件事；没写完的功能也能藏在开关后合进主干，支撑主干开发。开关可以先对员工开、再对 10% 用户开、最后全开；可以做 A/B 实验；“熔断开关”能在几秒内关掉出问题的功能。代价是复杂度：每个开关都让代码路径翻倍，所以两边都要测，每个发布开关要有负责人和到期日，功能全量后就删掉。陈旧开关就是技术债；2012 年 Knight Capital 约 4.4 亿美元的损失，就与复用旧开关有关。

example.en: The new checkout merges on Monday behind new_checkout = off. On Tuesday it is turned on for employees, on Wednesday for 10% of users chosen by a hash of the user id, so each user keeps a stable experience. Thursday's error spike ends ten seconds after someone flips the flag off, with no redeploy. Two weeks after reaching 100%, the flag and the old code path are deleted.
example.zh: 新结账流程周一合进主干，开关 new_checkout 为关。周二对员工打开，周三按用户 id 的哈希选出 10% 用户打开，每个用户的体验保持稳定。周四出现错误激增，有人把开关一关，十秒后就平息了，无须重新部署。全量两周后，开关和旧代码路径一起删掉。

summary.en: Make every release quick to undo, and change database schemas in expand-contract steps so old and new code both keep working.
summary.zh: 让每次发布都能快速撤回；数据库结构按“扩展—收缩”分步改，新旧代码都能运行。

explain.en: The fastest fix for a bad release is usually to roll back to the previous artifact rather than debug in production, so keep the last version ready and practise rolling back. Databases make this hard: if a deploy drops or renames a column, the old code can no longer run, and during any rolling deploy old and new versions run at the same time anyway. The expand-contract (parallel change) pattern avoids this. Expand: add the new column or table without removing anything. Migrate: deploy code that writes both, backfill old rows in batches, then switch reads to the new column. Contract: once no running code uses the old column, drop it in a later release. Every step is backward-compatible, so each deploy can be rolled back on its own.
explain.zh: 坏版本最快的解法通常是回滚到上一个制品，而不是在生产上调试，所以要让上个版本随时可用，并演练回滚。数据库让这件事变难：如果一次部署删除或重命名了某列，旧代码就跑不起来了；何况滚动部署期间新旧版本本来就同时在跑。“扩展—收缩”（expand-contract，又称并行变更）模式解决这个问题。扩展：新增列或表，什么都不删。迁移：部署同时写两处的代码，分批回填旧数据，再把读切到新列。收缩：确认没有运行中的代码再用旧列，在之后的版本里删掉它。每一步都向后兼容，每次部署都能单独回滚。

example.en: Renaming users.name to full_name: release 1 adds a nullable full_name; release 2 writes both columns while a job backfills 20 million rows in batches of 10,000; release 3 reads full_name; release 4, a week later, drops name. A plain ALTER TABLE … RENAME COLUMN would break every old instance still running during the rollout. In PostgreSQL, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY builds an index without blocking writes.
example.zh: 把 users.name 改名为 full_name：版本 1 新增可为空的 full_name；版本 2 同时写两列，后台任务以每批 1 万行回填 2000 万行；版本 3 改读 full_name；一周后版本 4 删除 name。直接 RENAME COLUMN 会让发布中仍在运行的旧实例全部出错。PostgreSQL 里 CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY 建索引不阻塞写入。

summary.en: In an incident one commander coordinates, the team mitigates first and diagnoses later, and a blameless postmortem turns the failure into fixes.
summary.zh: 事故中由一位指挥统筹，先止血、后查因；不追责的复盘把故障变成改进。

explain.en: When production breaks, declare an incident early and assign roles: an incident commander who coordinates and decides but does not debug, responders who work the problem, and a communications lead who updates stakeholders and the status page on a fixed rhythm. The first goal is to stop the user impact: roll back, flip a kill switch, fail over or shed load, even before the root cause is known; diagnosis can wait until users are safe. Keep a timeline in the incident channel. Afterwards write a blameless postmortem: impact, timeline, contributing causes and concrete action items with owners and dates. Blameless means asking how the system allowed the error, not who made it, because people who fear blame hide information and the same failure comes back.
explain.zh: 生产出故障时，要尽早宣布事故并分配角色：事故指挥（incident commander）负责协调和决策，但不亲自排查；处理人员解决问题；沟通负责人按固定节奏向相关方和状态页通报。第一目标是止住对用户的影响：回滚、关掉熔断开关、故障切换或削减负载，哪怕根因还不清楚；诊断可以等用户安全之后再做。在事故频道里记下时间线。事后写不追责的复盘（blameless postmortem）：影响、时间线、促成因素，以及有负责人和期限的具体改进项。不追责是指追问“系统为什么允许这个错误发生”，而不是“谁犯了错”，因为怕被追责的人会隐瞒信息，同样的故障还会再来。

example.en: 13:56 a config deploy goes out. 14:02 an error-rate alert pages the on-call engineer; 14:05 she declares a SEV-2 and takes the commander role; 14:09 the 13:56 deploy is identified as the likely trigger and rolled back; 14:14 errors are back to normal after about 18 minutes of impact. The postmortem finds that config changes skipped canary analysis and lists three action items, such as "enforce canaries for config deploys: platform team, by 30 Nov".
example.zh: 13:56 一次配置变更上线。14:02 错误率告警呼叫值班工程师；14:05 她宣布 SEV-2 事故并担任指挥；14:09 判定 13:56 的变更是可能诱因并回滚；14:14 错误率恢复正常，影响约 18 分钟。复盘发现配置变更绕过了金丝雀分析，列出三项改进，例如“配置变更强制走金丝雀：平台组，11 月 30 日前”。

image.en: Flames leap up from three spots on the stage. A commander in a red helmet directs everything through a megaphone and never touches the fire herself. A responder flings water from a bucket at the biggest blaze right now, without stopping to ask how it started. Downstage a round table with an open book already waits for the calm, blameless review afterwards, and there is no gavel in sight.
image.zh: 舞台上三处火苗窜起。戴红头盔的指挥举着扩音器调度一切，自己从不碰火。一名队员拎起水桶就往最大的火上泼，顾不上问火是怎么起的。台前一张圆桌上已经摊开一本书，等着事后平心静气、不追责的复盘，桌上没有法槌。
